3. 
Literal Interpretation of FORWARDuluth, Plan 2045 (Comprehensive Plan) 
 
The subject property is located in the River Green Employment District. 
FORWARDuluth envisions this Character Area to serve as the economic engine for the 
city, serving as a major regional distribution and office hub. The Future Land Use Map 
(FLUM) envisions the uses to be commercial/retail/office. 
 
IV. 
PLANNING STAFF REVIEW/FINDING OF FACTS 
 
As was stated in the Existing Conditions of the staff report, River Green Business Park, though 
zoned M-1 (Light Industrial District), has continued to evolve through the Special Use 
process. In 2023, Mayor and Council approved the elementary school portion of YHale (a 
private elementary charter school, grades kindergarten – fifth grade), New Life (Gwinnett 
County Charter School) and an Event Facility. In January of 2025 Mayor and Council approved 
a youth behavioral center for preschool aged kids living with Autism. And, in September of 
2025 Mayor and Council approved a preschool/daycare. In total, there are currently 10 (ten)

907.06. Street Lights 
Street lights shall be provided by the developer in new subdivisions which propose the construction of a new 
street to be dedicated to the City or which propose lot access to existing City streets. All fees, materials, 
labor, poles, fixtures and any other associated items shall be furnished, paid for and installed by the 
developer. Street lighting shall be installed and operating prior to approval of the final plat. 
1. This Section shall apply for all developments or phases of development which have not received a 
development permit as of the date of adoption of this ordinance. 
2. In all cases, guidelines related to materials, distances between poles, height, and any other relevant 
specifications shall be adhered to as set forth in ANSI/IES RP-8-22: Design of Roadway Facility 
Lighting. The American National Standard Practice for Roadway Lighting and the power provider for 
the project. 
3. A street lighting plan, including a photometric plan, is required and shall accompany the preliminary 
plat and shall be reviewed and approved by the City for compliance with the requirements of the 
national standard. Prior to approval of the Final Plat, all fees associated with materials, labor, and 
installation shall be paid to the appropriate power provider for the project and proof of payment shall 
be provided to the City. 
4. Street lights shall be provided by the owner/developer in any new development where the streets are 
proposed to be dedicated to the City or which propose lot access to existing City streets. 
a. Location and spacing shall be coordinated with the electric company with jurisdiction over 
the property and shall be installed at the time the streets are constructed. 
b. The City shall take over payment of the monthly energy charges from the owner/developer 
once the residential development is 95% complete based on issued Certificates of 
Occupancy and after a written request is received from the developer/builder to take over 
monthly costs. This applies to lighting within public right-of-way. 
c. In a residential development, street lights shall be installed prior to approval of the Final 
Plat. Electrification of the lights shall occur once the development or phase has achieved 
50% completion via issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy (C.O.) 
d. In a non-residential development, street lights are to be installed prior to issuance of a C.O. 
for the building(s). 
5. All fixtures and poles shall meet the requirements of the City. Fixtures that overhang the roadway 
must provide a minimum clearance of 16’ above the roadway Fixtures shall be mounted a minimum 
of 16 feet above the ground and each fixture shall have appropriate arm length to illuminate the 
street. Post top fixtures must be a minimum of 12 feet above finished grade. The City, in addition to 
other requirements, may require a light to be located at street intersections within the development. 
6. All lighting installed by a private developer within the Downtown Overlay District must coordinate 
with Georgia Power and use the standard Georgia Power fixture approved and required by the City of 
Duluth.

203.05. Accessory Buildings and Structures. 
a. Accessory uses or structures shall be permitted only in rear yards with the exception of detached 
garages in a residentially zoned area (R-100, R-75, RA-200, or any residential portion of a PUD), 
provided they are no closer to any street than the principal structure, except as otherwise provided in 
this Code. 
b. No accessory building shall be erected on a lot prior to the time of construction of the principal 
building to which it is accessory. 
c. Accessory structure requirements apply only to residential zoning districts. In a residentially zoned 
area, there shall be a minimum setback requirement from side and rear property line of 5 feet and a 
minimum separation requirement between accessory structures of 20 feet. Multiple accessory 
structures are permitted on a single platted lot, provided the combined square footage of the 
accessory structures complies with the size limitations set forth in Section 344 Detached Structures. 
d. Prohibited accessory buildings or structures. Manufactured homes, mobile homes, freight trailers, 
boxcars, trailers, shipping containers, temporary storage buildings or any other structure or former 
vehicle not originally fabricated for use as an accessory building shall be prohibited as an accessory 
building. 
e. Any structure built on commercial or industrial zoned property shall be considered a principal use. 
f. 
The setback requirements of this Code shall not prohibit the placement of any necessary retaining 
wall nor prohibit any wall or fence except that in a residential district. See also Section 304.02 
Fences and Freestanding Walls. 
 
 
Section 1403. Glossary of Definitions 
 
Boxcar. A completely enclosed, roofed railway freight car with sliding side doors, commonly used 
to transport various goods. 
Shipping container (s). A large, standardized steel box designed to store and transport goods 
across ships, trains and trucks. 
Trailer, freight. Non-motorized vehicle designed to be towed by a truck or tractor for transporting 
goods and cargo overland. 
Trailer. An unpowered wheeled vehicle towed by a motorized vehicle.

stalling pavement to pro-

SGC report reveal

1/2 to 2-1/2.

Woods Way. Brookton

ple times over

phalt thicknesses of 3-3/4

lish crown in center of

posed pavement

mix

binder

face Course Pavement

phalt prior to
variable milling and
repaving as described in
paragraph above. Ap-
proximate deep patch
milled area is marked by

isting asphalt appears

variable depth milling to

1/2 of Type 2 - 'F' mix

PROVIDE ONE( 1) PAGE SUMMARY IDENTIFYING HOW CONTRACTOR AND SUB-CONTRACTORS WILL COORDINATE
ROOFING ACTIVITIES WHILE ALLOWING FOR USE OF THE BUILDING DURING THE PROJECT.
We strive to minimize the disruption of the everyday use ofthe building by effectively communicating and coordinating roofing activities
with the Owner and Architect. Delivery dates, material lay down sites, dumpster and portable toilet location, work schedules and
activities are discussed in detail at the Pre- Construction meeting to assure potential issues have been addressed and everyone is in
agreement with the planned construction.
From the delivery of equipment and materials to the actual work on-site, Dusty Greer Roofing, Inc. works closely with those involved to
assure everyone's safety. This is of paramount importance. Ladders are removed at the end of each workday, and the site is cleared
of any debris that could cause a hazard to staff and visitors. Work areas are clearly defined, and if necessary, an employee is
assigned to remain on the ground to ensure access to the work area is denied.
Due to the number ofyears we have served government agencies across the state of Georgia, ouremployees are aware of the special
circumstances surrounding these projects and are highly trained to avoid interactions of any kind with children and adults on site.
The success of our company, the quality of our work, and smooth roofing process is due to our well-trained, experienced employees.
The longevity of our employees enables them to work together as an efficient team. Each person has a specific role and
responsibilities so the project runs smoothy.The team assembled forthis project has worked togetherto successfully complete
over 60 government facilities at or below the contracted amount.( Contracts ranged between$ 300,000.00 to over
3,300, 000. 00.) If awarded this project, our project management team will consist ofthe following professionals:
PROJECT MANAGER
100% DEDICATION TO THIS PROJECT
Geremy Markham will be the Executive Supervisorforthis project. Geremy has 15+ years ofexperience in the roofing industry, all
while being employed by Dusty Greer Roofing, Inc. His previous employment consisted of 5 years of Construction Project
Management for AT&T, overseeing their wireless construction projects in the state of Georgia.
SUPERINTENDENT/ SITE FOREMAN
100% DEDICATION TO THIS PROJECT
Ronnie Daniels will be the Superintendent/ Site Foreman for this project. Dusty has over 22 years of experience in the roofing
industry, all while being employed by Dusty Greer Roofing, Inc. His previous employment consisted of 16 years of experience as Vice
President of Daniels Construction Company( metal building/ steel erection).
SAFETY COORDINATOR
100% DEDICATION TO THIS PROJECT

1. ORDINANCE OF REZONING – CASE Z2026-004 – 3276 DELMA CT 
 
{C} 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider a rezoning request Oladeji to allow 
for the addition of a second duplex on a portion for 3276 Delma Court (Parcel ID R7264 
170) from R-75 (single family residential district) to RM (residential multifamily district) for 
the property that does not yet contain a structure, and make the existing duplex legal and 
conforming. 
 
Deputy Director of Planning and Engineering Aron Hall came forward to present. He 
outlined the surrounding property uses and existing conditions. 
 
The subject property is in the Established Neighborhood District. FORWARDuluth 
envisions this Character Area to continue to be the backbone of Duluth’s residential 
community. The Future Land Use Map (FLUM) envisions the uses to be low density 
residential (1-6 units an acre). 
 
The current property was platted in 1979, and the plat contemplated two duplexes when 
it was recorded. The current duplex was built in 1980; however, staff cannot locate when 
the duplex was rezoned to R-75 (Single-Family Residential District) from RM (Residential 
Multi-family). The property only became legal non-conforming in June of 2024 when 
duplexes were disallowed in RA-200, R-100 and R-75. 
 
The current owner purchased the property in August of 2015. There have been two code 
cases opened and subsequently closed on the property since the purchase: 
1. parking violation/outdoor storage and sanitary conditions (opened January 3, 2022, 
and closed January 22, 2022) 
2. Ground cover, outdoor storage, protective treatment, roof and drainage, unsafe 
structures and equipment, and vegetation (opened March 11, 2026, and closed April 
14, 2026). 
 
The Comprehensive Plan envisions low density residential (1-6 units an acre). Adding a 
duplex to this property would yield 10 units an acre, which is not in line with the 
Comprehensive Plan. It does, however, make the current duplex legal and conforming.

July 13, 2026 
Page 4 of 10 
 
4
 
Mr. Hall described the General Conditions and concluded by reporting that the Planning 
Commission and staff recommended approval of this item 
 
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council. 
 
Councilmember Thomas asked if it was on sewer, and owner-occupied or rented. 
 
Staff confirmed it was a rental. 
 
Councilmember Graeder noted that this request was only for the rezoning but not for the 
duplex approval itself. 
 
Mayor Whitlock called the applicant forward. 
 
Mr. Midia Jai of 810 Winderose Drive of Hoschton, Georgia came forward representing Bamji Oladeji. 
He showed similar duplex properties that they have developed in Lawrenceville as examples of what 
is intended for this property. 
 
Councilmember Park asked how many parking spaces were anticipated, and Mr. Jai said 2-3 per unit. 
 
The Mayor called for questions/comments from the public. Being none, the Mayor closed the public 
hearing and called for a motion. 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Cummings, seconded by Councilmember 
Thomas, to approve ordinance O2026-30 for the rezoning of 3276 Delma Court (Parcel 
ID R7264 170) from R-75 to RM with conditions as presented. 
 
Voted For: 
 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
2. REZONING REQUEST – CASE Z2026-006 -2407 MAIN ST 
 
 
 
The Mayor and Council considered a request from staff to rezone 2407 Main Street, 
(formerly 2407 Chattahoochee Drive), parcel ID R7205 001, from M-1 (light industrial 
district in unincorporated Gwinnett Co) to M-1 (light industrial district in the City of 
Duluth). Previously used as a pump house for the Gwinnett County Department of Water 
Resources, the County recently sold the property to the City. As the County is no longer 
vested in the property, it will need to be rezoned upon annexation accordingly. 
 
Deputy Director Aron Hall came forward to present. This is an annexation and rezoning of 
0.54 acres which was purchased by the City on March 12, 2026. The subject property is in 
the Sugarloaf Activity District. The comprehensive plan envisions this character area to be 
a connected yet self-sufficient activity center consisting of retail, office, and a variety of 
residential types serving as the northern gateway into the city. Since this was not annexed 
into the city yet, the future land use map has not considered the use of this property. But 
when we do, it would be the M1 Light Industrial. 
 
 
 
 

Draft Minutes of M&C 
July 13, 2026 
Page 5 of 10 
 
5
 
The city acquired this property to expand the public works space across Main Street. This 
also gives the neighboring properties peace of mind in that this M1 property will not be 
used like many M1 industrial properties in terms of noise and outdoor storage since the 
city would control this property. 
 
There are five methods for annexation in the state of Georgia. It's the 100% method, 60% 
resolution of referendum method, annexation by the General Assembly through local 
annexation, and then annexation of unincorporated islands totally surrounded by a city. 
We're doing a mix of both because the city owns 100% of it and it's an island surrounded 
by the city. 
 
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council. Being none, the Mayor called for 
questions/comments from the public. 
 
There being no questions, the Mayor closed the public hearing. No vote was required. 
 
3. ORDINANCE OF ANNEXATION CASE A2026-001 -2407 MAIN ST 
 
 
{D} 
 
Mayor and Council considered the annexation of 2407 Main Street, formerly 2407 
Chattahoochee Drive (Parcel ID R7205 001). The City owns 100% of the land being 
annexed, therefore a hearing was not required. 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Thomas, seconded by Councilmember Doss, 
to approve ordinance O2026-31 for case A2026-001 to annex 2407 Main Street (Parcel 
ID R7205 001) into the City of Duluth and amend the City's map accordingly. 
 
Voted For: 
 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
4. ORDINANCE OF REZONING CASE Z2026-006 - 2407 MAIN ST 
 
 
{E} 
 
Mayor and Council to considered rezoning 2407 Main Street as successfully annexed in a 
vote prior to this action. Per zoning procedures law O.C.G.A. § 36-66-4, the property 
rezoning hearing already took place, with no vote taken by Mayor and Council. 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Park, seconded by Councilmember 
Cummings, to approve Ordinance O2026-32 for case Z2026-006 to rezone 2407 Main 
Street (Parcel ID R7205 001) as presented by staff. 
 
Voted For: 
 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
5. ORDINANCE OF SPECIAL USE – SU2026-002 – YHALE 
 
 
 
{F} 
 
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider a request from owner FWR 
Partners Owner, LLC and Applicant, Yi Hwang Academy, Inc., to approve a special use 
permit for 4400 River Green Parkway (Parcel ID R6325 026) to allow for the operation of a 
public charter/language school in M-1 (Light Industrial District) zoning. 
 
 
 

Draft Minutes of M&C 
July 13, 2026 
Page 6 of 10 
 
6
 
Deputy Director of Planning and Engineering Aron Hall came forward to present. He 
outlined the surrounding property uses and existing conditions. The subject property for 
this one is 5.29 acres and currently zoned M-1. 
 
This is in the River Green Employment District. The Fort of Duluth envisions this character 
to be an economic engine for the city, serving as a major regional distribution and office 
hub. The future land use map envisions the uses to be commercial, retail, office. There are 
currently 10 conditional or special use permits within River Green, including two charter 
schools, a private Catholic school, a private pre-K through 12 school, and a behavioral 
center for pre-K children. The 10 are Notre Dame, Y-Hill, New Life. Notre Dame has two 
properties. New Life Academy has two properties. There's an event hall, and a pre- and 
after-school program. Elevation Autism Center, Scott Hutchins Park, and Ismaili Center 
are all the conditional or special uses within River Green Business Park. 
 
Mr. Hall reported that he building that they would like to occupy, half of it is leased. The 
other half, they would be occupying with grades six, seven, and eight. He showed their 
flow chart for stacking. He then described required conditions for approval and reported 
that the Planning Commission heard this case at the June 1, 2026 meeting and 
recommended approval. Staff also recommends approval of this item. 
 
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council. 
 
Questions were raised regarding parking, stacking and traffic patterns, and increase in 
number of students due to expansion. 
 
The Mayor called the applicant forward to address Council’s questions. 
 
Ms. Melody Glauton of Anderson Tate & Carr, 1960 Satellite Boulevard, Duluth came 
forward on behalf of the applicant. She explained that the school is a dual language 
immersion charter school commissioned in July 2018. The purpose is to allow for the 
continuation of the school that currently serves grades K through seven, and the desire is 
to provide classes for the 17 seventh grade students to roll up to eighth grade. 
 
Ms. Glauton noted all the other schools operating in the area and noted that traffic 
circulation is a factor that they were very willing to work on with the city to ensure safety 
and minimal impact on the area, but that current zoning of M-1 as light industrial could 
lead to truck and freight traffic. She described hours of operation, aftercare activities, and 
the projected growth pattern of enrollment increasing at the kindergarten/first grade 
levels. 
 
Questions were raised regarding future plans to expand to the high school level, feedback 
from the existing parent drivers, and the distance from Peachtree Industrial Blvd to 
ensure traffic would be minimized. 
 
Councilmember Thomas requested a condition be added preventing any students from 
driving, in case the desire to expand to HS was going to be entertained. Ms. Glouton 
agreed that would be acceptable. 
 
Mayor Whitlock called for questions/comments from the public. Being none, the 
Mayor closed public hearing and called for a motion. 
 

Draft Minutes of M&C 
July 13, 2026 
Page 7 of 10 
 
7
A motion was made by Councilmember Thomas, seconded by Councilmember 
Cummings, to approve Ordinance O2026-29 for case SU2026-002 to allow a special 
use permit for 4400 River Green Parkway (Parcel ID R6325 026) with conditions as 
presented and adding the condition that no student parking is permitted. 
 
Voted For: 
 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
6. ORDINANCE TO AMEND UDC – TA2026-004 – STREET LIGHTS 
 
 
{G} 
 
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider an ordinance adjusting the City's 
Unified Development Code Article 9, Project Design and Construction Standards, Section 
907.06. The goal of the revision is to provide clarification and detail regarding lighting 
requirements that must be met by developers and contractors. 
 
Deputy Director Aron Hall presented the proposed changes, which require use of 
ANSI/IES RP-822 as well as Georgia Power guidelines, submission of a photometric plan, 
and requirements for roadway clearance for overhead roadway lighting. Planning 
Commission and staff are recommending approval of this item. 
 
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council. 
 
Councilmember Graeder asked that if it would require LED lighting. 
 
Mr. Hall said he was unsure what the regulations require currently but he would assume 
most modern technology if that is what GA Power was following as well. 
 
Mayor Whitlock said he would hesitate describing technology that we think is modern, 
and then all of a sudden, it's outdated; it would be better to rely on staff. 
 
The Mayor called for questions/comments from the public. Being none, the Mayor closed 
the public hearing and called for a motion. 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Graeder, seconded by Councilmember Doss, 
to approve ordinance O2026-26 to amend the City's Unified Development Code, 
Article 9, as presented. 
 
Voted For: 
 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
 
7. ORDINANCE TO AMEND UDC – TA2026-005 – ACCESSORY STRUCTURES 
{Removed from agenda} 
 
 
8. ORDINANCE TO AMEND UDC – TA2026-006 – FINAL PLAT TEXT BOX 
 
{H} 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider an ordinance amending the City's 
Unified Development Code Article 11, Procedures and Permits, Section 1115.03. 
 
 
 

Draft Minutes of M&C 
July 13, 2026 
Page 8 of 10 
 
8
Deputy Director Aron Hall presented. 
 
Final Plat Specifications should include the option of a text box/signature box for plats 
that do not require dedication of infrastructure to the City. The UDC currently specifies 
only one text box, which includes dedication of infrastructure to the City. There are cases 
when this is not required or desired. Planning Commission and staff recommend 
approval of this item. 
 
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council. 
 
Hearing none, the Mayor called for questions/comments from the public. 
 
No questions brought forward. Mayor Whitlock closed the public hearing and called for a 
motion. 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Graeder, seconded by Councilmember 
Cummings, to approve ordinance O2026-28 for case TA2-26-006 to amend the Unified 
Development Code, Article 11, as presented. 
 
Voted For: 
 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
 
VII. 
NEW BUSINESS 
 
1. AWARD OF BID – 2026 WOODEHAVEN DRIVEWAY REPLACEMENT 
{I,J} 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The Mayor and Council considered awarding the bid for 2026 Woodehaven Driveway 
Replacement and Paving Project. 
 
Public Works Director Audrey Turner came forward to explain the request. The project 
was bid as base bid with three alternates. Base streets are: Woodehaven Driveways: 
Folkstone Drive, Fernsberry Court, Oakwood Way. Asphalt streets: River Mill Drive 
(section from Peachtree Industrial to cul de sac only), Mill Run Court, Mill Falls Court, 
Kingsbrooke Court and River Summit Court. Alternates one through three were priced 
separately and are as follows: Woodehaven Driveways: Crape Myrtle Lane. Asphalt 
Streets: Toccoa Falls Drive and Hiawassee Drive. 
 
The City received nine bids for this project. Following an analysis of each bid, plus 
reference checks by Keck and Wood engineering, staff recommended awarding the 2026 
Woodehaven Driveway Replacement and Paving Project bid (with contingency) to A&S 
Paving, in an amount not to exceed $618,574.37. Funds will come from 2026 
Supplemental LMIG/LRA funds provided by Georgia DOT and SPLOST. 
 
Previously, Council approved a budget amendment to accept the 2026 LRA funds and 
place them in budget to be used for this project. Therefore, staff is only requesting the 
2023 SPLOST Transportation funds needed for the project with approval of a budget 
amendment BA-FY27-03 to add $53,465 in unallocated 2023 SPLOST Transportation funds 
to the Transportation/Infrastructure Improvements - Paved Streets - Professional Services 
line item and $293,065.78 in unallocated 2023 SPLOST Transportation funds to the 
Transportation/Infrastructure Improvements - Paved Streets - Repairs & Maintenance - 
Streets/Sidewalks line item, including associated transfers. 

Draft Minutes of M&C 
July 13, 2026 
Page 9 of 10 
 
9
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Doss, seconded by Councilmember Graeder, 
to approve awarding the 2026 Woodehaven Driveway Replacement and Paving 
Project to A&S Paving, in an amount not to exceed $618,574.37 as presented and 
authorize the Mayor or City Manager to execute the contract as approved by the City 
Attorney and further move to approve ordinance BA-FY27-03 as presented. 
 
Voted For: 
 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
2. CITY HALL ROOF REPLACEMENT – CONTRACT REPLACEMENT 
{K,L} 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
City Manager James Riker explained that, in May of this year, Council awarded Cotton 
Commercial, Inc. a contract to replace the City Hall with a low slope roof. During a 
mandatory pre construction meeting representatives from Cotton Commercial realized 
they had failed to include pricing for the complete scope of the project and disputed the 
contents of the project details. Accordingly, Cotton Commercial and staff mutually agree 
it is in both parties’ best interests to cancel the contract. 
 
Once the contract with Cotton Commercial is terminated staff is recommending that a 
contract award be made to Dusty Greer Roofing for replacement of the City Hall roof. 
Dusty Greer Roofing scored the second highest points for the RFP scoring. The contract 
with Dusty Greer Roofing is slightly higher than the previously awarded contract with 
Cotton Commercial. Accordingly a budget amendment is required to add an additional 
$27,928 in 2023 SPLOST funds to the project. 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Thomas, seconded by Councilmember 
Graeder, to the Cancellation/Release Agreement with Cotton Commercial and to 
award a contract to Dusty Greer Roofing in the amount of $123,000 for replacement of 
the City Hall Roof. Further I move to authorize a budget amendment BA-FY27-02 to 
add $27,928 in unallocated 2023 SPLOST Administrative Facilities funds be added to 
City Hall Design\Build - General Government Buildings - Buildings line item, including 
associated transfers. 
 
Voted For: 
 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
 
VIII. 
MATTERS FROM DEPT HEADS/CITY ATTORNEY 
 
1. ORDINANCE REAPPOINTING TADAC MEMBERS 
 
 
 
{M} 
 
City Manager James Riker explained that re-appoinments were necessary to change the 
County representatives to the job titles required to serve rather than individuals, as well as 
renew the City’s appointments. Therefore, Mayor and Council were asked to consider 
approval of ordinance 02026-33, re-appointing Greg Whitlock and Manfred Graeder to the 
Tax Allocation District Advisory Committee, terms ending July 10, 2030 and specifying 
titles of other required members. 
 
Appointed Members: 
Greg Whitlock 
Expires 7/10/30. Term begin date: 2014 (Term limit ends 2028.) 
Manfred Graeder Expires 7/10/30. Term begin date: 2024 

Draft Minutes of M&C 
July 13, 2026 
Page 10 of 10 
 
10 
 
Permanent Members: 
Duluth City Manager 
Chair, Gwinnett County Commission 
Director, Gwinnett County Planning Dept 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Doss, seconded by Councilmember Park, to 
approve ordinance O2026-33 as presented. 
 
Voted For: 
 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
 
IX. 
MATTERS FROM MAYOR & COUNCIL 
 
1. APPRECIATION FOR EVENTS AND PROGRAMMING & SOCIAL MEDIA 
 
Council was complimentary of the types of recent city events that have been provided as 
well as the Duluth 150th social media posts. 
 
2. BUNTEN PARK IMPROVEMENTS 
 
Parks Director Kathy Marelle gave quick updates on the walking trail reconstruction. 
There is a QR code on the construction sign that points to the most recent information 
regarding the project. It is anticipated to be complete by spring break, 2027. 
 
3. JULY 3 LASER SHOW EVENT 
 
Staff and Council to revisit what type of July 4 commemoration would be appropriate and 
feasible for next year. 
 
 
X. 
MATTERS FROM CITY MANAGER 
 
City Manager James Riker noted that a previous noise complaint was investigated and 
found to have merit. He recommended a future amendment to the noise ordinance; 
council supported. 
 
 
XI. 
ADJOURNMENT 
 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Thomas, seconded by Councilmember 
Cummings, to adjourn at 7:20 pm. 
 
Voting for: 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried. 
 
 
 
 
The next scheduled meeting of the Mayor and Council is a work session 
for July 27, 2026 at 5:30 p.m.

related to Title VI requirements, successes, and annual reporting. Approval of this 
item authorizes the Mayor to execute the documents for staff submission to the 
Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT) prior to June 30, 2026. 
 
2. ACCEPT GA DOT GRANT/ORDINANCE TO AMEND BUDGET 
 
The City received $348,008.60 from the Georgia Department of Transportation 
(GDOT) representing the City's share of the 2026 Local Maintenance Improvement 
Grant (LMIG) Supplemental. Approval of this item approves ordinance BA-FY26-42 
to add $348,008.60 in 2026 LMIG Supplemental funds to the GDOT State Grant 
line item and a like amount to the Transportation/Infrastructure Improvements - 
Paved Streets - Repairs & Maintenance - Streets/Sidewalks line item.

3. ORDINANCE TO AMEND BUDGET -$55,000– HUDGENS TRL 
 
Based on council directions at the April 27th work session, staff is requesting 
approval of a budget amendment for $55,000 to contract with Practical Design 
Partners (PDP) to prepare design alternatives for the Hudgens Trail pedestrian 
and bike connectivity concepts. PDP will develop up to five alternatives with cost 
estimates, hold a public hearing, and finalize the alternatives and cost options 
based on public and city input. Approval of this item authorizes ordinance BA-
FY26-43 to add $55,000 in 2017 SPLOST Transportation Funds to (CD-61) Hudgens 
Trail - Sidewalks & Crosswalks - Professional Services line item, including 
associated transfers. 
 
 
VI. 
PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1. FY27 BUDGET – SECOND PUBLIC HEARING 
 
Per the State of Georgia code, the Mayor and Council to hold a public hearing to 
receive public comments on the proposed FY 2027 Annual Operating and Capital 
Projects Budget. Ken Sakmar, Assistant City Manager/Finance and 
Redevelopment Director, will present the proposed FY27 budget and highlight 
various changes in the budget. Following the public hearing an ordinance 
adopting the FY2027 budget will be presented for consideration. 
 
 
2. ORDINANCE – UDC TEXT AMENDMENT, CASE TA 2026-003 
 
Mayor and Council to consider an ordinance adjusting the City's Unified 
Development Code Article 2, Table 2-C (Use of Land and Structures Table). This 
table lists principal uses allowed by zoning district. The applicant is requesting the 
ability to apply for a special use permit to operate a medical office in the M-1 (Light 
Industrial) zoning district. Currently, this use is neither allowed by right nor by 
special use. 
 
Allowing a use via "special use permit" allows neighbors to weigh in at a public 
hearing, allows staff to review surrounding land uses, and allows council to place 
conditions on such uses if they are found to be appropriate. Staff recommends 
approval of this item. 
 
3. ORDINANCE OF SPECIAL USE– CASE SU2026-001 
 
 
 
Owner/Applicant, Rosibel Gonzalez Carpinone of R and H General Services, LLC is 
requesting a special use permit for 4319 Abbotts Bridge Road, Building 3, Suite 5 
(Parcel ID R6324 249) to allow for a med spa/medical office. This request assumes 
a prior approval of Text Amendment TA2026-003, which would add the potential 
for a special use permit to this zoning category. Planning Commission heard this 
case at the May 4, 2026 meeting and recommended approval (pending the 
approval of case TA2026-003.) Staff also recommends approval of this item.

June 8, 2026

4
4. ORDINANCE OF REZONING – CASE Z2026-002 
 
Owner, Cecil Eugene Tucker and Applicant, Altamirano Ramos are requesting the 
rezoning of 3639 Rogers Bridge Road (PIN R7203 045) from O-I (Office Institutional 
District) to R-100 (Single Family Residential District) to allow for the construction of 
a single family home. Planning Commission heard this case at the May 4, 2026 
meeting and recommended approval of the R-50 zoning district (over the R-100 
zoning district) with concurrence from the owner and applicant as R-50 will allow 
for more flexibility in designing and building the new home. Staff also 
recommends approval of this item. 
 
 
 
VII. 
NEW BUSINESS 
 
1. AWARD OF BID/AMEND BUDGET – CITY HALL ROOF 
 
The Mayor and Council to consider awarding a contract for replacement of the 
City Hall roof. 
 
The low slope roof system at City Hall is original to the building and circa 2007. 
Accordingly, staff published a Request for Proposal (RFP) for replacement. Staff 
received seven proposals and following an evaluation by an outside consultant, 
staff is recommending that the contract be awarded to Cotton Commercial USA, 
Inc, in the amount of $ 98,714.79. Given the complexity of the roof staff is also 
recommending a 15% contingency be added for a total request of $ 113,522.00 
 
Additionally, staff is requesting approval of a budget amendment BA-FY26-40 to 
add $113,522 in unallocated 2023 SPLOST Administrative Facilities funds to City Hall 
Design/Build - General Government Buildings - Buildings line item, including 
associated transfers.

Improvements at Public Safety Building. (Legal notice is attached and was run 
twice in Gwinnett Daily Post as well as placed on Georgia Procurement Registry 
and City website). Project was bid for repair and resurfacing of parking areas and 
repair of concrete sidewalks, steps, and entryway at front of Public Safety. 
 
The City received four bids for this project, bid tabulation is attached. Following an 
analysis of each bid by Pond & Company, staff recommends awarding the bid for 
Pavement Repairs and Site Improvements at Public Safety to Allied Paving, (with 
contingency) in an amount not to exceed $1,225,883.15. Funds will come from

Facilities funds of $425,500. Staff is requesting approval of a budget amendment 
BA-FY26-41 to add $1,225,884 in unallocated SPLOST Public Safety and Parking

Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider an ordinance to allow the

Ms. Pozin summarized the request. The owner, Duluth More Space, LLC and 
applicant, Duluth North Berkeley Industrial Owner, LLC are requesting a rezoning 
of this Planned Unit Development (PUD) to allow a change in the master plan. 
The current PUD includes facilities for indoor storage that were never constructed. 
The Owner and Applicant are requesting a change in the master plan to allow for 
demolition of the existing vacant seven story building and the construction and 
operation of roughly 198,000 square feet of flex office/warehouse. 
 
Ms. Pozin showed the location and described the subject property, which is 
approximately 16 acres in the North Berkeley International Village. 
FORWARDuluth envisions this Character Area to continue to be a magnet for 
small and medium sized minority and internationally owned businesses targeting 
Duluth’s diverse community. The Future Land Use Map (FLUM) envisions the uses 
to be Industrial.

office building shell and associated parking that has remained partially 
constructed since 2008. In 2020 the building was deemed unsafe by the Building 
Official. The property was placed on the blighted property list in 2021. The property

2. FY2027 BUDGET PRESENTATION 
 
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to receive public comments on the 
FY2027 budget. Prior to this public hearing, council and staff reviewed the 
proposed FY 2027 budget at a budget workshop on May 4th. A second public 
hearing will be held on Monday, June 8, 2026 at the regularly scheduled meeting 
of the Mayor and Council. Following the second public hearing, an ordinance 
adopting the FY 2027 budget will be presented for consideration. 
 
Assistant City Manager/Finance Ken Sakmar came forward to present an overview 
of the proposed FY 2027 Annual Operating and Capital Projects Budget of 
approximately $43 million. On the revenue side, similar figures are presented but 
the budget does require some reserves used to balance the budget. He showed 
the capital projects as well, which are based on the life of the project, not the fiscal 
year. 
 
Mr. Sakmar explained the conservative nature of budget philosophy, but noted 
that last year the proposal anticipated using about $921,000 of reserves to balance 
the budget, but this year it’s approximately $120,000 in excess of that number to 
balance this year's budget. This is the season of review and some of those funds 
that are unobligated would be used to balance prior to tapping into reserves.

Discrimination Complaint Procedure 
1. Any person who believes that he or she, individually, as a member of any specific class, or
in connection with any disadvantaged business enterprise, has been subjected to
discrimination prohibited by Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the American with
Disabilities Act of 1990, Section 504 of the Vocational Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and the Civil
Rights Restoration Act of 1987, as amended, may file a complaint with the recipient. A
complaint may also be filed by a representative on behalf of such a person. All complaints
will be referred to the recipient’s Title VI Specialist for review and action.
2. In order to have the complaint consideration under this procedure, the complainant must file
the complaint no later than 180 days after:
a) The date of alleged act of discrimination; or
b) Where there has been a continuing course of conduct, the date on which that conduct
was discontinued.
In either case, the recipient or his/her designee may extend the time for filing or waive the time 
limit in the interest of justice, specifying in writing the reason for so doing. 
3. Complaints shall be in writing and shall be signed by the complainant and/or the
complainant’s representative. Complaints shall set forth as fully as possible the facts and
circumstances surrounding the claimed discrimination. In the event that a person makes a
verbal complaint of discrimination to an officer or employee of the recipient, the person shall
be interviewed by the Title VI Specialist. If necessary, the Title VI Specialist will assist the
person in reducing the complaint to writing and submit the written version of the complaint to
the person for signature. The complaint shall then be handled according to the recipient’s
investigative procedures.
4. Within 10 days, the Title VI Specialist will acknowledge receipt of the allegation, inform the
complainant of action taken or proposed action to process the allegation, an advise the
complainant of other avenues of redress available, such as GDOT and USDOT.
5. The recipient will advise GDOT within 10 days of receipt of the allegations. Generally, the
following information will be included in every notification to GDOT:
a) Name, address, and phone number of the complainant.
b) Name(s) and address (es) of alleged discriminating official(s).
c) Basis of complaint (i.e., race, color, or national origin)
d) Date of alleged discriminatory act(s).
e) Date of complaint received by the recipient.

ning to a build a mixed-use

cial space on more than 111

clude about 1,400 residenc-

er house and a shed, and a

Chelsea Lumpkin just finished 
her first year as a teacher at Law-
renceville’s Alford Elementary 
School, but what should have 
been her first summer break as 
an educator is starting off with 
mourning from her friends and 
colleagues.
Lumpkin, 32, was killed in a 
car crash, which happened in 
the Cedar Ridge Road area near 
Monroe over the Memorial Day 
Weekend. Her death came just 
one year after she graduated from 
Kennesaw State University with a 
degree in elementary education.
“She was someone who lit up 
the room with her smile, pres-
ence, and attitude, 
which will be great-
ly missed,” Kenne-
saw State’s National 
Pan-Hellenic Coun-
cil, which Lumpkin 
was active in as a 
student, said in a 
tribute to her on 
Instagram.
The Georgia State 
Patrol said Lumpkin was driving 
west on State Route 10 near Ce-
dar Ridge Road at 10:40 a.m. last 
Saturday when her vehicle ran 
off the road and hit a tree. She 
was not wearing her seat belt at 
the time and was partially ejected 
from her vehicle.
A GSP spokesperson said Lump-
kin died from her injuries at the 
scene.
Tributes could be found all over 
the internet this week as friends 
and colleagues remembered her.
Some colleagues posted trib-
utes to her on a condolences 
wall maintained by Jackson Mc-
Whorter Funeral Home, which 
is handling Lumpkin’s funeral 
arrangements.
Some colleagues recalled her 
energy and how much she cared 
about her students.
“I’ll always remember her big, 
affectionate smile, her love of danc-
ing, and the passion she had for 
her students,” Alford Elementary 
teacher La’Toya Williams wrote. 
“She truly cared about making a 
difference.
“She had such a bright future 
ahead of her, and it was inspiring 
to see how excited she was about 
her first year of teaching and con-
tinuing her education in the field 
of Instructional Technology.”
Kennesaw State’s NPHC is plan-
ning to hold a balloon release in 
Lumpkin’s memory at 7 p.m. on 
Thursday at Swift Cantrell Park 
in Kennesaw. Attendees are asked 
to wear pink in her honor.
She was a native of Athens and 
a member of the Pi Phi chapter 
of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, 
where she served as vice presi-
dent and chaplain, at Kennesaw 
State. She was also an SGA sena-
tor, FSL ambassador, an orien-
tation leader, the membership 
chair for NSLS and executive di-
rector of diversity and inclusion 
during her time at KSU.
She graduated from Kennesaw 
State’s Bagwell College of Edu-
cation with cum laude honors.
“Chelsea Lumpkin has done it 
all with grace,” Kendalyn McBride 
said in a tribute to Lumpkin.
McBride started a GoFundMe 
campaign to help Lumpkin’s 
family with funeral costs. As of 
Wednesday night, the effort had 
already raised more than $9,000.
“Her kindness, humor, and 
uplifting energy will truly be 
missed,” McBride wrote on the 
GoFundMe page.
Details about Lumpkin’s funer-
al have not been made public yet. 
The GoFundMe campaign to help 
her family can be found at tinyurl.
com/yckdtzj6.

request from the Director, the Planning Commission, the Zoning Board of Appeals, or any private 
citizen or property owner, or on its own motion, upon a determination that the public necessity, 
general welfare or good zoning practice justifies such action.” 
 
This text amendment is brought before you at the request of Rosibel Gonzalez Carpinone, to allow a 
Medical Office (NAICS Code 621) to be allowed by Special Use in the M-1 (Light Industrial Zoning) 
district. Currently Medical Offices are allowed by right in the Central Business District/CBD (in 
certain circumstances), C-1 (Neighborhood Business District), C-2 (General Business District), HC-R 
(Highway-Commercial Retail District), HC-A (Highway-Commercial Auto District), O-I (Office-
Institutional District), and O-N (Office-Neighborhood District). 
 
Standards for Code Amendments 
 
The following four standards shall be considered when deciding on a code amendment: 
 
1. Is the proposed amendment consistent with the purpose and intent of this Development 
Code as stated under Article 1? 
2. Does the proposed amendment further or is it compatible with the purpose and intent of 
the Comprehensive Plan? 
3. Is the proposed amendment required to adequately address new or changing conditions or 
to properly implement the Comprehensive Plan? 
4. Does the proposed amendment reasonably promote public health, safety, or general 
welfare?

Literal Interpretation of the Unified Development Code (UDC) 
 
A. Assuming TA2026-003 is approved prior to hearing this case, Table 2-C of the UDC 
allows a “Medical Offices” in M-1 (Light Industrial District) zoning as a special use. 
 
B. Section 1101.02 of the UDC states if a proposed use is not allowed by right under the 
existing zoning on a property, a request for an amendment to the Official Zoning 
Map (often called a “rezoning”) must be approved prior to development, 
construction, or occupancy. 
 
C. Section 1105 of the UDC establishes the Special Use Considerations. 
 
The Special Use is designed to apply under any one of the following circumstances: 
1. A Special Use listed under the zoning district is desired for development and a 
more intensive zoning district containing that use, as a use by right would not be 
appropriate for the property; or 
 
2. A Special Use listed under the zoning district is desired for development and no 
zoning district contains that use as a use by right; or 
 
3. A unique use not addressed in any zoning district is desired for development and 
is not likely to be duplicated within the City of Duluth; or 
 
4. The density of development may be affected by the height of a building; or 
 
5. The neighboring properties may be affected by the height of any structure; or

6. The Special Use would be consistent with the needs of the neighborhood or the 
community as a whole, be compatible with the neighborhood and would not be 
in conflict with the overall objective of the Comprehensive Plan.

to approve such a use on a particular parcel without changing the general zoning district. 
Such approval shall be subject to the requirements set forth below and any additional 
conditions deemed necessary to ensure the compatibility of the Special Use with the 
surrounding properties. All Special Use applications shall be for firm development 
proposals only. The Special Use shall not be used for securing early zoning for conceptual 
proposals that may not be undertaken for some time. A Special Use application shall be 
considered only if the application is made by the owner of the property or by his/her 
authorized agent. The minimum requirements for a Special Use approval are: 
1. Any uses allowed under Special Use approval shall also conform to the 
requirements of this Development Code for all uses as found in the zoning 
district. 
 
2. The application and review process for a Special Use shall be the same as for the 
zoning district under which the Special Use is found. In addition to the 
information and/or site plans which are required to be submitted for the 
proposed development, additional information deemed necessary by the 
Director in order to evaluate a proposed use and its relationship to the 
surrounding area shall be submitted. In the review process, particular emphasis 
shall be given to the evaluation of the characteristics of the proposed use in 
relationship to its immediate neighborhood and the compatibility of the 
proposed use with its neighborhood. 
 
3. In the approval process for a Special Use approval application, the City Council 
shall consider the policies and objectives of the Comprehensive Plan, particularly

activities.

that may have been attached to the approval are binding to the property. All

C. Whether the zoning proposal will result in a use that will or could cause an excessive or 
burdensome use of existing streets, transportation facilities, utilities, or schools. 
D. Whether the zoning proposal is consistent with the Land Use Policy Plan, 
Comprehensive Plan, transportation plans, or other plans adopted for guiding

development within the City of Duluth. 
E. Whether there are other existing or changing conditions affecting the use and 
development of property that give supporting grounds for either approval or 
disapproval of the zoning or special use proposal. 
 
The Applicant has provided written responses to the above Special Use standards and 
Rezoning Standards as part of the application. Those documents are attached hereto as 
Exhibit “D”. 
 
 
Comprehensive Plan 
 
Every section of Duluth’s Comprehensive Plan, FORWARDuluth Plan 2040, is central to 
implementing the City’s vision and goals. However, the Character Areas and Future Land Use 
Maps are the most influential in terms of daily decision-making and land use changes. The 
Character Area Map is intended to work hand-in-hand with the Future Land Use Map when 
considering city-wide policies and when land-use applications are presented to the Planning 
Commission and City Council. The Character Area Map and related text will set the 
overarching goals for specific areas within the City. The Future Land Use Map gives parcel by 
parcel recommendations for future development. 
 
The subject property is located within the Established Neighbrohoods. FORWARDuluth 
states, “Established Neighbrohoods will continue to be the backbone of Duluth’s residential 
commmunity”. 
 
The Future Land Use Map envisions this property to be Commercial/Retail/Office. 
 
IV. 
PLANNING STAFF REVIEW 
 
Staff finds that a single-family detached home would be a better fit on this property than 
anything O-I (Office-Institutional District) could support on this half-acre property. The 
associated parking and stormwater requirements for a new build on a vacant half-acre lot 
would be most prohibitive to any kind of meaningful development other than single-family 
residential. 
 
The surrounding uses are all single-family residential save for the M-1 (Light Industrial 
District) property to the north which is currently occupied by Hands of Christ (also known 
as, the Duluth CO-OP), which is very much a neighborhood service tucked between single-
family residential uses. During construction for the new Hands of Christ location on Rogers 
Bridge Road, the developer had to extend sewer from Main Street, which now allows the 
opportunity for this property to be on sewer instead of septic. 
 
Rezoning to R-100 (Single-Family Residential District) would allow a single-family detached 
house on the property. 
 
Although the request was made for R-100 (Single-Family Residential District), staff is 
recommending, with the support of the applicant, that the parcel be rezoned to R-50 instead. 
The lot width of the property is 75’ along Rogers Bridge Road. Rezoning the property to R-

 
 
Z2026-002 
Page 4 of 13 
 
100 (Single-Family Residential District) would create a legal non-conforming lot. Though the 
applicant could legally build a single-family home on the property if it is rezoned to R-100, 
the width of the property would constrain the size and location of the home. R-100 (Single-
Family Residential District) lots have a front setback of 30’ minimum, side setback of 10’ 
minimum, and a rear setback of 20’ minimum. The lot coverage maximum is 45%. 
 
For a lot zoned R-50 (Single-Family Residential District), lots have a front setback of 10’ 
minimum, side setback of 5’ minimum, and a rear setback of 15’ minimum. The lot coverage 
maximum is 50%. 
 
R-50 is the newest zoning category, which allows minimum lot sizes of 7500 sq ft. If it is 
decided to rezone the property to residential, staff is recommending it be rezoned to R-50 
(Single-Family Residential District). 
 
 
 
 
V. 
Recommendation 
 
Planning Commission heard this case on May 4, 2026, and recommended the property be 
rezoned to R-50 (Single-Family Residential).

Termination 
 
11.1 
The City may terminate the contract for failure by the Contractor to comply with the 
terms and conditions of its contract or failure by the Contractor to correct problems 
brought to its attention by the City, each of which failures shall constitute a default. 
In the event of such termination, that Contractor will be paid only those sums due

offset for damages and other amounts which are, or which may become, due and 
owing to the City. 
 
11.2 
The City, for its convenience and without cause, may terminate this contract 
whenever the City determines that such termination is in its best interest after 
giving ten (10) days written notice of such termination to the Contractor. In the 
event of a termination for convenience, the City shall pay all amounts due and 
owing to the Contractor for performance satisfactorily rendered. However, in no 
event shall the total amounts paid to the Contractor exceed the contract price. The 
Contractor shall not be reimbursed for any profits which may have been 
anticipated, but which have not been earned up to the date of termination.

Disputes/Resolutions 
 
12.1 
Any claims or disputes that may arise, including adjustments to compensation or 
to time of completion, shall be initiated by written notice within five (5) days after 
either party becomes aware of the claim or issue in dispute. The parties shall have 
ten (10) days following such written notice to cure or resolve any dispute. 
Notwithstanding the foregoing, the failure to provide written notice shall not serve 
as a bar to an action in law or equity for either party. 
12.2 
The City and Contractor shall make all reasonable efforts to resolve any and all 
matters of dispute without the involvement of any third party. However, if such 
efforts are not successful after a thirty (30) day period, then both parties agree to 
resolve their claims by filing a Complaint in the Superior Court of Gwinnett County, 
Georgia. The terms of this Agreement shall be integrated and enforced under the 
Laws of Georgia.

1 FAMILIARITY WITH SITE 
Execution of this agreement by the Contractor is a representation that the Contractor has visited

This agreement consists of the City's request for proposals, instructions to bidders, Contractor's 
proposal, construction contract, Performance Bond, Payment Bond, general conditions, special 
provisions, specifications, plans, drawings, addenda, and written change orders. 
 
3 DEFINITIONS 
The following terms as used in this agreement are defined as follows: 
 
Change Order - a written order to the Contractor, prepared by the Consultant and issued by the 
City for changes in the work within the general scope of the contract documents, adjustment of 
the contract price, extension of the contract time, or reservation of determination of a time 
extension. 
 
City – The City of Duluth, a political subdivision of the State of Georgia. 
 
Day - a calendar day of twenty-four hours lasting from midnight of one day to midnight the next 
day. 
 
Notice to Proceed - written communication issued by the City to the Contractor authorizing it to 
proceed with the work and establishing the date of commencement and completion of the work. 
 
Substantial Completion - the date certified by the Consultant when all or a part of the work, 
identified in the Consultant's certification, is sufficiently completed in accordance with the 
requirements of the contract documents so that the identified portion of the work can be utilized 
for the purposes for which it is intended. 
 
Work - all of the services specified, indicated, shown or contemplated by the contract documents, 
and furnishing by the Contractor of all materials, equipment, labor, methods, processes, 
construction and manufacturing materials and equipment, tools, plans, supplies, power, water, 
transportation and other things necessary to complete such services in accordance with the 
contract documents to ensure a functional and complete facility.

additions, amendments and revisions of such referenced standards in effect as of the date of the 
request for proposals for this contract.

the Consultant any error, ambiguity, inconsistency or omission that may be discovered, including

year average of accumulated mean values for climatological data compiled by the U.S. 
Department of Commerce for Atlanta, Georgia and that such greater than normal inclement

therefore.

agreement.

anticipated extent of the delay, and any recommended action to avoid or minimize the delay.

condition precedent to such entitlement shall be strict compliance with all requirements and

89 FORCE ACCOUNT WORK 
Force account work is an Owner-defined emergency, a sudden or unforeseen failure or 
malfunction of an existing system, which results in the Contractor being obligated to respond to 
the site of the emergency as Owner-directed. Contractor may perform work on a force account 
basis and will be paid for properly allocated charges which may include labor, bond premium, 
supplies and materials, equipment and subcontract billings, incurred in the performance of such 
force account work as more particularly described below: 
 
A. Labor: All labor shall be billed at the hourly rates specified in the bid. Regular rates will apply 
during normal business hours, defined as Monday through Friday, 7 a.m.–5 p.m. Overtime 
rates will apply during non-normal business hours. If premium rates apply, then overtime rates 
shall be defined as Monday through Friday, 5 p.m.–8 p.m. Accordingly, premium rates, if 
applicable, shall be defined as Monday through Saturday, 8 p.m.–7 a.m., all hours on Sundays 
and all City recognized holidays. A foreman shall not be used where there are fewer than two 
(2) laborers employed, except with the written consent of the City. Subsistence and travel 
allowance where required by collective bargaining agreements shall be included. 
 
The charges for labor shall include all classifications through foremen when engaged in the 
actual and direct performance of the Work. They shall not include charges for such overhead 
personnel as assistant superintendents, superintendents, office personnel, timekeepers, and 
maintenance mechanics. 
 
B. Bonds and Insurance: For bonds and insurance premiums or increases thereto necessitated 
by the force account work, Contractor shall receive the actual cost to which no percent shall 
be added. Contractor shall furnish satisfactory evidence of the rate or rates paid for such bond 
and insurance. 
 
C. Materials: For materials accepted by the City and used as an integral part of the finished Work, 
Contractor shall receive the actual cost of such materials delivered on the Work, including 
transportation charges paid by him, exclusive of machinery rentals as hereinafter set forth.

prime contractors or the Owner.

including ductwork, pipe, cables and conduits penetrating floors, 
walls, smoke compartments to provide fire stops with fire resistance 
ratings for floor or wall assembly in which penetration occurs. 
7. 
Installation Techniques: Employ only proven installation techniques, which 
will ensure that caulks/sealants are deposited in uniform, continuous 
ribbons without gaps or air pockets, with "wetting" of joint bond surfaces 
equally on opposite sides. Except as otherwise indicated, fill sealant rabbet 
to a slightly concave surface, slightly below adjoining surfaces. Where 
horizontal joints are between a horizontal surface and vertical surface, fill 
joint to form a slight cove, so joint will not trap moisture and dirt. 
8. 
Sealant Depth: Install sealant to depths as shown or, if not shown, as 
recommended by sealant manufacturer but with the following general 
limitations, measured at center (thin) section of bead: 
a. 
For sidewalks, pavements and similar joints sealed with sealants and 
subject to traffic and other abrasion and indentation exposures, fill 
joints to a depth equal to 75% of joint width, but neither more than 5/8" 
deep nor less than 3/8" deep. 
b. 
For joints sealed with elastomeric sealants but not subject to traffic, 
fill joints to a depth equal to 50% of joint width, but neither more than 
1/2" deep nor less than 1/4" deep. 
9. 
Spillage: Do not allow sealants or compounds to overflow or spill onto 
adjoining surface, or to migrate into the voids of adjoining surfaces including 
rough textures such as exposed aggregate panels. Using masking tape or 
other precautionary devices to prevent staining of adjoining surfaces, by 
either primer/sealer or sealant/caulking compound. Clean adjoining 
surfaces by whatever means may be necessary to eliminate evidence of 
spillage.

Clean and free from stains surfaces of all materials adjoining caulked or sealed 
joints. Remove excess of caulking or sealant on adjoining surfaces in accordance 
with the caulking or sealant manufacturer's instructions. 
 
3.4

Cure sealants and caulking compounds in compliance with manufacturer's 
instructions and recommendations to obtain high early bond strength, internal 
cohesive strength and surface durability. Advise Contractor of procedures required

without deterioration or damage (other than normal wear and weathering) at time 
of substantial completion.

Cotton and the Client Partner will establish four specific times to assist in the implementation of
a disaster recovery plan:
Preparedness
The continuity planning phase is a period of time during which activities are undertaken by
Cotton to increase readiness posture, policies, procedures and incident command systems of
the partnership. This includes, but is not limited to, identification of risks that can bring about
disasters
by conducting
risk analysis
covering
threats
to business
continuity. Also, this period
includes, but is not limited to, pre-disaster assessment of critical infrastructure with emphasis on
the vulnerabilities that may affect the likelihood of catastrophic failure for an enterprise.
Response
The reaction phase is a period of time during which notification procedure activities and initial
damage and disruption surreys are undertaken. To establish how the contingency plan will be
executed following
a disaster, it is crucial to evaluate the nature and degree of damage to the
enterprise. Cotton then activates response plans and begins to execute contingency actions
with the Partner Client.
Mitigation
The mitigation
phase starts immediately after the disaster recovery plan has been activated and
appropriate teams have been mobilized. The activities of this phase focus on setting in motion
the disaster recovery system, reduction of initial damage, and detailed evaluation of the crisis
and potential for additional crisis or ancillary risks. The recovery procedure reflects priorities
previously analyzed during the activation planning phase.
Recovery
In the recovery phase, activities are undertaken to fully recover the enterprise from disaster,
place them back in a pre- loss condition, and return the enterprise operations back to the Partner
Client through
a complete host of catastrophe
management
and reconstruction services.

Advertisement for Bids
2026 LMIG Paving
Project on various
streets within the City of
Duluth
The City of Duluth is ac-
cepting sealed bids from
qualified contractors to
provide all necessary la-
bor, material and equip-
ment necessary to per-
form asphaltic concrete
milling, deep patching
(as directed), excavation
of unsuitable material as
needed,
 
replacement,
grading, compaction of
grade aggregate base
course as needed, patch-
ing, and installation or
replacement of thermo-
plastic striping, traffic
control, erosion control
and dust control on vari-
ous streets within the
City limits of Duluth. All
work shall be in accor-
dance with the specifica-
tions, the applicable
drawings and subject to
the terms and conditions
of this contract.
The contract will include
multiple road projects
for milling, patching and
resurfacing. A proposed
BASE project list as well
as a proposed Alternate
(additional
 
list
 
of
projects) is included in
the full Invitation to Bid
available at www.duluth-
ga.net under the heading
Notices and RFPs. 
All sealed bids will be re-
ceived by the City of Du-
luth City Clerk, 3167
Main Street, Duluth,
Georgia 30096, until 1:45
P.M. local time on Tues-
day, March 31, 2026.
Bids received after the
stated time will not be
accepted. Bids will be
opened publicly and read
aloud on Tuesday, March
31, 2026 at 2:00 P.M. on
the second floor of Du-
luth City Hall, 3167 Main
Street, Duluth GA 30096,
in the Executive Confer-
ence Room. The bid en-
velope must be marked
on the outside with the
following information:
City of Duluth
Bid 2026 LMIG Paving
Project
 
on
 
Various
Roads within City of Du-
luth
Date and Hour of Bid
Opening
Company Name
Winning contractor will
be required to provide an
Eighteen month (18)
warranty on all work
completed.
Pre-Bid Conference will
be held at City of Duluth
Public Works Facility
2450 Main Street in Du-
luth, Georgia 30096, on
Tuesday, March 10, 2026
at 10:00 A.M. 
Full Invitation to Bid is
available on the City of
Duluth website, www.du-
luthga.net under the
heading Notices and
RFPs
Full Invitation to Bid is
also available for view-
ing at the Duluth Public
Works Department, 2450
Main Street, Duluth,
Georgia 30097.
Bid will be awarded
based upon Base Bid and
selected alternates. Al-
ternates will be selected
by the City at time of bid
opening. City retains full
discretion on which, if
any, alternates will be
selected. 
Contract will be award-
ed, if at all, within sixty
(60) calendar days after
opening of the proposal.
Deadline for questions is
Tuesday, March 17, 2026
at 5 P.M. Submit all
questions to Adam Shel-
ton, PE, of Keck & Wood
at
 
GAbids2025@keck-
wood.com 
 No phone
calls will be accepted.
The selected contractor
must be able to start
work within ten (10) cal-
endar days after the No-
tice to Proceed is issued.
The time of completion
for the project is ninety
(90) calendar days from
the date of the Notice to
Proceed.
All bids shall be accom-
panied by a bid bond in
favor of the City, in the
amount of five percent
(5%) of the total bid,
(but not less than
$5,000); such bid bond
representing that the bid-
der, if awarded a con-
tract, will promptly en-
ter into a contract and
furnish
 
performance
bond and payment bond
as provided by law and
approved by the attorney
for the City. Failure to
submit a bid bond with
the proper rating will re-
sult in the bid being
deemed non-responsive. 
Successful bidder will be
required to meet insur-
ance requirements. Per-
formance and Payment
bonds will be required
upon acceptance of the
proposal and contract
submittal. 
The Performance Bond
shall be equal to one hun-
dred percent (100%) of
the contract amount. The
Payment Bond shall be
equal to one hundred ten
percent (110%) of the
contract amount. 
 Insurance and Bonding
Company must be li-
censed to do business by
the Georgia Secretary of
State, authorized to busi-
ness in Georgia by the
Georgia Insurance De-
partment, listed in the
Department of Treasurys
Publication of Companies
holding Certificates of
Authority as Acceptable
Surety on Federal Bonds
and as acceptable rein-
suring companies. The
bid bond, payment bond
and performance bond
must have an A.M. Best
rating of A-5 or higher.
Award will be made to
the lowest responsible
and responsive bidder.
The City of Duluth re-
serves the right to reject
any and all bids, to waive
technicalities and to
make an award as
deemed in its best inter-
est. 
Any change to the condi-
tions and specifications
must be in the form of a
written addendum to be
valid; therefore, the City
will issue a written ad-
dendum to document
each approved change.

1. FY27 BUDGET —- SECOND PUBLIC HEARING {D}
Per state law, the Mayor and Council are to hold a public hearing to receive public
comments on the proposed FY 2027 Annual Operating and Capital Projects Budget.
Council previously reviewed the budget at a work session on May 4, and a previous
public hearing was held May 11. Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing.

Ken Sakmar, Assistant City Manager/Finance Director, came forward to present the
proposed FY27 budget and highlight various changes in the budget. He summarized
the 43 million budget categories and the capital projects, gave the comparison from
FY26 to FY27, and highlighted the biggest changes and major expenses and
revenues.

The current millage rate has remained the same for several years and is anticipated to
be the same. An ordinance adopting the FY2027 budget was presented for
consideration.

Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council. Hearing none, the Mayor called
for questions/comments from the public.

Being no further discussion, Mayor Whitlock closed the public hearing and called for a
motion.

A motion was made by Councilmember Thomas, seconded by Councilmember
Doss, to approve ordinance 02026-21 approving the City of Duluth FY27 budget as
presented.

Voted For: Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings

City's Unified Development Code Article 2, Table 2-C (Use of Land and Structures
Table).

3

[page 4]

Margie Pozin, Director of Community Development and Engineering, came forward
to present and explained that the applicant is requesting the ability to apply for a
special use permit to operate a medical office in the M-1 (Light Industrial) zoning
district. Currently, this use is neither allowed by right nor by special use.
Allowing a use via "special use permit" allows neighbors to weigh in at a public
hearing, allows staff to review surrounding land uses, and allows council to place
conditions on such uses if they are found to be appropriate.
Ms. Pozin outlined the criteria that must be considered for this type of application,
and noted that the proposed amendment should be compatible with the purpose
and intent of the Comprehensive Plan, promote the public health, safety, or general
welfare, encourage the most appropriate use of land, buildings, and other structures
throughout the City of Duluth, and align with purpose and intent of the
Comprehensive Plan. Staff and the Planning Commission have reviewed and
recommended approval.
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council. Being none, the Mayor called for
questions/comments from the public.
There being no comments or questions, Mayor Whitlock closed the public hearing
and called for a motion.
A motion was made by Councilmember Cummings, seconded by Councilmember
Graeder, to approve ordinance 02026-22 to amend the Unified Development Code
as presented.
Voted For: Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings
Motion carried.

3. ORDINANCE OF SPECIAL USE- CASE SU2026-001 {F}
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider granting a special use permit
for 4319 Abbotts Bridge Road, Building 3, Suite 5 (Parcel ID R6324 249) to allow fora
med spa/medical office.

Margie Pozin, Community Development/Engineering Director presented. Based on
approval of O2026-22, Owner/Applicant, Rosibel Gonzalez Carpinone of Rand H
General Services, LLC is requesting a special use permit.
The subject property totals +/- 4.5 ACRES (Suite square footage: 1875 sf) and is split
zoned M-1 (Light Industrial District) and C-2 (General Business District). The subject
property is located in the River Green Employment District, and FORWARDuluth
envisions this Character Area to be an economic engine for the city, serving as a major
regional distribution and office hub with Commercial/ Retail/Office use.
Ms. Pozin reported the staff findings on reviewing this application. There are a wide
variety of uses on the subject property; each of the three buildings has six suites and
many of the suites are combined. The various uses include a sign company, salon and
4

spa, two bakeries, jerky retail, art studio, dance studio, dentist, cake shop and an
engineer and contracting firm. The entire property has 136 parking spaces, and the
medical office would require 9 of them. Medical Offices and Med Spas are under the
same NAICS (North American Industry Classification System), which is 621. The Med
Spa, if approved, would have office hours as follows: 9:00 am — 6:00 pm Monday —
Saturday. Some of the services they offer are Weight Loss, IV Therapy, Facials, Botox,
Microneedling etc. Ms. Pozin outlined the general conditions.
The Planning Commission heard this case at the May 4, 2026 meeting and
recommended approval (pending the approval of case TA2026-003.) Staff also
recommended approval of this item.
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council. Being none, the Mayor called the
applicant forward.
Henry Leo and Rosibel Gonzalez of 715 Babbling Creek Place, Alpharetta Georgia
30022 came forward to say that their proposal is to allow a small-scale outpatient
medical office and operate by appointment only, similar to a professional office,
performing services under a supervising physician offering services such as IV
therapies, and professional skin care retail products and services. They requested
Council support.

further comments or questions, Mayor Whitlock closed the public hearing and called
for a motion.

SU2026-001 with conditions as presented.

4. ORDINANCE OF REZONING - CASE Z2026-002 {G}
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider a rezoning request for 3639
Rogers Bridge Road (PIN R7203 045) from O-! (Office Institutional District) to R-100
(Single Family Residential District) to allow for the construction of a single family
home.
Community Development/Engineering Director Margie Pozin presented. Owner, Cecil
Eugene Tucker and Applicant, Altamirano Ramos are requesting rezoning of property
totaling +/- 52 ACRES. She showed the map location and described the surrounding
parcels, and explained that the subject property is in the Established Neighborhood
District. FORWARDuluth envisions this Character Area to continue to be the
backbone of Duluth’s residential community. The Future Land Use Map (FLUM)
envisions the uses to be Commercial/Retail/Office.
5

[page 6]

June 8, 2026

Ms. Pozin said the uses for O-| (Office-institutional District) would be extremely
limiting for such a small parcel. To fit in a building with the required parking would be
difficult. Staff finds that downzoning the property to residential would be a better fit
for this parcel. Although the request was made for R-100, the lot is only 75’ wide. The
more appropriate zoning would be R-50 (Single-Family Residential), which requires a
50’ wide lot. Ms. Pozin then described the general conditions.
Planning Commission heard this case at the May 4, 2026 meeting and recommended
approval of the R-50 zoning district (over the R-100 zoning district) with concurrence
from the owner and applicant, as R-50 will allow for more flexibility in designing and
building the new home. Staff also recommends approval of this item.
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council. Being none, the Mayor called the
applicant forward.
Applicant Juan Altamirano Ramos came forward and requested approval.
Mayor Whitlock called for questions/comments from the public. There being no
further comments or questions, Mayor Whitlock closed the public hearing and called
for a motion.

Z2026-002 as presented.

Hall roof.

original to the building and circa 2007. Accordingly, staff published a Request for
Proposal (RFP) for replacement. Staff received seven proposals and following an
evaluation by an outside consultant, staff is recommending that the contract be
awarded to Cotton Commercial USA, Inc, in the amount of $ 98,714.79. Given the
complexity of the roof, staff is also recommending a 15% contingency be added for a

Public Works Director Audrey Turner reported that over 500 cars came through the

which includes processing late notices, returned mail investigation, cross checks 
with the Gwinnett County' s Tax Assessors' real and personal property tax files, City
