Police Vehicles - Consolidated Vehicle Maintenance - Vehicles line item, including 
associated transfers. 
 
3. ACCEPT GRANT/ORD TO AMEND BUDGET - $319,771.07 – LMIG 
 
As discussed at the February 2nd work session, staff presented a grant the City 
received $319,771.07 from the Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT) 
representing the City's share of the 2026 LMIG (Local Maintenance Improvement 
Grant). LMIG funds are generated from the state motor fuel tax and are to be used 
for road improvements such as resurfacing. Approval of this item approves 
ordinance BA-FY26-28 to add $319,771.07 in 2026 LMIG funds to the GDOT State 
Grant line item and a like amount to the Transportation/Infrastructure 
Improvements -Paved Streets - Repairs & Maintenance - Streets/Sidewalks line 
item. 
 
4. ORDINANCE TO AMEND BUDGET - $50,000 – LANDSCAPING 
 
At the February 2 work session, staff presented a proposal for landscaping 
improvements near the intersection of Pleasant Hill Road and Peachtree 
Industrial Boulevard. The improvements would also include an area near 
Peachtree Industrial Boulevard and North Berkeley Lake Road. Funding of 
$50,000 for this project would come from 2017 SPLOST Transportation funds. 
Approval of this item authorizes ordinance BA-FY26-29 to add 2017 SPLOST 
Transportation funds of $50,000 to Landscape Median - Paved Streets - 
Infrastructure line item, including associated transfers. 
 
5. ORDINANCE TO AMEND BUDGET - $56,030 – PARKING SIGNAGE 
 
At the February work session, staff presented a proposal for converting the 
existing parking signage in downtown to the traditional blue, with the capital "P" 
designation, installing additional parking and pedestrian directional signage in 
strategic locations. Staff received a proposal for $56,030 from Image 
Manufacturing Group to fabricate and install the signage. Funding for the project 
will come from the Rental Motor Vehicle Tax Fund. Approval of this item 
authorizes ordinance BA-FY26-30 to amend the FY26 budget to add $56,030 in 
prior year reserves to Rental Motor Vehicle Tax Fund - Downtown Development - 
Signs/Banners line item. 
 
6. ORDINANCE TO AMEND BUDGET - $680,000 – TRANSPORTATION 
 
At the February Council work session, staff requested council consider adding 
$680,000 in 2023 SPLOST funds to the capital project fund Transportation/ 
Infrastructure Improvements to cover the cost of small one-off projects that do 
not meet the Purchasing Policy requirements for the formal bidding process and 
budget amendment, but nevertheless have budget impact. Approval of this item 
authorizes ordinance BA-FY26-31 to amend the FY26 budget by adding $680,000 
in 2023 SPLOST Transportation funds to Transportation/ Infrastructure

1. TEXT AMENDMENT ORDINANCE – CASE TA2026-001 
 
 
Mayor and Council to consider an ordinance adjusting the City's Unified 
Development Code Article 2, Table 2-C (Use of Land and Structures Table). This 
table lists principal uses allowed by zoning district. Staff is requesting 
modification for "Parking Lots and Garages" to be allowed by special use in the C-2 

M&C Pub Agenda 
February 9, 2026 
Page 6 of 9 
 
6 
(General Business), HC-R (Highway Commercial - Retail), and HC-A (Highway 
Commercial - Auto) zoning districts. They are currently shown as allowed by right, 
however, a parking lot or garage is considered an accessory use, not a principal 
use, under most circumstances. Staff would like to clarify this in the code by 
offering this use by way of special use permit allowing for a process to review each 
location for which a garage or parking lot is proposed as the principal use. This 
would also allow for conditions to be placed on such uses if they are found to be 
appropriate. 
 
2. TEXT AMENDMENT ORDINANCE – CASE TA 2026-002 
 
 
Mayor and Council to consider an ordinance adjusting the City's permit fee 
schedule to remove the fee for right of way utility permits. This fee was added in 
September of 2025 at staff's request, to cover the cost of the City's Engineer's 
review time. Staff has since learned that most utilities operate under franchise 
agreements that prohibit the utilities from paying this additional fee. The few 
applications that would pay the $100 fee would not cover the additional staff time 
to collect it and route the plans to and from review.

5. BID AWARD - BUNTEN RD PARK IMPROVEMENTS 
 
 
Mayor and Council to consider award of a contract for construction of the Bunten 
Road Park Improvements Project. On December 10, 2025, the project was 
advertised to contractors. On January 22, 2026, three sealed proposal packages 
were received. Evaluations were completed based on criteria listed in the request 
for proposals. 
 
Upon initial administrative inspection, one of the packages had errors and was 
disqualified from further evaluation. The remaining two packages were evaluated 
by four staff members (two from Parks, and two from Community Development 
and Engineering) with scores being totaled and averaged as listed below: 
 
IP Construction - Disqualified 
Tri-Scapes - 78.5 points (Base bid listed as $5,468,099.94) 
Ohmshiv Construction - 61 points (Base bid listed as $5,568,546.15)

contract documents. The difference between the bids remains at less than 2%. 
 
Staff recommends award of the construction contract for the Bunten Road Park 
Improvements Project to Tri-Scapes in the corrected amount of $5,505,197.54. Two

from the scope of the contractor's work. Staff has determined the best path

Page 5 of 7 
 
5
 
This grant requires the partnership of three unique entities - a climate adaptation 
practitioner, a community partner, and a local government. 
 
The "lead applicant" which in this case is the climate adaptation practitioner, is the 
recipient of the grant, though some of the funds will pass through the community 
partner and the local government. The City will work with the climate adaptation 
practitioner and the community partner, which at this time we believe will be the 
Chattahoochee River Keepers, to apply for the grant and if awarded, will work with the 
same partners to develop a climate resilient stormwater master plan. We believe this 
effort will need to be done in at least two phases under separate projects to cover the 
two major drainage basins that Duluth covers. With the River Keepers on our team, we 
believe the Chattahoochee Basin will be the first to be master planned. Depending on 
the size of the grant award, the City may opt to scope by subbasins (smaller than basins) 
to avoid outspending the budget. 
 
Ms. Pozin said the typical award is between $90k and $110k. The City is going to pursue 
$110, and then the practitioner will assist to determine a scope that can be reasonably 
achieved regarding number of sub basins, perhaps several that can be incorporated into 
a master plan. Once there is a formal plan, it can be used to pursue additional and larger 
grants to help us implement other projects. There is no match requirement for this 
particular grant, but in order to get to a logical scope additional funds have been 
identified from the stormwater budget if we receive the grant and have to increase the 
scope for any reason. 
 
In summary, having a Stormwater Master Plan will set the City up for more success with 
future grant applications, and allow the City to better prioritize funding. Staff is 
requesting Council consider support of this grant and allow the Mayor or City Manager to 
sign a letter of commitment to be included with the grant application. 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Park, seconded by Councilmember Thomas, 
to approve Council's support of this grant application and authorize the City 
Manager or Mayor to sign a letter of commitment for the Climate Smart 
Communities Initiative Grant as presented.

EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT 
 
THIS AGREEMENT, made and entered into this 9th day of February 2026, by and between the City of 
Duluth, GA, a municipal corporation, hereinafter called "Employer," as party of the first part, and James 
Riker hereinafter "Employee" as party of the second part, both of whom understand as follows: 
 
WITNESSETH: 
 
WHEREAS, the Employee is currently under contract to serve as the City Manager for the City of Duluth 
through December 31, 2026; and 
 
WHEREAS, the parties desire to amend the terms of the current employment agreement to extend the 
number of months of severance to be paid; and 
 
WHEREAS: Employer desires to continue to employ the services of James Riker as City Manager of the 
City of Duluth, as provided by the charter; and 
 
WHEREAS, it is the desire of the governing board, hereinafter called "Council," to provide certain 
benefits, to establish certain conditions of employment, and to set working conditions of said Employee; 
and 
 
WHEREAS Employee desires to continue his employment as City Manager of said City of Duluth under the 
terms and conditions set forth in this agreement; and 
 
NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein contained, the parties agree as 
follows: 
 
Section 1: Duties 
 
Employer hereby agrees to continue to employ James Riker as City Manager of said Employer to perform 
the functions and duties specified in said City of Duluth Charter and by said City of Duluth Code of 
Ordinances and to perform other legally permissible and proper duties and functions as the Council shall 
from time-to-time assign. Further, Employee agrees that he shall take all necessary steps and diligently 
pursue an ICMA Credentialed Manager Certification without delay or interruption. 
 
Section 2: Term 
 
A. Employee agrees to remain in the exclusive employ of Employer until December 31, 2026, and neither 
to accept other employment nor to become employed by any other employer until said termination 
date, unless said termination date is affected as hereinafter provided. 
 
B. In the event written notice is not given by either party to this agreement to the other 90 days prior to 
the termination date as hereinabove provided, this agreement shall be extended on the same terms and 
conditions as herein provided, all for an additional period of one year. Said agreement shall continue 
thereafter for a one-year period unless either party hereto gives 90 days written notice to the other 
party that the party does not wish to extend this agreement for an additional one-year term. 
 
C. Nothing in this agreement shall prevent, limit, or otherwise interfere with the right of the Council to 
terminate the services of Employee at any time, subject only to the provisions set forth in Section 3, 
paragraphs A and B, of this agreement. 

Employment Agreement 
Page 2 of 8 
 
 
D. Nothing in this agreement shall prevent, limit, or otherwise interfere with the right of the Employee 
to resign at any time from his position with the Employer, subject only to the provision set forth in 
Section 4 of this agreement. 
 
Section 3: Termination and Severance Pay 
 
A. In the event the Employee is terminated by the Council during such time that the Employee is willing 
and able to perform his/her duties under this agreement, then the Employee is entitled to termination 
pay of twelve months of the Employee's salary. Any termination pay earned in accordance with the 
provisions of this section shall be in addition to any other accrued or guaranteed benefits which the 
Employee maybe entitled under the personnel policies of the City or the laws of the State of Georgia or 
the United States of America; however, the official shall not gain or accrue any additional benefits as a 
result of the termination pay provided to the employee. 
 
B. The Employee shall be entitled to termination pay if he is terminated by the Mayor and Council for 
any reason other than arrest and/or conviction of a crime or for professional misconduct. For purposes 
of this article, the term "professional misconduct" shall include but not be limited to the following 
offenses: Willful disregard of an express directive of the City Council and/or refusal to obey reasonable 
orders of the City Council; willful neglect of duties; inappropriate or illegal harassment of City 
employees; or actions involving fraud or dishonesty. The Employee shall also be entitled to termination 
pay should he resign following a request by a majority of the City Council that a resignation be tendered 
in lieu of termination for a reason other than arrest or conviction of a crime or for professional 
misconduct. The Employee shall not be entitled to termination pay as described in this section upon 
voluntary resignation of his position. (Ord. Of 11-11-97) 
 
C. If Employee is terminated, Employer agrees to provide for out placement services to Employee at its 
expense, should Employee desire them, in an amount not to exceed a total of $2,500. 
 
Section 4: Resignation 
 
In the event Employee voluntarily resigns, his position with the Employer before expiration of the 
aforesaid term of his employment, then Employee shall give Employer 90 days' notice in advance, unless 
the parties agree otherwise. 
 
Section 5: Disability 
 
If Employee is permanently disabled or is otherwise unable to perform the essential functions of the job 
because of sickness, accident, injury, mental incapacity, or health for a period of four successive weeks 
beyond any accrued sick leave, Employer shall have the option to terminate this agreement, subject to 
the severance pay requirements of Section 3, paragraph A. 

Employment Agreement 
Page 3 of 8 
 
 
Section 6: Salary and Compensation 
 
Employer agrees to pay Employee an annual base salary of $244,538.58, effective with the January 1, 
2026, payroll start date. Employee salary shall be payable in installments at the same time as other 
management employees of the Employer are paid. In addition, Employer agrees to increase said base 
salary annually, consistent with any cost-of-living increase provided to all other City employees. 
Notwithstanding the foregoing, Employer may increase Employee's base salary and/or benefits of 
Employee in such amounts and to such extent as the Council may determine that is desirable to do so on 
the basis of an annual salary review of said Employee conducted prior to the end of each fiscal year. 
 
Section 7: Performance Evaluation 
 
A. The Mayor and Council shall confer with the Employee on at least an annual basis regarding job 
performance and compensation. The Mayor and Council shall provide the Employee with a written job 
evaluation at least once per fiscal year and may conduct periodic interim reviews; shall conduct a salary 
review prior to the end of each fiscal year; and shall determine whether any adjustment of the 
compensation and benefits provided for the City Manager should be made for the next fiscal year. 
 
B. Annually, at a strategic planning session, the Council and Employee shall define such goals and 
performance objectives that they determine necessary for the proper operation of the City of Duluth 
and in the attainment of the Council's policy objectives and shall further establish a relative priority 
among those various goals and objectives, said goals and objectives to be reduced to writing. They shall 
generally be attainable within the time limitations as specified and the annual operating and capital 
budgets and appropriations provided. Should the goals, objectives, or their relative priority be unclear to 
the Employee, it is his obligation to inform the Council, in writing, of any specific area(s) that 
necessitate clarification. 
 
C. In effecting the provisions of this section, the Council and Employee mutually agree to abide by 
the provisions of applicable law. 
 
Section 8: Hours of Work 
 
It is recognized that the Employee must devote a great deal of time outside the normal office hours to 
the business of the Employer, and to that end, Employee will be allowed to take compensatory time off 
as he shall deem appropriate during normal office hours. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Employment Agreement 
Page 4 of 8 
 
 
Section 9: Outside Activities 
 
Employee shall not spend more than 10 hours per week in teaching, consulting, or other non-Employer-
connected business without the prior approval of the Council. 
 
Section 10: Automobile 
 
Employee's duties require use of an automobile at all times during his employment with Employer. The 
Employee shall have access to a City car for use during regular business hours. In addition, Employer 
shall pay a car allowance to Employee for a personal vehicle in the amount of $550.00 per pay period, 
effective January 1, 2026. 
 
 
 
 Section 11: Vacation and Sick Leave 
 
As an inducement to Employee to continue employment as City Manager, at signature hereof, Employee 
shall have credited to his personal account four weeks of vacation leave. On January 1st of each year 
thereafter, Employee shall have credited to his personal account four weeks of vacation leave. 
Employee's sick leave shall accrue at the same rate as other general management employees of 
Employer. 
 
 Section 12: Disability, Health, and Life Insurance 
 
Employee shall receive the same benefits as all other general management employees of the City. 
These benefits include, but are not limited to, medical insurance, dental insurance, short-term disability 
insurance, long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and 457b Plan with limited matching 
contributions by the City. 
 
Section 13: Dues and Subscriptions 
 
Employer agrees to budget for and to pay for professional dues and subscriptions of Employee 
necessary for his continuation and full participation in national, regional, state, and local associations 
and organizations necessary and desirable for his continued professional participation, growth, and 
advancement, and for the good of the employer. 
 
Section 14: Professional Development 
 
A. Employer hereby agrees to budget for and to pay for travel and subsistence expenses of Employee 
according to the City's travel policy as it applies to all management employees for professional and 
official travel and meetings, and occasions adequate to continue the professional development of 
Employee and to adequately pursue necessary official functions for Employer, including, but not limited 
to, the Georgia Municipal Association, ICMA Annual Conference, the American Planning Association and 
such other national, regional, state, and local governmental groups and committees thereof which 
Employee serves as a member. 
 
B. Employer also agrees to budget for and to pay for travel and subsistence expenses of Employee for 
short courses, institutes, and seminars that are necessary for his professional development and for the 
good of the Employer. 

Employment Agreement 
Page 5 of 8 
 
 
 
Section 15: Civic Club Membership 
 
Employer recognizes the desirability of representation in and before local civic and other organizations, 
and Employee is authorized to become a member of anyone (1) such civic clubs or organizations subject 
to the approval of the City Council, for which Employer shall pay all expenses. Employee shall report to 
the Employer on each membership that he has taken out at Employer's expense. 
 
 
Section 16: Indemnification 
 
The City will provide errors and omissions insurance coverage for the Employee at the same level as that 
provided for elected officials and other management level employees and subject to the same 
conditions and exclusions. 
 
Section 17: Bonding 
 
Employer shall bear the full cost of any fidelity or other bonds required of the employee under any law 
or ordinance. 
 
Section 18: Other Terms and Conditions of Employment 
 
A. The Council, in consultation with the City Manager, shall fix any such other terms and conditions of 
employment, as it may determine from time to time, relating to the Performance of Employee, provided 
such terms and conditions are not inconsistent with or in conflict with the provisions of this agreement, 
the City of Duluth Charter or any other law. 
 
B. All provisions of the City of Duluth Charter and Code, and regulations and rules of the Employer 
relating to vacation and sick leave, retirement and pension system contributions, holidays, and other 
benefits and working conditions as they now exist or hereafter maybe amended, also shall apply to 
Employee as they would to other employees of Employer, in addition to said benefits enumerated 
specifically for the benefit of Employee except as herein provided. 
 
C. Employee shall be entitled to receive the same vacation and sick leave benefits as are accorded 
department heads, including provisions governing accrual and payment therefor on termination of 
employment.

Section 19: No Reduction of Benefits. 
 
Employer shall not at any time during the term of this agreement reduce the salary, compensation, or 
other financial benefits of Employee, except to the degree of such a reduction across-the-board for all 
employees of the employer. 
 
Section 20: Notices 
 
Notices pursuant to this agreement shall be given by deposit in the custody of the United States Postal 
Service, postage prepaid, as follows: Employer: Attn: Asst. City Manager/City Clerk, City of Duluth, 3167 
Main Street, Duluth, GA 30096. Employee: Attn: James Riker, or via hand delivery. 
 
 
Section 21: General Provisions 
 
A. The text herein shall constitute the entire agreement between the parties. 
 
B. This agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the heirs at law and executors 
of Employee. 
 
C. This agreement shall become effective commencing January 1, 2026. 
 
D. If any provision, or any portion thereof, contained in this agreement is held unconstitutional, invalid,

Background: 
 
Since the readoption of the Unified Development Code (UDC) on September 8, 2025, Staff have 
continued to review the document for improvement. This is a living document that staff use daily. 
Recently, staff noticed the land use labeled as “Parking Lots and Garages” is currently allowed by 
right in the C-2 (General Business), HC-R (Highway Commercial-Retail) and HC-A (Highway 
Commercial-Auto) zoning districts. While parking facilities are inherent to the uses commonly 
found in these zoning districts, staff do not believe the intent of the UDC was to allow parking 
facilities to exist as the principal use. Therefore, staff are requesting these uses be revised to be 
permitted as a special use (rezoning required) to allow them under special circumstances when and 
where appropriate.

location of parking relative to the principal building. There are no direct references in the UDC to 
parking being a principal use, other than in Table 2-C. This proposed text amendment will remove 
ambiguity.

I. 
Background: 
 
In September of 2025, Mayor and Council voted to approve a revision to the City’s Fee Schedule to 
allow a $100 fee to be assessed for review of utility permits also known as Right of Way 
registrations. This was in an effort to recover the cost of the City’s Engineer’s time, which is paid on 
contract. The City Engineer reviews utility installations, adjustments, and additions for utility work 
within the right-of-way. 
 
To charge the fee, staff set up an option through our permitting software that would be registrants 
would access in order to upload their plans. 
 
Once staff put this assessment into practice, it was discovered that most of the utilities operating 
within our right of way do so under franchise agreements which preclude the payment of additional 
permit or review fees. And adding the steps necessary to collect a fee from the very few utilities 
who would pay it made the overall process longer and less efficient. 
 
Staff is recommending removing the fee for new installations, adjustments, and additions to utilities 
in the right-of-way and going back to the simpler process involving fewer individuals.

Sec. 8-66. General regulations. 
a. The chief of police or his designee or the city manager or designee is hereby

TRAFFIC 
CALMING 
PROGRAM
February 2026

AGENDA
What is traffic calming?
When is traffic calming effective?
What options exist?
Process / Cost? How is it funded?
How might we prioritize requests for traffic 
calming?
Next steps

WHAT IS TRAFFIC CALMING?
Systematic improvements to safety of roadways for 
all users with self-enforcing physical measures
Not just vehicular traffic, but all forms of Traffic: 
Pedestrians, Bikes, and Vehicles
Not a “One size fits all” solution
Often requires multiple speed-appropriate measures 
to provide the most effective solution
Frequently there is a perceived speeding problem

WHEN IS 
TRAFFIC 
CALMING 
EFFECTIVE?
Reduce speeding
Reduce cut-through traffic
Reduce the severity of accidents
Increase access for all modes of 
transportation
Self-enforcing

Higher speed facilities may not be intended for bicycle and pedestrian usage (like an interstate). 
Whereas the roads in a CBD should encourage cyclists and pedestrians through ped friendly design, 
sidewalk availability, and lower speed limits.
Speed limits are typically dictated by land use. Land use is a good indication of how many modes of 
transportation will be utilized and how many pedestrians may be generated in a given corridor. 

WHAT OPTIONS EXIST?
Changing the driver’s horizonal alignment 
(horizontal deflection)
Changing the driver’s vertical alignment (vertical 
deflection)
Reducing street width (“shy line” perception)
Routing restriction (physical turn prohibitions, etc)
IN COMBINATION WITH…
Signage & Pavement Markings
Corner Radius Reduction (forces slower speeds)
Streetscaping / Landscaping

PROCESS / COST?
Situationally dependent & data driven
Start with an investigation to confirm the facts – this may be an up-front cost 
of up to $2500
Determine if location is a candidate for traffic calming measures
If so, applicant to seek and submit petition including support from property 
owners along the subject street
If supported, develop location specific solutions – may require additional 
traffic studies. (Need to define “support”. Is it is based on a tiered system?)
Determine cost based on preferred solutions
Set aside a certain amount of SPLOST budget to cover this program? 
Possible grants for safety improvements?

HOW DO WE PRIORITIZE REQUESTS?
Requests have come in from 19 neighborhoods 
(over time)
Through the Mayor and Council’s 2025 outreach, 
citizens have indicated a desire for traffic calming
Need a strategy for prioritizing the requests, AND
Need funding sources to cover initial investigations 
and follow up projects
First - initial investigations for each request to 
determine extent of need
Staff will create a form (in advance) for citizen 
requests
Then – prioritize based on initial investigation(s)

STRATEGIES FOR PRIORITIZING 
REQUESTS – PHASED APPROACH
• Initial site visit to investigate/determine 
unique circumstances
• Safety concerns, type/history
• Historical context from PD (accident 
history/patterns, other citation 
information)
• Initial data collection to determine 
volumes and speeds

STRATEGIES FOR PRIORITIZING 
REQUESTS – PHASED APPROACH
Once a determination has been made that 
improvements are warranted and once a petition in 
support of improvements has been received and 
verified:
Develop context specific concept plan and 
concept level cost estimate (this task will have a 
cost to it, which will vary based on complexity)
Add project to a traffic calming program list to 
await funding. Funding will need to cover 
design, possible right of way acquisition, 
construction, and post construction studies.

STRATEGIES FOR PRIORITIZING REQUESTS – 
PHASED APPROACH
Once on the project list, projects could be released 
for design and construction based on the following:
Severity of existing conditions
Average Daily traffic (ADT)
Cost and availability of funds
Number of properties served by the improvements 
(as listed on the petition). This is called the 
“service area”.

NEXT STEPS
Council to shape and approve the policy – staff 
requires feedback
Council to set aside budget
Staff can then engage with list of citizens making 
requests and start the investigations
Staff to prioritize the requests based on finding of 
facts and petitions received
Staff to move forward with projects on the list as 
funding is available

QUESTIONS?

1. TEXT AMENDMENT ORDINANCE - CASE TA2026-001 {J}
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider an ordinance adjusting the
City's Unified Development Code Article 2, Table 2-C (Use of Land and Structures
Table).
Community Development/Engineering Director Margie Pozin came forward to
explain the request. She stated that Table 2-C lists principal uses allowed by zoning
district. Staff is requesting modification for "Parking Lots and Garages" to be allowed
by special use in the C-2 (General Business), HC-R (Highway Commercial - Retail), and
HC-A (Highway Commercial - Auto) zoning districts. They are currently shown as
allowed by right, however, a parking lot or garage is considered an accessory use, not
a principal use, under most circumstances. Staff proposed offering this use by way of
special use permit allowing for a process to review each location for which a garage or
parking lot is proposed as the principal use. This would also allow conditions to be
placed on such uses if they are found to be appropriate.
The language in the code itself refers to type and location of parking relative toa
principal building; the text amendment will remove the ambiguity between the chart
and the text. Planning Commission heard this at their February meeting and
recommended approval.

support.

4. ORDINANCE TO AMEND DULUTH CODE - DOWNTOWN PARKING {P}
Economic Development Director Chris McGahee came forward to summarize the
request. Approval of this item approves ordinance 02026-06 to amend section 8-67 of
the Duluth Code of Ordinances relating to adding new parking spaces, removing no
longer used parking spaces, directional parking, handicapped parking and parking
duration in public spaces. Approval also updates the parking map associated with the
ordinance.

He explained that the 48 hour parking presents an opportunity to allow people who
live and work downtown to use the spaces, but not to be used as storage areas for
extra vehicles or by companies that just leave their vehicles parked downtown. The 15-
minute parking is for basically dropping off and loading for the businesses who need
their items brought in daily. And then three-hour parking is to deal with the turnover
of the high-volume areas where people should come in, do their business, and then
leave those spaces, allowing others to come in and support our businesses
downtown.
Councilmember Cummings asked about the time and date restrictions.
Mr. McGahee responded that 15-minute parking areas are permanently designated as
such. The three-hour parking will be enforced from 6:30 until 3:00 each day. The 48-
hour parking would also be constant.

ENCROACHMENT AND USE OF CITY PROPERTY 
IN THE CITY OF DULUTH, 
GWINNETT COUNTY, GEORGIA 
 
THIS AGREEMENT (“Agreement”) is made, entered into and effective this _____ day 
of ___________, 2026, by and among the City of Duluth, a Georgia municipal corporation 
(hereafter referred to as “City”) and Knox House Holding, LLC, a Georgia limited liability 
company(hereafter “User”). 
Subject to the terms and conditions hereafter stated and based on the representations, 
warranties, covenants, agreements and recitals of the parties herein contained, the parties do hereby 
agree as follows: 
ARTICLE 1 
DEFINITIONS 
1.1 
Terms. The following terms, unless elsewhere specifically defined herein, shall 
have the following meanings as set forth below. 
1.2 
City. “City” means the City of Duluth, a Georgia municipal corporation. 
1.3 
User. “User” means Knox House Holding, LLC, a Georgia limited liability 
company, and their successors and assigns in interest with respect to the Encroachment Property. 
1.4 
User Property. User Property means the following real property: 
All property identified in Exhibit “A” attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference 
as “Knox House Holding, LLC” property. 
1.5 
Encroachment Property. “Encroachment Property” means that certain real 
property identified as “Easement Area” in that certain survey (the “Survey”) for Kenneth Smith, 
dated September 16, 2024, as amended September 26, 2024, by Land Surveying and Planning, 
Douglas R. Sherrill (GRLS# 2995), for real property located in Land Lot 293, 6th District, City of 
Duluth, Gwinnett County, Georgia, said Survey attached hereto as Exhibit “A” and incorporated 
herein by reference. 
1.6 
User Improvements. “User Improvements” means a deck and steps extending 
from the Encroachment Property to City Property for the purposes to provide access to and from 
the User Property and City Property. 
1.7 
City Property. City Property means the following real property: 
All property identified in Exhibit “A” attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference 
as “City of Duluth” property and the “Easement Area”. 
1.8 
Survey of Encroachments. “Survey of Encroachments” means the survey 
attached hereto and incorporated herein as Exhibit “A”. 

 
2 
ARTICLE 2 
RECITALS 
 
Recital No. 1. City owns the Encroachment Property. 
Recital No. 2. The User Property is being developed and improved by the User by 
constructing an extension of its existing deck onto and through the Encroachment Property, and 
adding steps to join said deck with City Property greenspace. Whereby, User requires the 
Encroachment Property for the furtherance and completion of its intended use of the User Property. 
Recital No. 3. The City for good and valuable consideration hereby grants and conveys 
to the User, Its successors and assigns, a perpetual non-exclusive encroachment and use easement 
(the “Easement”) within the Encroachment Property for the purposes and uses as stated herein. 
ARTICLE 3 
AGREEMENTS 
3.1 
Construction And Maintenance Of User Improvements. Under the terms and 
conditions stated herein, User, at its own cost, is hereby granted the Easement as authorized by the 
City to permit the User Improvements to be constructed and to remain in the Encroachment 
Property, subject to the terms and conditions as stated herein. The User Improvements allowed 
shall consist of the extension of an existing deck from the User Property through the Encroachment 
Property along with steps from said deck to existing City Property greenspace. 
3.2 
City Not Responsible For User Improvements. Nothing contained herein shall 
be deemed an assumption by the City of any responsibility for construction, maintenance, 
replacement or repair of the User Improvements. 
3.3 
Continuing Right To City Easement. Nothing contained herein shall be deemed 
a waiver or abandonment or transfer of the right, title and interest that the City holds to the City 
Property identified as the Easement Area in Exhibit “A”. 
3.4 
Subordinate Position Of User Improvements. The User Improvements are 
subordinate to the rights of the City in the Encroachment Property and on all City Property. 
3.5 
Risk Of Loss. User and the City understand and agree that the User Improvements 
may be adversely affected by damage caused to User Improvements arising out of the User’s 
and/or its invitees use of the Encroachment Property. The parties agree that the City is not 
responsible for such events; and the City shall have no liability to User or its invitees for such 
events, and the User assumes the risk of installing the User Improvements in the Encroachment 
Property. 
3.6 
User To Bear Cost Of Relocating User Improvements. The User is responsible 
for the repair and maintenance of the User Improvements in the Encroachment Property. 
If the User does not perform such tasks, the City may perform such tasks and in such case 
the User shall reimburse the City for the City’s costs and expenses. Prior to commencing such 
tasks, the City shall send a notice to the User and allow the User twenty (20) days from the date of 

 
3 
the written notice to perform the tasks. If the User has not completed the work within the twenty 
(20) days, then the City may proceed to perform the tasks. Once the City’s reasonable costs and 
expenses incurred have been determined by the City, the City shall send an invoice for such costs 
and expenses to the User. The User must pay the invoice within thirty (30) days after the date of 
the invoice. Such costs and expenses include, but are not limited to, costs charged the City by third 
parties such as contractors as well as the costs for City personnel that may have performed the 
work. Bills not paid shall incur the standard penalty and interest established by the City for utility 
billings within the City. 
3.7 
Emergency. Notwithstanding the requirements contained in Sections 3.6 relating 
to a twenty (20) day written notice to the User to perform its obligations under Sections 3.6, the 
City shall not be required to give such notice if the City’s engineer determines that an emergency 
exists. In such instance, the City, without giving notice to the User may perform the work and in 
such case the User shall reimburse the City for the costs and expenses relating to the work. Once 
the City’s costs and expenses have been determined by the City, the City shall send an invoice for 
such costs and expenses to the User. The User must pay the invoice within thirty (30) days after 
the date of the invoice. Such costs and expenses include, but are not limited to, costs charged the 
City by third parties such as contractors as well as the costs for City personnel that may have 
performed the work. Bills not paid shall incur the standard penalty and interest established by the 
City for utility bills within the City. The charges shall be divided equally among the Encroachment 
Property. 
3.8 
Remedies. If the User fails to perform its obligations under this Agreement, then 
the City may avail itself of any remedy afforded by law or in equity and any of the following non-
exclusive remedies: 
(a) 
The City may specifically enforce this Agreement. 
(b) 
If User fails to make payments under Section 3.6, or 3.7, then the City may 
certify to Gwinnett County, Georgia the amounts due as payable with the real estate taxes for the 
Encroachment Property in the next calendar year; such certifications may be made under Georgia 
law in a manner similar to certifications for unpaid utility bills. Further, as an alternate means of 
collection, if the written billing is not paid by the User, the City, without notice and without 
hearing, may specially assess the Encroachment Property for the costs and expenses incurred by 
the City. The User hereby waives any and all procedural and substantive objections to special 
assessments for the costs including, but not limited to, notice and hearing requirements and any 
claims that the charges or special assessments exceed the benefit to the Encroachment Property. 
No remedy herein conferred upon or reserved to the City shall be exclusive of any other 
available remedy or remedies, but each and every such remedy shall be cumulative and shall be in 
addition to every other remedy given under this Agreement or now or hereafter existing at law or 
in equity or by statute. No delay or omission to exercise any right or power accruing upon any 
default shall impair any such right or power or shall be construed to be a waiver thereof, but any 
such right and power may be exercised from time to time and as often as may be deemed expedient. 
3.9 
Indemnification. The User shall indemnify, defend and hold the City, its council, 
agents, consultants, attorneys, employees and representatives harmless against and in respect of 

 
4 
any and all claims, demands, actions, suits, proceedings, losses, costs, expenses, obligations, 
liabilities, damages, recoveries, and deficiencies including interest, penalties and attorneys’ fees, 
that the City incurs or suffers, which arise out of, result from or relate to any of the following: 
(a) 
The User Improvements; 
(b) 
Installation and maintenance of the Users Improvements; 
(c) 
Failure by the User to observe or perform any covenant, condition, 
obligation or agreement on their part to be observed or performed under this Agreement; and 
(d) 
Use of the User Improvements. 
3.10 City Duties. Nothing contained in this Agreement shall be considered an 
affirmative duty upon the City to perform the User’s obligations contained in Article 3 if the User 
does not perform such obligations. 
3.11 No Third Party Recourse. Third parties shall have no recourse against the City 
under this Agreement. 
3.12 Recording. The User shall record this Agreement with the Clerk of the Gwinnett 
County, Georgia Superior Court and within 30 days after the date of this Agreement, the User shall 
present evidence to the City that this Agreement has been recorded. 
3.13 Binding Agreement. The parties mutually recognize and agree that all terms and 
conditions of this Agreement run with the Encroachment Property shall be covenants running with 
the land and shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the successors, successors-in-title 
and assigns of the parties hereto. 
3.14 Amendment And Waiver. The parties hereto may by mutual written agreement 
amend this Agreement in any respect. Any party hereto may extend the time for the performance 
of any of the obligations of another, waive any inaccuracies in representations by another contained 
in this Agreement or in any document delivered pursuant hereto which inaccuracies would 
otherwise constitute a breach of this Agreement, waive compliance by another with any of the 
covenants contained in this Agreement and performance of any obligations by the other or waive 
the fulfillment of any condition that is precedent to the performance by the party so waiving of any

amendment, extension or waiver must be in writing. No waiver of any of the provisions of this 
Agreement shall be deemed, or shall constitute, a waiver of any other provisions, whether or not 
similar, nor shall any waiver constitute a continuing waiver. 
3.15 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accord 
with the laws of the State of Georgia. 
3.16 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, 
each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which shall constitute one and the same 
instrument.

PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT 
 
 THIS PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) is made between 
the GWINNETT COUNTY WATER AND SEWERAGE AUTHORITY, hereinafter referred 
to as “SELLER”, and the CITY OF DULUTH, a Georgia municipal corporation, hereinafter 
referred to as “PURCHASER”. The Effective Date shall be the date the Agreement is signed by 
the last party signing the Agreement. 
 
WITNESSETH: 
 
The undersigned Purchaser agrees to buy, and the undersigned Seller agrees to sell, all that 
certain tract of land containing 0.59 acres, more or less, and all improvements and dwellings 
located thereon, located at 2407 Main Street, in Land Lot 205, 7th District, Gwinnett County, 
Georgia, being known as Tax Parcel Number R7205 001, the said tract of land and all 
improvements and dwellings located thereon being hereinafter referred to as the “Premises” and 
being more particularly described in Exhibit “A”, a copy of which is attached hereto and hereby 
incorporated by reference as part of this document. 
 
The terms and conditions of this Agreement are as follows: 
 
1. 
PURCHASE PRICE AND TERMS: 
 
 
For and in consideration of the sum of Ten and 00/100 Dollars ($10.00), the mutual 
promises and covenants set forth herein, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt 
and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the Seller agrees to sell the Premises to the 
Purchaser, and the Purchaser agrees to purchase the Premises under the terms and conditions set 
forth herein. The purchase price for the Premises shall be ONE HUNDRED NINETY-FIVE 
THOUSAND AND 00/100 DOLLARS ($195,000.00), which the Purchaser shall pay to Seller at 
Closing. If Seller refuses or cannot convey unencumbered marketable fee simple title to the 
Premises as provided herein, or in the event any condition set forth herein is not met within the 
time provided, such condition not having been waived by Purchaser, then this Contract shall 
terminate. Should Seller refuse to close and Purchaser desires to close, Purchaser shall have the 
right to pursue specific performance as its sole remedy. 
 
2. 
PRORATIONS: 
 
Ad valorem taxes, stormwater fees and other similar charges or fees for the current year, if 
any, shall be prorated as of the date of Closing. 
 
3. 
TRANSFER TAX: 
 
The parties acknowledge that the transfer of the Premises is exempt from State of Georgia 
property transfer tax pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-6-2(a)(3). 
 

2 
4. 
TITLE: 
 
Real Property. Seller agrees to convey good, marketable, and insurable fee simple title to 
the Premises by limited warranty deed. For the purposes of this paragraph, a “good, marketable 
and insurable title” is a title which is insurable by a reputable title insurance company in Atlanta, 
Georgia, at its standard rates without exception other than any Permitted Exceptions agreed to by 
the parties. The Permitted Exceptions shall include the matters set forth on Exhibit “B” which is 
attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. Purchaser shall have one hundred twenty 
(120) days after the date of execution of this Agreement in which to examine title. If Purchaser 
finds any legal defects to title that are unacceptable to the Purchaser, Seller shall be furnished with 
a written statement hereof and shall have thirty (30) days from the date of receipt of said statement 
in which to correct the same. If Seller shall fail to correct or satisfy such legal defects within said 
thirty (30) day period, Purchaser shall have the choice of (a) accepting said Premises with such 
legal defects or (b) declining to accept said Premises with such legal defects, such choice to be 
exercised by written notice to Seller mailed within ten (10) days following the end of the thirty 
(30) day period for correction by Seller of such legal defects. 
 
5. 
WARRANTIES & REPRESENTATIONS: 
 
(a) 
Seller makes the following warranties and representations, all of which shall survive the 
closing, delivery of possession, and recording of the deed 
 
 i) 
Title: Seller warrants that Seller presently has good, insurable and marketable title to said 
Premises and that Seller has the right, power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to sell 
the Premises in accordance with the terms and conditions herein. 
 
 ii) Leases, Contracts: There are no leases, contracts, or other obligations existing with respect 
to the Premises except the Premises is leased by the Seller to Gwinnett County pursuant to a 1985 
Lease, as supplemented. The Seller intends to exclude the Property from the 1985 Lease, as 
supplemented, by executing a 2025 SUPPLEMENTAL LEASE CONTRACT with Gwinnett 
County. This Purchase and Sale Agreement is contingent on Gwinnett County approving and 
signing a 2025 SUPPLEMENTAL LEASE CONTRACT excluding the Property from the 1985 
Lease, as supplemented. 
 
 
 
iii) To the best of the knowledge, information and belief of Seller, no portion of the 
Premises is being used, or in any previous time has been used, as a dump or fill or for the disposal, 
storage, treatment, processing or other handling of hazardous substances and waste. 
 
 
iv) There are no special assessments against or relating to the Property. 
 
 
v) No goods or services have been contracted for or furnished to the Property which might 
give rise to any mechanic’s liens affecting all or any part of the Property. 
 
 
vi) Seller has not entered into any outstanding agreements of sale, leases, options or other 
rights of third parties to acquire an interest in the Property other than disclosed herein. 

 
 
3 
 
vii) Seller shall not further encumber the Property or allow an encumbrance upon the title 
to the Property, or modify the terms or conditions of any existing leases, contracts or 
encumbrances, if any, without the written consent of Purchaser. 
 
 
viii) 
Seller has not entered into any agreements with any state, county or local 
governmental authority or agency which are not of record with respect to the Property, other than 
those approved in writing by Purchaser or disclosed herein. 
 
 
 
x) 
Seller has full power to sell, convey, transfer and assign the Property on behalf of 
all parties having an interest therein. 
 
 
 
 
xv.) 
This Contract has been duly authorized, executed and delivered by Seller and all 
documents executed by Seller which are to be delivered to Buyer at closing will be (a) duly 
authorized, executed and delivered by the Seller, (b) the legal, valid and binding obligation of 
Seller, and (c) sufficient to convey title and do not and at the time of Closing will not violate any 
provisions of any agreement or judicial order affecting Seller of the Property. 
 
 
6. 
INSPECTION: 
 
 
Purchaser or its agents shall have the right to enter upon the Premises and make inspections, 
investigations, test borings and boundary line and topographical surveys. To the extent permitted 
by law, Purchaser agrees to indemnify Seller and hold Seller harmless against all liability, loss, 
cost, damage and expense (including, without limitation, attorney's fees and cost of litigation) 
Seller suffers or incurs as a result of said activities of Purchaser, its engineers, surveyors, agents 
and representatives, upon the Premises. 
 
7. 
POSSESSION: 
 
 
Possession of the Premises shall be granted by Seller to Purchaser at closing. 
 
8. 
SURVEY: 
 
 
Prior to the date of closing as hereinafter provided, Purchaser may, at Purchaser's expense, 
cause an accurate survey to be made of the Premises by a reputable surveyor registered as such 
under the laws of the State of Georgia. All surveys made pursuant to this Paragraph will indicate 
the acreage of said Premises computed to the nearest one hundredth of an acre and may indicate 
any easement or right-of-way lying within said Premises. 
 
9. 
CLOSING: 

 
 
4

sixty (60) days after expiration of the due diligence period and at such time and place 
as shall be mutually agreed upon by Seller and Purchaser. Seller and Purchaser agree 
that such papers as may be legally necessary to carry out the terms of this Agreement 
shall be executed and delivered by such parties at the time the sale is consummated. 
 
 
(b) Purchaser shall pay all closing costs including, but not limited to, title examination

costs incurred by Purchaser in connection with the transaction contemplated herein. 
Each party shall bear the expense of their own legal counsel. 
 
(c) At closing, Seller shall execute and deliver or cause to be delivered to Buyer the 
following original documents: 
 
i) 
A good and marketable Limited Warranty Deed. 
 
 
ii) 
Owner’s Affidavit and additional documents as may be required in

d)

iv) 
All other documents as may be required to be executed and delivered

10. 
SPECIAL STIPULATIONS: 
 
 
This Agreement is contingent on the approval of the 2025 Supplemental Lease Contract 
by Gwinnett County and the approval of this Agreement in an open meeting by the Seller and 
Buyer in accordance with the Georgia Open Meetings Act.

TIME:

Mayor Whitlock called the work session to order at 5:35 p.m. 
 
 
I. 
PUBLIC COMMENTS 
 
None. 
 
 
II. 
DISCUSSION ITEMS/PRESENTATIONS/UPDATES 
 
1. STUDENT LEAD PRESENTATION 
 
 
 
 
 
{A} 
 
Participants from the City's 2025 Duluth HS Student LEAD program presented their 
project for Council review and comment. 
 
2. DULUTH 150TH CELEBRATION 
 
 
 
 
 
 
{B} 
 
Events/Marketing staff presented ideas related to the year-long 150th birthday celebration 
for Duluth. 
 
3. BUDGET AMENDMENTS – UPCOMING FEBRUARY AGENDA 
 
Assistant City Manager/Finance and Redevelopment Director Ken Sakmar presented 
budgets amendment requests pertaining to landscaping improvements, parking and 
pedestrian signage and street resurfacing projects. 
 
Council directed staff to place these items on the February 9th agenda for approval. 
 
4. MAILBOX REIMBURSEMENT PROGRAM 
 
 
 
City Manager James Riker reported that the United States Post Office (USPS) is requiring 
certain mailboxes within the Hall Circle area to be relocated to the opposite side of the 
street in order to accommodate the one-way roadway conversion. Given that this 
requirement was unknown to the City and property owners, staff is recommending 
establishing a reimbursement program for property owners to cover this expense.

2
 
Staff recommended that property owners submitting receipts to the Community 
Development Department for costs associated with relocating the mailboxes be allowed 
to receive up to $ 200 per mailbox. Staff anticipates approximately 28 properties that may 
be impacted by this requirement from USPS. 
 
Council directed staff to notify potentially affected property owners and offer 
reimbursement for 90 days following notice. 
 
5. ENCROACHMENT AGREEMENT – KNOX HOUSE 
 
Knox House Holding, LLC is extensively repairing and adapting the 1908 Knox House with 
both indoor and outdoor improvements for its proposed restaurant site. The improvement 
requires a relocation of an existing water line and valve as well as step access in the 
proposed encroachment area. Planning staff have reviewed and approved the 
construction plans in the encroachment. 
 
Council directed staff to place this item on the February 9th consent agenda for approval. 
 
6. RED CLAY REMODELING PROJECT BID AWARD/IGA 
 
City Manager James Riker presented. Mayor and Council were asked to consider a bid 
award for the Red Clay Theatre Remodeling Project. The city received 5 proposals for the 
remodeling project. After an evaluation of the proposals, staff recommended award of the 
project to BG Construction Group LLC. Staff is also recommending Council approve a 
budget amendment and corresponding Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) with the 
DDA to fund the project. 
 
Council directed staff to place these items on the February 9th agenda under New 
Business for approval.

graduate school working on a critical analysis paper and will attend the next Council meeting.

• Employee Benefits committee opening; Councilmember Park agreed to serve.

7. ORDINANCE TO AMEND BUDGET - $100,00 - DULUTH 150TH 
 
n October 2025, the City received $100,000 from the Duluth Fall Festival Committee 
to support Duluth's 150th Anniversary Concert that will take place later this year, 
requiring a budget amendment to added the funds to the FY 2026 budget. Approval 
of this item authorizes ordinance BA-FY26-23 to add General Funds of $100,000 to

VIII. NEW BUSINESS 
 
1. STORMWATER GRANT – LETTER OF COMMITMENT 
 
 
The stormwater department is applying for a "Climate Smart Communities Initiative 
Grant." This grant requires the partnership of three unique entities - a climate 
adaptation practitioner, a community partner, and a local government. 
 
The "lead applicant" which in this case is the climate adaptation practitioner, is the 
recipient of the grant, though some of the funds will pass through the community 
partner and the local government. The City will work with the climate adaptation 
practitioner and the community partner, which at this time we believe will be the 
Chattahoochee River Keepers, to apply for the grant and if awarded, will work with 
the same partners to develop a climate resilient stormwater master plan. We believe 
this effort will need to be done in at least two phases under separate projects to 
cover the two major drainage basins that Duluth covers. With the River Keepers on 
our team, we believe the Chattahoochee Basin will be the first to be master planned. 
Depending on the size of the grant award, the City may opt to scope by subbasins 
(smaller than basins) to avoid outspending the budget. 
 
Having a Stormwater Master Plan will set the City up for more success with future 
grant applications, and allow the City to better prioritize funding. Staff is requesting 
Council consider support of this grant and allow the Mayor or City Manager to sign a 
letter of commitment to be included with the grant application.

unallocated 2014 and 2023 SPLOST Parking funds to City Hall Design/Building -

transfers.

Climate Smart Communities Initiative (Climate Resilience Fund) – Memo 
Wednesday December 17th, 2025 
 
1. Grant Overview 
• Program: Climate Smart Communities Initiative (CSCI) 
• Funder: Climate Resilience Fund 
• Purpose: Support climate-smart planning and implementation that advances resilience, equity, 
and community-focused outcomes (e.g., climate-ready stormwater master planning). 
• Applicant: City of Duluth 
• Required Partners: Adaptation Practioners (AP) from the grants registry list (LINK HERE). We are 
in the process of interviewing AP’s that we would like to work with and will ultimately select one. 
We are interviewing with Community Based organizations as well. 
 
2. Roles & Responsibilities 
Adaptation Practioner (Fiscal Agent) 
Role: Provide climate science, hydrology, and adaptation expertise to ensure the Stormwater Master Plan 
accounts for future climate conditions, flood risk, and long-term system resilience. 
• Cash flows through AP to City the funds when needed. 
• Provide data, access, and subject-matter oversight. 
• Execute grant agreement; ensure compliance with funder terms. 
• Deliver scoped technical work 
 
Stormwater Division (Program Lead) 
Role: Works with AP & CBO to prioritize investments and adopt a resilient stormwater plan 
• Manage budget, invoicing, reporting, and audits. 
• Coordinate partners and oversee deliverables and timeline. 
• Submit application and serve as primary grantee. 
• Define project scope and technical priorities. 
• Review and approve partner deliverables. 
• Support reporting with programmatic updates. 
Community Based Organization (CBO) 
Role: Ensure the Stormwater Master Plan reflects lived experience with flooding, drainage issues, and 
climate impacts—particularly in historically underserved or flood-prone neighborhoods.

Subject: Letter of Commitment – Climate Smart Communities Initiative (CSCI) 
 
Dear Mayor and Members of City Council, 
 
This letter is submitted to formally request City Council’s approval and acknowledgement of the City of 
Duluth’s intent to apply for the Climate Smart Communities Initiative (CSCI) grant, administered by the 
Climate Resilience Fund, in partnership with a Community-Based Organization (CBO) of the City’s 
choosing and an Adaptation Practitioner (AP) selected from the CSCI Registry. 
 
The grant supports climate-smart planning that advances long-term resilience and equity. If awarded, 
the City will conduct a climate-informed stormwater and watershed planning effort that addresses future 
flood risk and incorporates community priorities. 
 
City Role and Responsibilities 
If awarded funding, the City of Duluth, through its Stormwater Division, commits to serving as the 
Program Lead and primary governmental partner. The City’s responsibilities will include: 
• Providing overall project leadership, coordination, and oversight 
• Defining project scope, priorities, and desired outcomes in alignment with City goals 
• Coordinating with the selected Adaptation Practitioner and Community-Based Organization 
• Reviewing and approving all partner deliverables 
• Managing programmatic reporting and supporting required grant documentation 
• Ensuring alignment with local policies, plans, and regulatory requirements 
 
Adaptation Practitioner Partnership 
The City intends to engage one Adaptation Practitioner selected from the Climate Smart Communities 
Initiative Registry to provide technical and professional expertise. Final selection of the Adaptation 
Practitioner will follow interviews and due diligence to ensure alignment with project needs and City 
procurement requirements. The Adaptation Practitioner is expected to: 
• Provide climate science, hydrology, and adaptation expertise 
• Manage fiscal administration as required by the grant

process. The CBO is expected to: 
• Facilitate community engagement and outreach activities 
• Support inclusive participation, particularly in historically underserved or flood-prone 
neighborhoods 
• Provide input to shape project priorities, recommendations, and outcomes 
 
Commitment and Authorization 
By submitting this application, the City affirms its commitment to: 
• Participate fully in the grant program if awarded 
• Enter into partnership agreements consistent with City and funder requirements 
• Allocate appropriate staff time and resources to support successful project implementation 
• Comply with all applicable grant terms, reporting obligations, and financial requirements

Climate Smart Communities Initiative Grant Application

Application Instructions 
Grant applications must be submitted by 8:00pm ET on Thursday, March 12, 2026. 
Check out the CSCI glossary for help with phrases, terms, and definitions. 
The CSCI grant application should be completed by a climate adaptation practitioner in 
the role of "lead applicant" in collaboration with one or more representatives from a 
community-based organization and from a local or regional government entity. All three 
of these partner types must be assembled to be eligible for a CSCI grant (learn more 
about typical roles on the CSCI funding page). 
To be eligible for a CSCI grant, the adaptation practitioner's firm or organization must 
have applied and been accepted into the Registry of Adaptation Practitioners. 
As the lead applicant, the adaptation practitioner will be the recipient of the award 
should the application be selected for a grant (though typically some funds are passed 
through to the local government and/or community-based organizations). The lead 
applicant will also be responsible for grant administration and reporting responsibilities 
throughout the grant period. If a different member of the project team is preferred as the 
lead applicant, please reach out to info@climatesmartcommunity.org before submitting 
your application. 
Application questions are designed to elicit information that will enable reviewers to 
evaluate answers based on CSCl's selection criteria, and to determine at which phase 
proposed projects are in the Steps to Resilience Framework (take time to become 
familiar with the Steps to Resilience in detail here or a brief summary here). Applications 
will be assessed based on whether a project is at the "Get Started" phase (climate 
resilience needs and goals are being discussed in the community for the very first time) 
or other later steps such as the "Take Action" phase (where climate change 
vulnerabilities are well understood and have been used to create a climate resilience 
plan from which particular aspects are now being put into action). 
Note: Application responses cannot be saved as a draft. (See the PDF preview of the 
application). It is strongly recommended to answer the questions in a word processor or

Project team readiness to make progress on climate resilience 
The Steps to Resilience (StR) cover the range of key phases in a climate resilience planning 
and implementation process from information gathering to research and analysis to planning 
and implementation. Integrating equity and community engagement can take place at any or 
all phases. 
Work within any and all StR phases is equally competitive. This will help reviewers 
understand where you are in a broader climate resilience planning process which helps them 
more accurately assess how what you are proposing aligns with your cited climate-related 
hazards, goals, and planned activities during the grant period. Reviewers are not evaluating 
how many phases a project will advance through or even whether a project completes a 
single phase as the pace and degree of progress that is appropriate or feasible varies greatly 
across project teams, the phase that project is currently at, the community, and how climate 
change is impacting it. 
* 30. At what phase in the Steps to Resilience (StR) Framework are the activities you are

proposed work during the 12-month grant period. Each selection will prompt you to 
provide more information about the prior work done to prepare your project team and 
community to take on the proposed activities. 
D Get Started. Assemble a team of partners and stakeholders to explore local climate change 
issues, consult existing community plans or prior climate resilience efforts, and develop 
community vision and goals. Typically, this step is reserved for communities that are 
pursuing climate resilience planning or implementation efforts for the first time or are at the 
very beginning a brand new planning effort. 
D Understand Exposure. Identify what assets (people, infrastructure, natural systems, etc.) 
are being impacted by climate change-related hazards and prioritize their importance to 
the community within a defined project area. This process/step helps inform where a future 
risk assessment and/or vulnerability analysis should focus. 
D Assess Vulnerability and Risk. Follow an assessment process with input from the 
community and relevant experts to analyze the sensitivity and adaptive capacity of assets, 
the risk levels of the potential impacts on them, and pre-existing non-climate stressors that 
can amplify vulnerability or contribute to certain groups being disproportionately impacted. 

D Investigate Options. Gather information on adaptation options (actions, strategies) that 
are likely to reduce the community's risk and vulnerability to climate change, work with the 
community to refine its climate resilience objectives, and understand what can be done to 
manage its risk. 
D Prioritize and Plan. In coordination with the community, key stakeholders and partners 
determine a method or criteria to prioritize which adaptation options are most aligned with 
the community's goals and values and should be included in a community climate resilience 
or climate adaptation plan. 
D Take Action. Implement adaptation actions aimed at reducing community vulnerability to 
climate change (e.g., expanding or creating programmatic activities or installation of nature-
based solutions (NbS) or building physical infrastructure). 
D Take Action. Leverage or obtain public or private funding sources to finance adaptation 
actions in the community. 
D Take Action. Revise or create new laws or policies or regulations that require or incentivize 
adaptation action and penalize maladaptation. 
D Any or all StR phases. Integrate equity by explicitly incorporating equity into climate 
resilience goals, plans, planning processes, planning and implementation decisions, 
engagement processes, and policies. 
D Any or all StR phases. Engage the community by effectively communicating about climate 
risks and potential solutions with the goal of increasing community preparedness for 
climate change and ensuring adaptation actions are effective and provide equitable 
benefits.

To: Climate Smart Communities Initiative Grant Review Committee 
 
Re: City Council Support for Climate Smart Communities Initiative (CSCI) Grant Application 
 
Dear Grant Review Committee, 
 
At its voting meeting on January 12, 2026, the Duluth City Council voted to support the City of 
Duluth Stormwater Division’s application for the Climate Smart Communities Initiative 
(CSCI) Grant to advance a climate resilience watershed study and related planning efforts. 
 
If awarded, the City will conduct a climate-informed stormwater and watershed planning 
effort that addresses future flood risk and incorporates community priorities. This work is 
intended to be carried out in partnership with an Adaptation Practitioner selected from the 
CSCI Adaptation Practitioner Registry and a Community-Based Organization selected by the 
City, consistent with grant requirements and City procurement policies. 
 
The City of Duluth understands and supports the obligations associated with this application 
and, if awarded, will serve as the Program Lead through its Stormwater Division. The City 
anticipates providing City staff time to support application preparation, project coordination, 
and project oversight, and authorizes staff to administer the grant and coordinate the project 
if awarded. 
 
The Duluth City Council supports this application and affirms the City’s commitment to 
successfully carrying out the proposed scope of work in accordance with grant 
requirements. 
 
 Sincerely, 
 
 
 
 
Greg Whitlock 
Mayor, City of Duluth 
On behalf of the Duluth City Council

{K} 
 
Community Development/Engineering Director Margie Pozin explained that the 
stormwater department is applying for a "Climate Smart Communities Initiative Grant." 
 

Draft Minutes of M&C 
January 12, 2026 
Page 5 of 7 
 
5
 
This grant requires the partnership of three unique entities - a climate adaptation 
practitioner, a community partner, and a local government. 
 
The "lead applicant" which in this case is the climate adaptation practitioner, is the 
recipient of the grant, though some of the funds will pass through the community 
partner and the local government. The City will work with the climate adaptation 
practitioner and the community partner, which at this time we believe will be the 
Chattahoochee River Keepers, to apply for the grant and if awarded, will work with the 
same partners to develop a climate resilient stormwater master plan. We believe this 
effort will need to be done in at least two phases under separate projects to cover the 
two major drainage basins that Duluth covers. With the River Keepers on our team, we 
believe the Chattahoochee Basin will be the first to be master planned. Depending on 
the size of the grant award, the City may opt to scope by subbasins (smaller than basins) 
to avoid outspending the budget. 
 
Ms. Pozin said the typical award is between $90k and $110k. The City is going to pursue 
$110, and then the practitioner will assist to determine a scope that can be reasonably 
achieved regarding number of sub basins, perhaps several that can be incorporated into 
a master plan. Once there is a formal plan, it can be used to pursue additional and larger 
grants to help us implement other projects. There is no match requirement for this 
particular grant, but in order to get to a logical scope additional funds have been 
identified from the stormwater budget if we receive the grant and have to increase the 
scope for any reason. 
 
In summary, having a Stormwater Master Plan will set the City up for more success with 
future grant applications, and allow the City to better prioritize funding. Staff is 
requesting Council consider support of this grant and allow the Mayor or City Manager to 
sign a letter of commitment to be included with the grant application. 
 
A motion was made by Councilmember Park, seconded by Councilmember Thomas, 
to approve Council's support of this grant application and authorize the City 
Manager or Mayor to sign a letter of commitment for the Climate Smart 
Communities Initiative Grant as presented. 
 
Voted For: 
Council members Park, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Cummings 
Motion carried.

I. 
PURPOSE AND DESCRIPTION OF THE REQUEST 
The purpose of the request (2025-005) from the City of Duluth, on behalf of Rainbow 
Village, is to rezone a previously unused right-of-way parcel (+/-.135 acres) from unzoned to 
PUD (Planned Unit Development). The proposed rezoning request corresponds with the sale 
of real property (unused right-of-way) by the City of Duluth to Rainbow Village. The unused 
right-of-way will be an egress driveway for the expansion of the Rainbow Village campus. 
Maps detailing the location, zoning district and character area of the subject property are 
attached hereto as Exhibit "A". The survey and legal description of the +/-.135 acre subject 
property is attached hereto as Exhibit "B". Recommended conditions of approval are detailed 
in Exhibit "C". 
The city initiated the rezoning as part of a housekeeping matter to document consistency 
with the overall Rainbow Village campus expansion. 
 
II. 
EXISTING CONDITIONS 
The subject property totals +/- 0.135 acres. The property is located within the Downtown 
Overlay District. The property to the west of Rainbow Village is zoned PUD. The rezoning 
request for this parcel is part of a housekeeping matter to document consistency with the 
overall Rainbow Village campus expansion. The subject parcel was previously unused right-
of-way and was sold to Rainbow Village with deed conditions that it be used for access 
relating to their expansion. 
 
III. 
REVIEW OF THE REQUEST 
 
1. 
Literal Interpretation of the Unified Development Code (UDC) 
 
The application is reviewed for compliance with the requirements for PUD development 
(Sec. 504.02 of the UDC), review standards for PUD Rezoning (Sec. 504.06 of the UDC), and 
standards governing the exercise of zoning power (Sec. 1104.02 of the UDC). 
 
2. 
Standards Governing the Exercise of Zoning Power 
 
The current zoning of the property is unzoned. Therefore, a rezoning to PUD is necessary to 
allow for consistency with the Rainbow Village campus expansion. In accordance with 
Section 504.01 of the Unified Development Code (UDC), the PUD zoning district is intended 
to: 
1) Encourage larger scale planned development which will produce a logically 
organized and compatible set of land uses resulting in a higher overall quality of 
community development than if accomplished in incremental unplanned stages. 
2) Allow a mixture and/or density of land uses not otherwise allowed in an established 
zoning district; by careful site planning the appropriate site improvements are 
incorporated into the plan that establish compatible relationships between the uses 
within the site and uses adjacent to the site.

A. How the proposed special use will allow a use that is suitable in view of the use and development of

The proposed gold buying business is suitable for this location, as the suite is within a commercial shopping 
center (Parc Walk at River Green) that already supports retail and service-based businesses. A professional 
gold buying operation aligns with the character of surrounding uses, such as retail shops, restaurants, and 
service providers. It will operate during normal business hours and will not generate noise, odors, or other 
disturbances that would be incompatible with nearby tenants or properties. 
 
B. How the proposed special use will adversely affect the existing use or usability of adjacent or 
nearby property. 
 
The business will not adversely affect adjacent or nearby properties. Gold buying is a low-traffic, appointment-
and walk-in-based service with minimal impact on parking or pedestrian flow. Unlike higher-intensity uses 
such as restaurants or event venues, the business requires only a small footprint and a limited number of daily 
customers. Security measures, including surveillance cameras and controlled transactions, will further ensure 
that the business enhances, rather than diminishes, the safety and usability of the area. 
 
C. Whether the property to be affected by a proposed special use has a reasonable economic use as 
currently zoned. 
 
The property is currently zoned for commercial use and is located within a retail/service shopping center. The 
proposed special use is consistent with commercial economic activity and represents a reasonable economic 
use of the property. Without this approval, the space would otherwise remain limited to general retail/service 
uses, many of which are similar in intensity and scale to the proposed gold buying business. 
 
D. Whether the proposed special use will result in a use which will or could cause an excessive or 
burdensome use of existing streets, transportation facilities, utilities, or schools. 
 
The proposed business will not create an excessive or burdensome demand on streets, utilities, or public 
facilities. Customer traffic is minimal compared to restaurants or retail anchors in the center. The business 
does not impact schools or require additional municipal services beyond standard water, power, and internet 
usage. Waste generation is negligible and limited to standard office refuse.

B. If the use is discontinued or abandoned for a period of ninety (90) days, regardless of the 
intent of the owner or occupier to resume the use, the Special Use is hereby terminated. 
C. If the use is extended in any way, either on the same or adjoining property, the Special Use is 
terminated. 
 
2. The business must participate in the LEADSOnline program. Duluth Police must be made aware 
when the business is registered and this must be done prior to operating the business. 
 
3. All signage must comply with Article 6 of the Unified Development Code; furthermore, the 
aggregate for all wall signs and window coverings shall not exceed 20% of all windows combined. 
 
4. The property shall be maintained in a state of good repair at all times, free from any violations of 
the Property Maintenance Code; Unified Development Code; License and Business Regulations; 
Nuisance Codes, and any other codes adopted by the City of Duluth. Failure to maintain the 
property at or above the minimum standards adopted in the City of Duluth codes and ordinance 
shall be cause for possible legal action by the City. 
 
5. The privilege of a Special Use is subject to all conditions that have been attached to it. It is within 
the City’s rights to take legal action if it is proven that the conditions of the Special Use have been 
violated.
