7.14 Conflict Of interest 
These conflict of interest requirements are provided for GDOT employees engaged in the award and 
administration of consultant services and agreements and to provide for governing the conduct and roles 
of consultants in the performance of services under such agreements to prevent, identify, and mitigate 
conflicts of interest in accordance with 2 CFR 200.112, 23 CFR 1.33, and 23 CFR 172.7(b)(4). The 
requirements will also assure that GDOT meets Federal requirements related to conflict of interest and 
will be consistent in the actions taken when a conflict arises. 
7.14.1 CONSULTANT RESPONSIBILITY 
When responding to an RFP, it is expected that firms will not submit proposals on projects where a 
conflict of interest exists. The consultant is required to submit a letter to the Procurement 
Administrator disclosing a potential conflict of interest each time they submit a proposal. Upon 
selection for on-call services: Embedded consultant staff is instructed to not review work performed 
by their firm. If at any time, the consultant has any questions or concerns regarding a potential 
conflict they may contact the Project Manager. 
7.14.2 GDOT Responsibility 
The Project Manager will review the potential conflict identified in the consultant’s proposal and any 
agreement relationships and determine, in consultation with appropriate GDOT staff, if a conflict of 
interest or the appearance of a conflict of interest exists. If a conflict is found to exist, GDOT will 
determine the appropriateness of the proposed measures to mitigate the conflict. The 
determination needs to be balanced between the benefits to GDOT and the potential issues that can 
arise if a consultant or the affiliate (a corporate entity linked to the consultant through common 
ownership) is responsible to more than one party on the same project. GDOT will inform the 
consultant that a conflict of interest does exist along with the proposed mitigation measures. If the 
consultant chooses to retain the interest constituting the conflict, GDOT may remove the consultant 
from the selection for cause in accordance with the provisions stated in the agreement. 
For on-call services, GDOT Project managers/supervisors are responsible to avoid a conflict of 
interest by ensuring the consultant assigned the work and the embedded consultant reviewer is not 
employed by the same firm. Embedded consultants will not be involved in the consultant 
solicitation process, or the review of consultant fee proposals or negotiation. 
GDOT’s employees shall not participate in selection or in the award or administration of a consultant 
agreement if a conflict of interest, real or apparent, would be involved. Such a conflict arises when 
there is a financial or other interest in the consultant selected for award by: 
a) The employee; 
b) Any member of his or her immediate family; 
c) His or her partner; or 
d) An organization that employs or is about to employ any of the above. Accepting items that 
would influence a selection committee’s judgement is not acceptable. See the following for 
more information regarding this topic: GDOTs Human Resources Policies & Procedures 3A-17- 
Code of Conduct Pertaining to Conflict of Interest in Award and Administration of Contracts, 
and 2 CFR Section 200.318(c)(1) and (c)(2).

I. 
PURPOSE AND DESCRIPTION OF THE REQUEST 
The purpose of this Special Use request (SU2024-001) is to allow the sale of Tobacco and 
Tobacco products (cigars, tobacco, vape products) in the C-2 (General Business District) 
zoning district. 
Maps detailing the location, zoning district and character area of the subject property are 
attached hereto as Exhibit “A”. The legal description of the subject property is attached 
hereto as Exhibit “B”. Recommended conditions of approval are detailed in Exhibit “C”. 
 
II. 
EXISTING CONDITIONS 
 
The subject property totals +/- 1.05 acres. The suite in which the applicant would like to place 
the business is a 1,395 sq ft store front. To the east of the subject property is the residential 
subdivision Chattahoochee Landing, which is a Planned Unit Development (PUD). To the west 
of the subject property is the senior living facility Parc at Duluth, which is also a PUD. To the 
north and south of the subject property is zoned C-2 (General Business District). 
 
 
III. 
REVIEW OF THE REQUEST 
 
1. 
Literal Interpretation of the Unified Development Code (UDC) 
 
A. Table 2-C of the UDC allows “Cigar, Tobacco and Other Smoker’s Supply Stores” in 
the C-2 zoning district by way of Special Use approval from the Duluth City Council. 
 
B. Section 1101.02 of the UDC states if a proposed use is not allowed by right under the 
existing zoning on a property, a request for an amendment to the Official Zoning Map 
(often called a “rezoning”) must be approved prior to development, construction, or 
occupancy. 
 
C. Section 1105 of the UDC establishes the Special Use Considerations. 
 
The Special Use is designed to apply under any one of the following circumstances: 
1. A Special Use listed under the zoning district is desired for development and a 
more intensive zoning district containing that use, as a use by right would not be 
appropriate for the property; or 
 
2. A Special Use listed under the zoning district is desired for development and no 
zoning district contains that use as a use by right; or 
 
3. A unique use not addressed in any zoning district is desired for development and 
is not likely to be duplicated within the City of Duluth; or 
 
4. The density of development may be affected by the height of a building; or 
 
5. The neighboring properties may be affected by the height of any structure; or

community as a whole, be compatible with the neighborhood and would not be 
in conflict with the overall objective of the Comprehensive Plan.

to approve such a use on a particular parcel without changing the general zoning district.

3. 
Literal Interpretation of FORWARDuluth, Plan 2040 (Comprehensive Plan) 
 
The subject property is located in the Peachtree Retail Corridor District. 
FORWARDuluth envisions this Character Area to serve as an attractive and energized 
retail corridor easily accessed by Duluth residents and non-city residents alike. The 
Character Area is characterized by strip retail centers and stand alone commercial 
buildings. The Future Land Use Map (FLUM) envisions the uses to be 
commercial/retail/office. 
 
 
IV. 
PLANNING STAFF REVIEW 
 
Between an amendment to the UDC on April 11, 2016 and today’s current iteration of the 
UDC, Cigar and Tobacco Stores as a use went from being allowed by right in C-2, HC-Retail 
and HC-Auto, to only being allowed by special use in the C-2 zoning district. Since that change, 
the City of Duluth has only had a single application for a tobacco or tobacco product retail 
store. That request came in front of the Planning Commission in November of 2023. At that 
hearing, Planning Commission recommended approval with conditions. The Mayor and 
Council heard the request in December of 2023 and denied that application. 
The Vision & Aspirations chapter and supporting Character Area Map of FORWARDuluth 
(also known as the Comprehensive Plan) identifies the Character Area of this property as the 
Retail Corridor District. The Retail Corridor District is currently characterized by strip retail 
centers and stand-alone commercial buildings. The corridor is easily accessible to city 
residents by car as well as non-city residents traveling through Duluth. A few of the 
aspirations within the Peachtree Retail Corridor are: work with building owners to help 
maintain high occupancy rates through business retention and recruitment; continue code 
compliance efforts to maintain an attractive appearance of shopping centers and buildings; 
encourage more development and reinvestment in older commercial buildings. In the case

I. 
PURPOSE AND DESCRIPTION OF THE REQUEST 
The purpose of the rezoning request (Z2024-001) is to rezone the current parcel from O-I 
(Office-Institutional District) to PUD (Planned Unit Development). 
 
Maps detailing the location, zoning district and character area of the subject property are 
attached hereto as Exhibit “A”. The legal description of the subject property is attached hereto 
as Exhibit “B”. Recommended conditions of approval are detailed in Exhibit “C”. Applicant’s 
Responses to the Standards Governing Special Use Consideration are provided in Exhibit “D”. 
Applicant’s Letter of Intent is provided in Exhibit “E”. The Master Plan is located in Exhibit “F”. 
In order for the applicant to achieve their desired land use on the subject property, they are 
required to rezone the subject property. 
 
II. 
EXISTING CONDITIONS 
 
The subject property totals +/- 11.2 acres and is currently undeveloped. The subject property 
lies on the edge of unincorporated Gwinnett County along Sugarloaf Parkway. To the east of the 
subject property is Hull Middle School, which is zoned R-100 (Single-Family Residential), but 
functions as O-I in this case. The subject property is bound to the north by Old Peachtree Road. 
Across from Old Peachtree Road to the north is a single-family neighborhood known as the 
Haven at Sugarloaf Ridge, which is zoned PUD (Planned Unit Development). The subject parcel 
is bound to the west by Sugarloaf Parkway. Across from Sugarloaf Parkway is a single-family 
subdivision known as Sugarloaf Country club, which lies in unincorporated Gwinnett County. 
To the south of the subject is zoned RTH (Residential Town Home) in unincorporated Gwinnett 
County. It is currently being developed into a townhome development with 33 townhomes on 
6.055 acres, which yields a density of 5.45 units per acre. 
 
 
III. 
ZONING HISTORY 
 
In 2003, the subject property was annexed into the City of Duluth as part of a larger +/-120 acre 
annexation and rezoning. Prior to the annexation into the City, the property was zoned R-100 
(Single-family Residential) by Gwinnett County. The annexation was accompanied by a rezoning 
application for a PUD (Planned Unit Development). As is typical with PUD application, the 
applicant submitted a master concept plan to be approved with the rezoning. The subject 
property was shown to be the commercial portion of the mixed-use PUD with the remaining 
property being residential. Between 2004 – 2007, the residential portion of the PUD was 
developed by Pulte into the 350-unit Haven at Sugarloaf Ridge subdivision. The subject property 
remained undeveloped. 
 
In 2009, an amended site plan for the subject site was submitted and approved. The amended 
site plan included six (6) buildings consisting of grocery, restaurant, office, retail and food court 
uses. The total square footage of the proposed buildings was 178,796 sf. The plan also called for 
a “central park” feature in the middle of the site. 
 
In 2018, Paradise Evangelistic Association applied for and was approved for a rezoning from 
PUD (Planned Unit Development) to O-I (Office-Institutional District) to allow for the 
construction of a +/- 60,000 sf building intended to be used as a place of religious assembly. 
 
In 2020 the zoning was modified again to allow a slightly smaller church building and a medical 
office building. 
 
Paradise Evangelistic Association, LLC has amended the proposal and is seeking approval for a 
rezoning from O-I (Office-Institutional) to PUD (Planned Unit Development) to allow for a 
smaller footprint church from the previously requested, from a +/- 60,000 sf building to a +/- 

30,890 sf building (636 seat sanctuary), a 150 seat accessory chapel and amphitheater, and a 
residential component including 71 townhome residences on the remaining 7.504 acres, 
yielding a density of 9.42 units per acre. 
 
IV. 
REVIEW OF THE REQUEST 
 
1. 
Literal Interpretation of the Unified Development Code (UDC) 
 
A. Section 1101.02 of the UDC states if a proposed use is not allowed by right under the 
existing zoning on a property, a request for an amendment to the Official Zoning Map 
(often called a “rezoning”) must be approved prior to development, construction, or 
occupancy. 
 
2. 
Standards Governing the Exercise of Zoning Power 
 
Section 1104.02 of the UDC establishes the standards governing the exercise of zoning 
power. The following standards are relevant in balancing the interest and promoting the 
public health, safety, morality, and general welfare against the right to the unrestricted 
use of property: 
A. 
Whether the zoning proposal will permit a use that is suitable in view of the use 
and development of adjacent and nearby property. 
 
B. 
Whether the zoning proposal will adversely affect the existing use or usability of 
adjacent or nearby property. 
 
C. 
Whether the zoning proposal will result in a use that will or could cause an 
excessive or burdensome use of existing streets, transportation facilities, utilities, 
or schools. 
 
D. 
Whether the zoning proposal is consistent with the Land Use Policy Plan, 
Comprehensive Plan, transportation plans, or other plans adopted for guiding 
development within the City of Duluth. 
 
E. 
Whether there are other existing or changing conditions affecting the use and 
development of property that give supporting grounds for either approval or 
disapproval of the zoning or special use proposal. 
 
The Applicant has provided written responses to the above Special Use standards and 
Rezoning Standards as part of the application. Those documents are attached hereto as 
Exhibit “E”. 
 
3. 
Literal Interpretation of FORWARDuluth, Plan 2040 (Comprehensive Plan) 
 
The subject property is located in the Established Neighborhoods Character Area. 
FORWARDuluth envisions this Character Area to be the backbone of Duluth’s residential 
community. Ranging from traditional suburban neighborhoods to more walkable and 
community centered townhome developments, a variety of housing types and price 
ranges gives a wide variety of people across income levels, age groups and other social 
strata the opportunity to live in Duluth. The Future Land Use Map (FLUM) envisions this 
parcel as mixed use.

Walkability 
With its proximity to many commercial and entertainment nodes including Sugarloaf Market,

at Sugarloaf, Galleria at Sugarloaf and the Gas South District, the proposed development is well

Landscaping 
It is the staff’s opinion that a key feature of this development would be a lush landscape plan. 
The landscape plan should enhance the buffer between Sugarloaf Parkway, Old Peachtree Road 
and the subject property. The buffer should incorporate a mix of region-appropriate evergreen 
trees and shrubs along with a mix of native deciduous trees. This mix of deciduous trees should 
incorporate small, medium and large canopy trees throughout the site. This enhanced buffer is 
in addition to the required 224.16 Tree Density Units for the entire site. An approved landscape 
plan shall be reviewed and approved prior to development.

Open Space 
A minimum of 10% of the gross area of the site shall be retained in common open space that is 
required to be deeded as a separate tract to an Owners Association and shall forever remain as 
open space. The required common open space shall include any conservation areas within a 
conservation easement established in accordance with Section 505. Without underground 
detention, meeting this requirement will be difficult. 
While this PUD is not solely multi-family dwellings, the uses are so disparate that 504.02 (c) will 
be considered, meaning that there should be some programed ground floor space area for non-
residential use, such as access to a church gym or common room for the residents of the 
townhome development. 
The proposal demonstrates a pocket park, gazebo and fire pit among elements of the open space. 
Parking 
Per the UDC (Unified Development Code), Townhome uses require 2 enclosed spaces per 
dwelling unit, plus an additional outdoor space per 5 units. With 71 units, there are, proposed, 
142 garage covered parking spaces, with an additional 142 by way of driveway. Proposed guest 
parking is at 34 spaces, which is over required parking by 19 spaces, exceeding the allowable 
120% excess of minimum parking spaces. 
Per the UDC, Churches or other Places of Worship require 1 space per 5 seats. The proposed 
church is proposing 262 parking spaces, which exceeds the allowable parking spaces by 187 
parking spaces by 75 parking spaces. 
Please see how parking was discussed in the “First Amended Statement of Intent/Written 
Justification” in Exhibit “F”

INTRODUCTION 
This Application seeks to rezone ± 11.208 acres of land located in the Land Lot 199, 7th District, 
Gwinnett County, City of Duluth, Georgia (“Subject Property”). More particularly, the Subject Property is 
located in the southeast quadrant of the intersection of Old Peachtree Road and Sugarloaf Parkway 
(“Subject Property”) from Office-Institutional District (O-I) to Planned Unit Development (PUD) to allow 
the development of 71 single family townhomes and a church. The Subject Property has a lengthy 
rezoning history dating back 20 years. In 2003, the Subject Property was annexed into the City of Duluth 
as part of a larger ±120-acre annexation and rezoning. Prior to the annexation into the City, the property 
was zoned R-100 by Gwinnett County. The annexation was accompanied with a rezoning application for 
PUD (“2003 PUD”). Between 2004 and 2007, the residential portion of the PUD was developed into the 350 
unit Sugarloaf Ridge neighborhood. In 2009, an amended site plan for the Subject Property was submitted

to allow the development of a ±60,000 square foot church. This zoning was modified in 2020 to allow a 
slightly smaller church building and the incorporation of a medical office building. The Church’s vision for 
the medical office building, however, never materialized and likewise the church was not constructed. 
Since that time, the Church has been searching for opportunities for the development of this property.

WHETHER THE ZONING PROPOSAL WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE EXISTING USE 
OR USABILITY OF ADJACENT OR NEARBY PROPERTY 
Prior to the filing of this Application, the Applicant has engaged in conversations with City Staff and 
will engage the community to make sure its proposal is acceptable to the neighbors. The primary goal of 
land use planning is to eliminate or minimize the potential adverse effect of the dissimilar uses of adjacent 
tracts of land by establishing a harmonious transition between them. The traditional method of achieving 
this goal is through both "off-site" and "on-site" transition. Off-site transition consists of avoiding the 
placement of dissimilar uses next to each other by placing uses of intermediate density between them. 
On-site transition, which might either supplement or replace off-site transition, consists of measures 
imposed on or adjacent to the more intensive use to protect neighborhoods from adverse effects. Thus, 
this method of land use planning includes measures such as maintenance of buffers; walls, fences or 
berms; lighting control; noise control; aesthetic control; limitations on building location and orientation; 
location of or restrictions upon accessory uses; and prohibition of certain uses or hours of use normally 
permitted for that district. All of these devices have been utilized in this Application.

corporate limits of the City of Duluth, Georgia. 
 
This Ordinance shall become effective on May 13, 2024. 
 
The City Clerk of the City of Duluth is instructed to send certified copies of this ordinance, together with a 
map and appropriate survey to the Department of Community Affairs for the State of Georgia, and to the 
governing authority and election officials of Gwinnett County, within thirty (30) days after the effective 
date of the annexation as set forth above.

WHEREAS, all ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordinance are repealed; and 
 
NOW THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF DULUTH HEREBY ORDAINS AS FOLLOWS: 
 
SECTION 1. FINDINGS. 
 
Pursuant to Article 11 of the Duluth Unified Development Code, the City Council finds that it is 
appropriate to rezone the properties listed above from R-75 (Single-Family Residential, Gwinnett 
County) to R-75 (Single-Family Residential, City of Duluth) for the following reasons: 
 
A. The rezoning is suitable given the use and development of adjacent and nearby properties. 
 
B. The proposed rezoning is not anticipated to adversely affect the existing use or usability of 
adjoining or nearby properties as conditions within the Unified Development Code will be 
imposed on any development that address uses and intensities, architecture and design, landscape 
and screening, transportation and parking, roadways, stormwater facilities, street lighting and 
signage. 
 
C. The proposed rezoning is not anticipated to cause excessive or burdensome use of existing streets, 
transportation facilities, utilities, or schools. 
 
D. While every section of FORWARDuluth (Duluth Comprehensive Plan, 2045) is central to 
implementing the City’s vision and goals, the Character Areas and Future Land Use Maps are the 
most influential in terms of daily decision-making and land use changes. Residential – low density 
has been envisioned on these properties through the Comprehensive Plan and the Future Land 
Use Map. 
 
E. In April of 2024, the City amended FORWARDuluth, the 2045 update to the Comprehensive Plan. 
The subject properties are located within the “Established Neighborhoods District” character area. 
The aspirations for this character area include maintaining a high level of owner occupancy, 
promoting property upkeep and maintenance through effective code compliance and the Duluth 
N.O.W. program, and to identifying opportunities to increase walkability and connectivity through 
possible street and pedestrian connections between neighborhoods. 
 
SECTION 2. SEVERABILTY. 
 
Should any section or provision of this Ordinance or any Ordinance pertaining to the companion 
applications as identified above be declared invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent 
jurisdiction, such declaration shall not affect the validity of this Ordinance as a whole or any part thereof 
which is not specifically declared to be invalid or unconstitutional. 
 
SECTION 3. EFFECTIVE DATE. 
 
The effective date of this Ordinance shall be upon approval by the City Council of the City of Duluth, 
Georgia.

Advertisement for Bids 
Asphalt Rejuvenation 
The City of Duluth is accepting sealed bids from qualified contractors to 
provide all necessary labor, material and equipment necessary to perform all 
operations for the application of an asphalt rejuvenating agent to asphalt 
concrete surfaces. The rejuvenation of surface courses shall be by spray 
application of a cationic rejuvenating agent composed of petroleum oils and 
resins emulsified with water. All work shall be in accordance with the 
specifications, the applicable drawings and subject to the terms and 
conditions of this contract. 
A proposed list of streets is included in the full Invitation to Bid available at 
www.duluthga.net under the heading “Notices and RFP’s”. The roads shown on the 
proposed list are intended locations. During the life of the contract it may become 
necessary to remove one or more locations from the list, it may also be necessary to 
add one or more locations to the list. It is the City of Duluth’s intention to stay within 
total contract cost; therefore work may stop when the total cost reaches or nearly 
reaches the awarded amount. The final decision will be made as work progresses. The 
City of Duluth reserves the right to such. No claims will be considered for extra 
compensation. 
All sealed bids will be received by the City of Duluth City Clerk, 3167 Main Street, 
Duluth, Georgia 30096, until 9:45 A.M. local time on Monday, April 29, 2024. 
Bids received after the stated time will not be accepted. Bids will be opened 
publicly and read aloud on Monday, April 29, 2024 at 10:00 A.M. on the second 
floor of Duluth City Hall, 3167 Main Street, Duluth GA 30096, in the Executive 
Conference Room. The bid envelope must be marked on the outside with the following 
information: 
 
City of Duluth 
 
Bid – 2024 Asphalt Rejuvenation 
 
Date and Hour of Bid Opening 
 
Company Name 
The complete Invitation to Bid is available for download on the City of Duluth website at 
https://www.duluthga.net/aboutduluth/noticesandrfps/requestsforproposa
ls.php 
Full Invitation to Bid is also available for viewing at the Duluth Public Works 
Department, 2450 Main Street, Duluth, Georgia 30097. 

There will not be a pre-bid conference for this procurement. Contract will be awarded, 
if at all, within sixty (60) calendar days after opening of the proposal. 
The deadline for questions is Monday, April 22, 2024 at 5:00 P.M. Submit all questions 
to Audrey Turner, Public Works Director at aturner@duluthga.net No phone calls will 
be accepted. 
The selected contractor must be able to start work within ten (10) calendar days after 
the “Notice to Proceed” is issued. The time of completion for the project is sixty (60) 
calendar days from the date of the “Notice to Proceed”. 
All bids shall be accompanied by a bid bond in favor of the City, in the amount of five 
percent (5%) of the total bid, (but not less than $5,000); such bid bond representing 
that the bidder, if awarded a contract, will promptly enter into a contract and furnish 
performance bond and payment bond as provided by law and approved by the attorney 
for the City. Failure to submit a bid bond with the proper rating will result in 
the bid being deemed non-responsive. 
Successful bidder will be required to meet insurance requirements. Performance and 
Payment bonds will be required upon acceptance of the proposal and contract 
submittal. 
 
The Performance Bond shall be equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the 
contract amount. The Payment Bond shall be equal to one hundred ten 
percent (110%) of the contract amount. 
 
 Insurance and Bonding Company must be licensed to do business by the Georgia 
Secretary of State, authorized to business in Georgia by the Georgia Insurance 
Department, listed in the Department of Treasury’s Publication of Companies holding 
Certificates of Authority as Acceptable Surety on Federal Bonds and as acceptable 
reinsuring companies. The bid bond, payment bond and performance bond 
must have an A.M. Best rating of A-5 or higher. 
 
Award will be made to the lowest responsible and responsive bidder. The City of 
Duluth reserves the right to reject any and all bids, to waive technicalities and to make 
an award as deemed in its best interest. 
 
Any change to the conditions and specifications must be in the form of a written 
addendum to be valid; therefore the City will issue a written addendum to document 
each approved change.

Advertisement for Bids 
2024 LMIG Mill, Patch and Resurface Program on various streets within the City of 
Duluth 
The City of Duluth is accepting sealed bids from qualified contractors to provide all 
necessary labor, material and equipment necessary to perform asphaltic concrete milling, 
deep patching (as directed), excavation of unsuitable material as needed, replacement, 
grading, compaction of grade aggregate base course as needed, patching or other 
structures, and installation or replacement of thermoplastic striping as directed, traffic 
control, erosion control and dust control on various streets within the City limits of 
Duluth. All work shall be in accordance with the specifications, the applicable drawings 
and subject to the terms and conditions of this contract. 
The contract will include multiple road projects for milling, patching and resurfacing. A proposed 
BASE project list as well as a proposed Alternate (additional list of projects) is included in the full 
Invitation to Bid available at www.duluthga.net under the heading “Notices and RFP’s”. 
All sealed bids will be received by the City of Duluth City Clerk, 3167 Main Street, Duluth, Georgia 
30096, until 1:45 P.M. local time on Monday, April 22, 2024. Bids received after the stated 
time will not be accepted. Bids will be opened publicly and read aloud on Monday, April 22, 
2024 at 2:00 P.M. on the second floor of Duluth City Hall, 3167 Main Street, Duluth GA 30096, in 
the Executive Conference Room. The bid envelope must be marked on the outside with the following 
information: 
City of Duluth 
Bid – 2024 LMIG Mill, Patch and Resurface Program on Various Roads within City 
of Duluth 
Date and Hour of Bid Opening 
Company Name 
 
Winning contractor will be required to provide an Eighteen month (18) warranty on all 
work completed. 
Pre-Bid Conference will be held at City of Duluth Public Works Facility – 2450 Main Street 
in Duluth, Georgia 30096, on Thursday, April 4, 2024 at 10:00 A.M. 
Full Invitation to Bid is available on the City of Duluth website, www.duluthga.net under the heading 
“Notices and RFP’s” 
Full Invitation to Bid is also available for viewing at the Duluth Public Works Department, 2450 Main 
Street, Duluth, Georgia 30097. 
Bid will be awarded based upon Base Bid. 
Contract will be awarded, if at all, within sixty (60) calendar days after opening of the proposal. 

Deadline for questions is Monday, April 15, 2024 at 5 P.M. Submit all questions to Adam Shelton, 
PE, of Keck & Wood at bidquestions@keckwood.com No phone calls will be accepted. 
The selected contractor must be able to start work within ten (10) calendar days after the “Notice to 
Proceed” is issued. The time of completion for the project is ninety (90) calendar days from the date 
of the “Notice to Proceed”. 
All bids shall be accompanied by a bid bond in favor of the City, in the amount of five percent (5%) 
of the total bid, (but not less than $5,000); such bid bond representing that the bidder, if awarded a 
contract, will promptly enter into a contract and furnish performance bond and payment bond as 
provided by law and approved by the attorney for the City. Failure to submit a bid bond with the 
proper rating will result in the bid being deemed non-responsive. 
Successful bidder will be required to meet insurance requirements. Performance and Payment bonds 
will be required upon acceptance of the proposal and contract submittal. 
 
The Performance Bond shall be equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the contract 
amount. The Payment Bond shall be equal to one hundred ten percent (110%) of the 
contract amount. 
 
 Insurance and Bonding Company must be licensed to do business by the Georgia Secretary of State, 
authorized to business in Georgia by the Georgia Insurance Department, listed in the Department of 
Treasury’s Publication of Companies holding Certificates of Authority as Acceptable Surety on Federal 
Bonds and as acceptable reinsuring companies. The bid bond, payment bond and performance 
bond must have an A.M. Best rating of A-5 or higher. 
 
Award will be made to the lowest responsible and responsive bidder. The City of Duluth reserves the 
right to reject any and all bids, to waive technicalities and to make an award as deemed in its best 
interest. 
 
Any change to the conditions and specifications must be in the form of a written addendum to be 
valid; therefore the City will issue a written addendum to document each approved change.

1. ORDINANCE TO APPOINT COURT SOLICITORS {A}
Chief Solicitor Richard Armond has requested a second Assistant Solicitor be
appointed to be assured of having a back-up solicitor for all court sessions.
2

Page 3 of 11
Approval of this item approves ordinance 02024-24 appointing the following
individuals as Municipal Court Solicitors of the Municipal Court of the City of
Duluth, who are authorized to serve in said positions unless a majority vote of
Council removes such member(s) or until successors are appointed: Mr. Richard
Armond-Chief Solicitor, Robert Giannini-Assistant Solicitor, Kelsey Wiley-Assistant
Solicitor, Maggie Benson-Assistant Solicitor(new).
2. INSOLVENT AD VALOREM TAXES . {B}
Per Chapter 2, Article 1, Sec 2- 4 of the Duluth Code, approval of this item grants
insolvency status to personal property tax accounts determined to be
uncollectible for years up through 2023 in the base amount of $22,449.12 plus
penalties and interest for a total of $28,353.48. Business personal property
accounts are considered insolvent only after every effort to collect them has been
exhausted, which includes processing late notices, returned mail investigation,
cross checks with the Gwinnett County's Tax Assessors' real and personal property
tax files, City and County Occupational Tax records, and onsite visits by the City's
Licensing Compliance inspector.
3. FINANCE/PURCHASING POLICY {C}
As reviewed at the April 22 work session, approval of this item approves the
updated purchasing policy, which outlines allowable methods for city purchases
and clarifies soending thresholds.
4. APPROVAL OF CONTRACT - ANNUAL LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE {D}
The annual landscape maintenance contract will expire on June 30, 2024. The City
advertised a Request for Proposal (RFP) for a new contract to provide citywide
landscape maintenance. The new contract will be for a term of one year,
beginning on July 1, 2024, and will be renewable annually for up to five total years.
As discussed at the March 25 work session, after reviewing all of the responses,
approval of this item accepts the staff's recommendation to award the annual
landscape maintenance contract to Yellowstone Landscape.
5. ORDINANCE TO AMEND DULUTH CODE - CHAPTER 10 {E}
The proposed ordinance will establish regulations on use of Unmanned Aircraft
Systems (UAS), commonly known as drones, on City-owned or City-operated
property. Approval of this item approves ordinance O2024-26 as presented.
6. LAP RECERTIFICATION —- ADOPTION OF GDOT PROCUREMENT POLICY
{F,G}
Georgia Dept. of Transportation (GDOT) requires that local governments adopt a
formal procurement policy that strictly follows Federal and State requirements
where federal funds are being used.
3

[page 4]
Minutes of M&C
May 13, 2024
Page 4 of 11
In the absence of a separate policy, GDOT allows for local governments to adopt
GDOT's policy by way of a letter of agreement. The council last adopted GDOT's
procurement policy in October of 2021. To maintain LAP Certification, the City
must adopt GDOT's procurement policy every three years and sign letters of
agreement. Local projects will continue using local procurement policies.
Approval of this item authorizes the Mayor and Council to sign the agreement
letters as presented.
A motion was made by Councilmember Holloway, seconded by Councilmember
Harkness, to approve the Consent Agenda as presented.
Voted For: Council members Harkness, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Holloway
Motion carried.
Vil. PUBLIC HEARINGS
]. FY25 BUDGET - FIRST PUBLIC HEARING {H}
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing and called Assistant City Manager/
Finance Director Ken Sakmar forward to present.
Per the State of Georgia code, the Mayor and Council are to hold a public hearing
to receive public comments on the proposed FY 2025 Annual Operating and
Capital Projects Budget. Prior to this public hearing, the council and staff
reviewed the proposed FY 2025 budget at a budget workshop on held April 15th.
Mr. Sakmar presented the strategic vision statements of the City and the
proposed balanced FY25 proposed budget, prior year audit results, and various
changes in the budget. He gave a budget comparison for the General Fund and
explained that the conservative approach used for projections means that
revenues are based on long term trends and expenditures are projected without
discounting. He summarized the revenues and expenditures, noting that the
highest expenditure items were staff salaries and the addition of the trash
collection service. He reviewed the expenditures by department and the stated
the intent to keep the tax millage rate the same for 2024.
Mr. Sakmar highlighted other funds such as the Public Art Fund, Stormwater
Utility, Rental Motor Vehicle, Tax Allocation District, and American Rescue Plan
(ARPA).
A second public hearing will be held on Monday, June 10, 2024, at the regularly
scheduled meeting of the Mayor and Council. Following the second public
hearing, an ordinance adopting the FY 2025 budget will be presented for
consideration.
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council.
4

[page 5]
Minutes of M&C

May 13, 2024

Page 5 of 11
Councilmember Thomas requested that the increase in the Mayor and Council
budget be communicated clearly. It was a result of moving the Gwinnett
Municipal Association annual dues to the Mayor and Council budget.
The Mayor called for questions/comments from the public. Being none, Mayor
Whitlock closed the public hearing and announced that the second public
hearing will be held on June 10, 2024. No motion was necessary at this time.

2. ORDINANCE OF SPECIAL USE — CASE SU2024-001- SMOKE FACTORY
{}}
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider the special use request.
Community Development/Engineering Director Margie Pozin came forward to
present. She explained that Property Owner Young Seo, and Applicant
Mohammed Alhadad have applied for special use permit for parcel R6322 151,
which is located at 3308 Peachtree Industrial Boulevard. The request is for
opening a vape shop, which requires a special use permit.
Ms. Pozin showed a map of the area and described the existing conditions on the
adjacent properties. She also discussed the Character Area in the Peachtree Retail
Corridor District and the recommended conditions that were placed on the
Planning Commission approval at their May 6, 2024 meeting. Staff also
recommended approval with conditions.
Mayor Whitlock called for discussion from Council.
Councilmember Harkness said he was morally against it and felt that the City has
enough smoke shops; therefore he would not support it.
Councilmember Holloway questioned the conditions regarding signage and
asked if vehicle signage was prohibited also. Ms. Pozin said the restriction only
applies to signage on the property.
Councilmember Graeder asked for clarification on the use. He asked if it was sale
of products only, as it appears to include hookah products and also consumption
of hookah on premise. Ms. Pozin confirmed that the applicant asked for sale of
tobacco products, but a secondary use could include hookah consumption on
premise.
Councilmember Doss noted that there is a Child Day Care next door and thus he
could not support.
Mayor Whitlock felt that onsite smoking invokes different requirements and
wanted to ensure other tenants would not be disturbed.
Councilmember Thomas asked what the main points are to review from staff
perspective since the Planning Commission and staff both recommended
approval with conditions.
5

[page 6]
Minutes of M&C

May 13, 2024

Page 6 of 11
Ms. Pozin responded that Staff reviewed the primary purpose to determine land
use conformity and compliance with the Comprehensive Plan. Any additional
permits governing the onsite activity would be under the authority of Gwinnett
County.
City Attorney Stephen Pereira clarified that the City has no specific regulations
regarding hookah bars, but the applicant has not asked for that at this point.
Mayor Whitlock called the applicant forward for a response. The applicant was not
present.
The Mayor called for questions/comments from the public. There being none,
Mayor Whitlock closed the public hearing and called for a motion.
A motion was made by Councilmember Holloway, seconded by Councilmember
Thomas to approve ordinance 02024-28 with conditions as presented.
Voted For: Council members Thomas and Holloway
Voted Against: Council members Harkness, Doss and Graeder
Motion denied.

3. ORDINANCE OF REZONING - CASE Z2024-001- FUTURES CHURCH
Mayor Whitlock opened the public hearing to consider a rezoning request.
Property Owner Paradise Evangelistic Association, Inc. and Applicant, The
Providence Group, LLC, are requesting a rezoning of parcel R7199 224, which is
located at the east corner of Old Peachtree Road and Sugarloaf Parkway. The
property is currently zoned Office-Institutional (O-l). The request is to rezone the
property to a Planned Unit Development (PUD) to allow for the development of
the Church as well as townhomes on the same property.
Planning Commission recommended approval with revised conditions on May 6,
2024. Staff recommends approval with original conditions.
As of May 8, 2024, the applicant has requested a continuation of this case until
June 10, 2024.
The Mayor called for a motion.
A motion was made by Councilmember Harkness, seconded by Councilmember
Graeder, to continue the public hearing for case Z2024-001 until June 10, 2024.
Voted For: Council members Harkness, Thomas, Doss, Graeder, and Holloway
Motion carried.

1. ORDINANCE OF REZONING — CASE Z2024-002 - ANNEXED PARCELS {J}
City Attorney Stephen Pereira presented the request. He explained that, on April
8, 2024, in accordance with the requirements of O.C.G.A. 36-66-4(d) (1), the Mayor
and Council held a public hearing to consider the appropriate zoning of 110

1. SERVER REPLACEMENT/EXTENDED WARRANTIES 
 
SUMMARY: 
The question was raised about replacing servers instead of extending the warranties 
through a third party (Service Express, Inc. (SEI)). We are currently using SEI for 2 
servers and 14 network switches. The hardware is still in good shape and the operating 
systems on the servers (Server 2019 Datacenter) will be supported until January 2029. It 
is IT's recommendation that we keep this equipment in service for 2 or 3 more years. 
 
2. RESIDENTIAL OFF-STREET PARKING 
 
SUMMARY: 
Staff is currently reviewing our ordinances and regulations pertaining to residential off-
street parking restrictions for certain vehicles. Staff will give a presentation of some 
current conflicts and disparities within our regulatory framework. Following the

of the review. Staff will walk through each and answer questions so that there is a

SUMMARY:

request input during portions of the presentation, and will explain the public 
involvement process that will follow this summer.

Purpose 
The purpose of this policy is to provide guidance to City of Duluth elected officials and employees 
regarding procurement, in turn maximizing the value for each dollar of expenditure on the goods and 
services necessary to provide governmental services for our citizens. It is the intent of the City to foster 
financial transparency while acting in the best interests of the City and maintaining fair, open, and 
transparent relationships with active and prospective vendors. 
Objectives 
▪ to assure taxpayers that dollars provided to the City and appropriated by the City Council are 
spent wisely and effectively 
▪ to provide guidance and procedures to all City personnel engaged in the purchasing / accounts 
payable process 
▪ to maintain reliable, competitive sources of supply based on fair and open vendor relations 
▪ to establish ethical standards for procurement 
▪ to remit payments to vendors in a timely manner without error, consistent with vendor terms 
and taking advantage of any discounts 
▪ to establish and maintain internal controls over purchasing and vendor payments that deter 
misappropriation of City resources 
Purchasing Guidelines 
General Rules & Principles 
• 
All City financial activity is subject to audit and open records. The City is committed to expending 
tax dollars in appropriate and necessary manners. 
• 
It is the responsibility of the Finance Department to assure sound procedures are established, to 
educate and assist City departments in understanding the procedures, and to assure the 
purchasing and accounts payable processes run efficiently. 
• 
Because purchasing activity is decentralized, individual departments hold primary responsibility 
for their own purchasing. This places accountability and responsibility in the hands of 
Department Directors, who must ensure that all policies and procedures are followed. It is the 
Department Directors’ responsibility, with assistance from the Finance Department, to make 
certain that staff involved in procurement are aware of, understand, and adhere to purchasing 
policies and procedures. Any delegation of authority by Department Directors shall be exercised 
with prudence and care. 
• 
When practical, employees making a purchase on a vendor account must provide their name at 
checkout so that when the statement arrives, the Finance Department can identify the origin of 
each charge. 
• 
All purchasing activity is expected to comply with departmental budget availability and 
established budget procedures. 
 

 
5 
 
• 
All departments are expected to seek the most cost-effective goods and services that meet 
departmental needs, taking into account the quality of the service or products provided. 
Departments should anticipate needs so as to purchase sufficient quantities in order to lower 
unit costs while avoiding waste due to over-stocking or pilferage. 
• 
Competition for City business is vital to cost-effective purchasing. However, the amount of staff 
time and effort required to complete a purchase should be based on the total cost of the 
purchase. In other words, a smaller amount of time and effort should be expended for low 
dollar purchases and considerable time and effort is normal for larger purchases. 
• 
The City of Duluth is exempt from State of Georgia sales and hotel tax. Departments are 
expected to take active measures to avoid payment of sales tax; therefore, sales taxes will not 
be reimbursed. Sales taxes may be avoided by providing a Sales Tax Certificate of Exemption 
(Exhibit A) to vendors. Lodging within the state of Georgia is also tax exempt. A Hotel Tax 
Exemption Certificate (Exhibit B) shall be provided in order to comply with this rule. 
• 
Purchases on the City credit card or with City vendor accounts are sales tax exempt. Therefore, 
elected officials and employees are prohibited from making personal purchases on any City 
account, as abuse could lead to the City’s loss of tax-exempt status. 
• 
Under no circumstances shall a City issued credit card, fuel charge card, or vendor account be 
used to put gas in a personal vehicle, to wash a personal vehicle, or otherwise purchase any 
types of maintenance services or goods for a personal vehicle. 
• 
Alcohol, tobacco, vaping, lottery, and other related purchases are strictly prohibited 
• 
City employees must refrain from all indications or appearance of impropriety with regard to 
vendors, as these may be construed as evidence of favoritism or providing unfair advantage. 
Specifically, employees are not to accept gifts, gratuities, or offers from any individual, 
company, firm, or business establishment that is a current or prospective vendor. Offers may 
include, but are not limited to money, entertainment, gifts, favors, loans, or promises of 
employment. Any such offers shall be politely declined, and any offers of significant value that 
could be construed as an attempted bribe are to be reported immediately to your Department 
Director. These limitations may not be interpreted so as to prohibit acceptance of social 
courtesies that contribute to good public relations, such as a token gift of edibles to a 
department so long as the value is minimal. 
• 
Ethical standards of conduct of city officials including the mayor, members of the city council, 
municipal judges (including substitute judges), city manager, city clerk, city attorney and all 
other persons holding positions designated by the city charter are governed by the Chapter 2, 
Article X – Code of Ethics, sections 2-224 & 2-225. 
• 
City employees must refrain from all indications or appearances of conflict of interest. A conflict 
of interest arises when the purchase of goods or services would result in the employee, or any 
immediate family member, realizing a financial gain. All potential or actual conflicts of interest 
shall be reported to the Department Director and the City employee must remove themselves 
from the decision-making process. 
 
 
 

 
6 
 
State Contracts 
The State of Georgia Department of Administrative Services maintains statewide contracts on many 
commodities and services. Many of these contracts are available for use by local governments. Using 
this source for purchases does NOT require any additional bidding procedures, therefore saving time 
and money. Nevertheless, departments are encouraged to spot-check State contract prices with prices 
available for the same item from another source in an effort to obtain the most favorable price. 
When utilizing this method of purchasing, it should be noted on the purchase order/invoice – “Purchase 
Made Under State Contract”. 
State contract information can be found on the Department of Administrative Services website: 
http://doas.ga.gov/state-purchasing/statewide-contracts 
 
Purchase Orders 
Purchase orders should be utilized when possible so that budgeted funds are held until the associated 
invoice is paid. Each department is responsible for completing their own purchase orders. Once goods 
are received, they must be inspected and compared with the packing slip and the purchase order. The 
receiving verification also includes assurance that the goods arrived in good condition. Any discrepancies 
in quantity or condition must be satisfactorily resolved prior to payment. 
Lodging, Travel, Per Diem & Overnight Expenses 
Lodging, travel, per diem, and overnight expenses are reimbursed by the City while an elected official or 
employee is performing their official duties or while attending training approved by the supervisor or 
Department Director. An Expense Report Form (Exhibit D) must be completed, approved by the 
Department Director, and submitted to the Finance Department. This form must be accompanied by 
supporting documentation to show the reason for travel, registration confirmation, conference 
itineraries showing any meals provided, mileage based on an internet driving map site, and any 
accompanying receipts, etc. All receipts must include a detail of the items purchased and not just the 
total charges. 
See the Duluth Code of Ordinances for a detailed explanation of the City of Duluth’s travel regulations. 
(Duluth Code § 2-47 & 2-48) 
Methods of Procurement 
Petty Cash 
The intent of petty cash is to provide a payment option for cash only purchases and small dollar 
purchases (generally under $50.00) resulting in greater productivity and less transaction cost. 
Each department with petty cash funds shall designate an employee to be in charge of petty cash. A 
Petty Cash Reimbursement Form (Exhibit D) must be approved and submitted before petty cash is 
dispensed. Any change and receipts must be returned to the designee within 24 hours or the next 
business day. 
 
 

 
7 
 
When a petty cash fund needs to be reimbursed, the designee should complete a Petty Cash 
Reconciliation form (Exhibit E). The form is then approved by the Department Director, and sent to the 
Finance Department along with all receipts and related documentation. The Finance Department shall 
review the form and supporting documents. Once approved, the Finance Department will process a 
reimbursement check and have it cashed at the bank. The Finance Department will then notify the 
designee that the cash to replenish the petty cash fund is ready to be picked up. 
In order to record all year end expenditures, the above reconciliation and reimbursement of petty cash 
must also be done shortly after the close of each fiscal year (June 30th). Petty cash is subject to audit by 
the Finance Department at any time. 
Credit Cards 
The intent of credit cards is to provide a quick, efficient, flexible manner to procure small to moderate 
dollar goods at less transaction cost resulting in greater productivity. City personnel are issued individual 
credit cards upon approval of the Department Director. Department Directors must exercise extreme 
care in determining who is to be assigned a credit card. Individual credit cards may be suspended or 
cancelled at the discretion of the Finance Director. Intentional inappropriate use or illegal use of credit 
cards could result in severe discipline and/or criminal prosecution. 
Use of credit cards is absolutely prohibited in the following situations: 
• 
Any purchase that is not budgeted or exceeds the department’s approved budget amount 
• 
Any purchase that is not work-related 
• 
Cash advances through ATMs or bank tellers 
• 
Annual contracts, maintenance, or other service agreements 
• 
Purchase of personal items of any nature 
• 
Purchase of alcohol, tobacco, vaping, lottery, or other related items 
In addition, the use of credit cards should be avoided for those merchants with whom the City has an 
established billing relationship or credit/store account (for example, Home Depot). If it is unclear from 
which vendor purchases should be made, the purchaser should refer to the Active Vendor List found 
here W:\Forms\Purchasing & Finance Forms. The Finance Department can also provide assistance and 
information on these vendors. 
Each department shall have an employee designated to maintain an employee credit card sign in/out 
log. A Credit Card Sign Out Authorization Form (Exhibit C) must be approved and submitted prior to 
anyone checking out a credit card. Credit cards should not be signed out for more than 24 hours unless 
the card is checked out for overnight travel. Once an employee returns from travel, the credit card and 
all receipts must be submitted to the Finance Department within 24 hours or the next business day. The 
person who signs out a credit card is held personally responsible for the safekeeping of the card until it 
is signed back in. City personnel are encouraged to write “See ID” on the signature space on the back of 
the credit card. Credit card information should not be written down or saved on computers or merchant 
websites; the credit card should be checked out for each use. 
 
 

 
8 
 
Receipts for any credit card purchases are mandatory and are the responsibility of the card user. This 
responsibility also entails knowledge of the card’s locations at all times and the immediate reporting of 
any misuse or loss. Each receipt must detail the items purchased and must be submitted to the 
department’s designee within 24 hours or the next business day. Any undocumented credit card 
purchases will be the responsibility of the card user. 
The Senior Accounting Technician (or Police Department Purchasing Technician) is responsible for 
reconciling the credit card statement and contacting the employee or department to resolve any 
discrepancies. The credit card statement shall be paid in full prior to the due date to avoid any late fees 
or finance charges. 
Purchases Less Than $25,000 
A Department Director has the responsibility and authority to control the funds budgeted for the 
operation of their department. The department director is expected to control expenditures, to meet 
budgeted amounts and effect savings where possible. Reasonable effort should be made to obtain the 
most favorable price for these purchases, but no formal or informal competitive pricing is required. 
It is often advantageous to procure service contracts/agreements on an annual basis to ensure effective 
and efficient operations. Service or maintenance contracts are to be in writing and once approved by 
Council as part of the budget process, authorize the department director to execute the necessary 
agreement without further Council action. Contracts not approved as part of the budget process, in 
excess of $25,000, or for multiple years will require Council approval. 
Purchases made in this category are generally made using one of the following four methods: 
1. Petty Cash 
2. Credit Card 
3. Vendor Invoice/Accounts Payable 
4. Purchase Order 
Petty cash and credit card purchases are to be made based on the guideline in the above sections. These 
purchasing methods are generally used for small purchases because they may be expedited more 
efficiently for these types of purchases. However, due to the limited funds available under these 
methods, great care should be taken to limit the use of these methods of purchasing. 
Vendor Invoice/Accounts Payable 
Operational Procedures 
1. When a department receives an invoice, whether it arrives through mail, email, or other means 
of delivery, it should be stamped for approval, and coded by an employee familiar with the 
department’s account codes. Invoice approval should be done by an employee(s) who can 
verify receipt of the goods or services. Once approved, the invoice should be forwarded to the 
Accounts Payable Department for processing and payment. 
2. Approval of invoices is part of each department’s fiscal accountability. This step ensures that 
payments are not issued merely because an invoice has been received or prior to verification 
that the goods and services have been provided. Invoices should be carefully reviewed, 
approved by authorized personnel, and returned to the Finance Department in a timely manner. 

 
9 
 
3. Checks and ACH Transmittal Reports are matched with the associated invoice and supporting 
documentation and then signed by either the City Clerk, City Manager, or designated Authority 
or Agency Member, as appropriate. 
4. Checks to City employees are delivered via inter-office mail. Checks to other payees are 
normally mailed. Alternatively, payees may pick up checks from the Business Office with proper 
identification. 
Other Accounts Payable Guidelines 
• 
A “Payment Request” form (Exhibit F) may be used for payees who do not generate invoices. For 
example, payments to class instructors, event entertainers, and occasional recipients of refunds 
may be initiated with a Payment Request form. This form is to be completed, approved by the 
Department Director, and sent to the Finance Department with appropriate supporting 
documentation. 
• 
Late fees due to failure to process invoices promptly are to be avoided at all times. The 
procedures outlined in this document are designed so that all departments working together 
cooperatively will be able to process payments in a timely manner to avoid past due notices. 
Investigating and resolving past due notices is time consuming and costly. Should a problem 
occur meeting a payment deadline, the Finance Department must be promptly notified. The 
Finance Department will assess the situation and determine any required corrective action. 
Purchase Orders 
A purchase order is a legal document used to create a written obligation between the City of Duluth and 
a vendor. Purchase orders can be used for any purchase less than $25,000. 
Each department, except for Community Development and Engineering, is responsible for completing 
their own purchase orders. The Finance Department shall be responsible for Planning and Development 
purchase orders. 
A department initiates a purchase order by preparing a Purchase Requisition form (Exhibit G). The 
purchase order should include the vendor’s name, item description (written description and stock #, if 
applicable), quantity, cost, delivery requirements, and the appropriate budget account code. All 
purchase requisitions shall be approved by the Department Director responsible for the purchase. 
The department must then enter the information from the purchase requisition form into the City’s 
accounting system and generate the purchase order. After the information is entered into the 
accounting system, the purchase information is sent via accounting system to the department director 
responsible for the purchase order approval. 
If necessary, after the Department Director approves the purchase order in the system, the 
department’s purchasing agent may print a copy and send it to the vendor. It is not necessary to keep a 
hard copy of the purchase order as all the purchase orders are stored in the accounting system. 
 
 

 
10 
 
Purchases Over $25,000 But Less Than $99,999 
Obtaining competitive prices is a requirement for purchases of this dollar amount. However, the 
competitive requirements are much less than the formal competitive procedures for purchases greater 
than $99,999. 
Departments are required to obtain a minimum of 3 price quotations or proposals prior to issuing a 
requisition for purchase of this dollar amount. The quotations should all meet the requirements, 
standards, or specifications of the goods or services to be purchased so that the purchasing decision will 
be based on comparable competition. 
Quotations may be obtained by fax, e-mail, sealed quotation, printed catalogs, on-line catalogs, or other 
third-party external documentation. All comprehensive information documenting the quotations shall 
be compiled on a City of Duluth Purchasing Quotation Form (Exhibit H). A copy of the Quotation Form 
shall be attached to the purchase requisition. If 3 price quotations or proposals are not obtained, the 
Quotation Form should include an explanation as to the reason. 
For budgeting purposes, purchase of this dollar amount should be made using purchase orders. In 
addition, the purchase may not be divided into two or more small purchases to circumvent these 
requirements. 
Purchases Over $99,999 
Public Works Construction 
Construction contracts costing less than $100,000 are not subject to the requirements of the Local 
Government Public Works Construction Law. Local governments are specifically prohibited from 
intentionally subdividing a contract over $100,000 in order to avoid the requirements of the Local 
Government Public Works Construction Law. 
If a department does not competitively bid a contract/item because the total expenditures are below 
the $100,000 threshold and it is likely subsequent services or purchase will take the expenditures over 
the threshold, the competitive bidding process should be used. 
In awarding Local Government Public Works Construction contracts, the City uses both the Invitation to 
Bid process (aka Competitive Sealed Bid) and Request for Proposals process (aka Competitive Sealed 
Proposal) The selection is based on the individual project, designed to ensure the best possible value is 
received by the City and to give those qualified and responsible bidders a fair and equitable opportunity 
to do business with the City. 
Procedure Requirements for Invitation to Bid (ITB)/Request for Proposals (RFP) 
When using local funds, the Department may choose the Invitation to Bid or the Request for Proposal 
option. Both options require City Council approval and award. 
 
 

 
11 
 
Prior to entering into a public works construction contract other than those exempted by OCGA Code 
Section 36-91-22, a governmental entity shall publicly advertise the contract opportunity. Such notice 
shall be posted conspicuously in the governing authority’s office and shall be advertised on the Georgia 
Procurement Registry as provided for in OCGA Code Section 50-5-69 at no cost to the governmental 
entity. Such notice may be advertised in the legal organ of the city or by electronic means on the 
website of the city or any other appropriate websites. 
Contract opportunities that are advertised in the legal organ shall be advertised a minimum of two 
times, with the first advertisement occurring at least four weeks prior to the opening of the sealed bids 
or proposals. The second advertisement shall follow no earlier than two weeks from the first 
advertisement. 
Contract opportunities that are advertised solely on the Internet shall be posted continuously for at 
least four weeks prior to the opening of sealed bids or proposals. 
Invitation to Bid (ITB) 
Contract opportunities that will be awarded by Invitation to Bid shall have plans and specifications 
available on the first day of the advertisement and shall be open to inspection by the public. The plans 
and specifications shall indicate if the project will be awarded by base bid or base bid plus selected 
alternates and: 
A. A statement listing whether all anticipated federal, state, or local permits required for the 
project have been obtained or an indication of the status of the application for each such 
permit including when it is expected to be obtained; and 
B. A statement listing whether all anticipated rights of way and easements required for the 
project have been obtained or an indication of the status as to when each such rights of way 
or easements are expected to be obtained. 
 
Bidders shall submit sealed bids based on the criteria set forth in the invitation. 
 
The City shall open the bids publicly and evaluate such bids without discussions with the bidders. 
 
The contract shall be awarded to the lowest responsible and responsive bidder whose bid meets the 
requirements and criteria set forth in the Invitation to Bid; provided, however, if the bid from the lowest 
responsible and responsive bidder exceeds the funds budgeted for the public work construction project, 
the City may negotiate with such lower bidder to obtain a contract price within the budget amount. 
Such negotiations may include changes in the scope of work and other bid requirements. 
 
Should the lowest responsible and responsive bidder be disqualified for any reason, the City would 
select the next lowest responsible and responsive bidder. 
 
Request for Proposal (RFP) 
The Request for Proposal (RFP) bidding format may be used when the goods and services do not lend 
themselves to a clear accurate statement of work, and/or the objective of solicitation is to identify the 
bidder who can offer the best possible solution at the most reasonable cost. The RFP seeks to identify 
the “best value” for the City by using a combination of technical and commercial factors to evaluate 
bidders’ proposals. All eligible proposals will be subject to confidential evaluations prior to award. 
 

 
12 
 
Contract opportunities that will be awarded by Request for Proposal shall be publicly advertised, and 
shall include conceptual program information in the request for proposals describing the requested 
services in a level of detail appropriate to the project delivery method selected for the project. The 
advertisement shall include such details and specifications as will enable the public to know the extent 
and character of the work to be done. 
 
Request for Proposal must include language describing how each proposal will be evaluated, and 
whether cost is evaluated, and if so, to what degree. Only those items listed for evaluation in the 
proposal will be evaluated. 
 
All required notices of advertisement shall also advise of any mandatory prequalification requirements 
or pre-proposal conferences as well as any federal requirements pursuant to subsection (d) of OCGA 
Code Section 36-91-22. Notice of mandatory pre-proposal conference or prequalification shall provide 
reasonable advance notice of said conference. 
 
In making any Request for Proposal, the City shall: 
A. Publicly advertise the Request for Proposal, which shall include conceptual program 
information describing the requested service in a level of detail appropriate to the project 
delivery method selected for the project, as well as the relative importance of the evaluation 
factors. 
B. Open all proposals received at the time and place designated in the request for proposal so as 
avoid disclosure of contents to competing offerors during the process of negotiations. 
C. Make an award to the responsible and responsive offeror whose proposal is determined in 
writing to be the most advantageous to the City, taking into consideration the evaluation 
factors set forth in the request for proposal. The evaluation factors shall be the basis on 
which the award is made. 
 
As set forth in the request for proposal, offerors submitting proposals may be afforded an opportunity 
for discussion, negotiation, and revision of proposals. Discussions, negotiations, and revisions may be 
permitted after submission of proposals and prior to award for the purpose of obtaining best and final 
offers. In accordance with the request for proposal, all responsible offerors found by the City to have 
submitted proposals reasonably susceptible of being selected for award shall be given an opportunity to 
participate in such discussions, negotiations, or revisions. During the process, the City shall not disclose 
the contents of proposals to competing offerors. 
 
Other Factors 
Where a public works construction contract involves the expenditure of federal assistance or funds, the 
receipt of which is conditioned upon compliance with federal laws or regulations regarding the 
procedures for awarding public works construction contracts, the City shall comply with such federal 
requirements and shall not be required to comply with the provisions of (OCGA 36-91-22 d) Chapter 91 
of Title 36 that differ from the federal requirements. The City shall provide notice that federal 
procedures exist for the award of such contracts in the advertisement required by subsection (b) of 
OCGA Code Section 36-91-20. 
 
The above contracting and bidding requirements shall not apply to public works construction projects 
necessitated by an emergency, provided the contract is ratified as soon as practicable and the nature of 
the emergency is described in the minutes of the City Council. 

 
13 
 
Submittal of Bids/Proposals 
The Invitation to Bid/Request for Proposal shall specify that vendors submit bids/proposals in a sealed 
package that clearly indicates that the package is a response to the Invitation to Bid or Request for 
Proposal. The receiving department shall date, and time stamp the package immediately upon receipt. 
The bids/proposals shall remain sealed and secured until the time for the opening. Bids/proposals may 
be withdrawn only by written request of the submitting party, at any time prior to the opening. 
Mistakes discovered before bid/proposal opening may be modified by written request of the submitting 
party. Bids/Proposals received after the designated date and time of opening shall not be opened or 
considered. An Invitation for Bid/Request for Proposal may be cancelled prior to the opening date at the 
sole discretion of the City. 
 
Bid/Proposal Opening 
The City Clerk or his/her designee, in the presence of one or more witnesses, shall open bids publicly on 
the date and at the time and place designated in the Invitation for Bid without discussion with the 
bidders. The name of each bidder, the purchase price contained in each bid and/or such other 
information as deemed appropriate shall be announced as the bids are opened. A record of bid 
information and bid tabulation shall be recorded and maintained as a public record. If stated in the 
Request for Proposal a formal opening will take place, said opening shall take place according to the 
Request for Proposal at the date, time and location listed. 
 
After bid opening, no changes in bid prices or other provisions of bids prejudicial to the interest of the 
City or fair competition shall be permitted. However, corrections in bids shall be permitted only to the 
extent that the bidder can show by clear and convincing evidence that a mistake of a nonjudgmental 
character was made, note the nature of the mistake, and the bid price actually intended. 
 
Invitation to Bid/Request for Proposal Evaluation 
Bids shall be evaluated based on the requirements set forth in the Invitation to Bid, which may include 
criteria to determine acceptability such as inspection, testing, quality, workmanship, delivery, and 
experience/suitability for a particular purpose. No criteria may be used in bid evaluation that is not 
specifically set forth in the invitation. Proposals shall be evaluated based on the requirements set forth 
in the Request for Proposal, including the process for scoring each proposal. 
 
Rejection/Disqualification of Bid/Proposal 
The City reserves the right to reject any or all bids/proposals if it determines such a rejection to be in the 
best interest of the City. The following types of bids/proposals shall be subject to disqualification for 
cause: 
 
a. A bid/proposal which is incomplete in any material aspect. 
b. A bid/proposal submitted without required bonds. 
c. A bid/proposal received after the deadline for submitting proposals. 
 
 
 

 
14 
 
Bid Award 
Subject to approval by the City Council, bids shall be awarded to the lowest responsible bidder whose 
bid, conforming to the Invitation for Bid, will be most advantageous to the City of Duluth, with price and 
other factors considered. However, if the bid from the lowest responsible and responsive bidder 
exceeds the funds budgeted for the public works construction contract, the City may negotiate with 
such an apparent low bidder to obtain a contract price within the budgeted amount. Such negotiations 
may include changes in the scope of work and other bid requirements. Any rejections of low bids shall 
be explained and documented in writing. A written award mailed (or otherwise furnished) to the 
successful bidder within the time for acceptance specified in the bid shall be deemed to result in a 
binding contract without further action by either party. 
 
Proposal Award 
Subject to approval by the City Council, projects shall be awarded to the offeror whose proposal 
received the highest score based on the published evaluation criteria provided the proposal included the 
required administrative paperwork formally requested in the Request for Proposal. 
Receipt of One Sealed Bid 
In the event only one sealed bid is received, the City has the option to open said bid or suspend said bid 
opportunity while investigating the reason for receipt of only one bid. In the event a sole bid is opened; 
City has the right to reject sole bid if it exceeds the budget for said project. In this event, City may 
choose to readvertise bid opportunity with same, similar, or altered scope. The city also has the right to 
negotiate with said bidder for the best and final offer taking scope and other project requirements into 
consideration. 
 
Emergency Purchases 
Normal competitive purchasing procedures may be temporarily waived during bona fide emergencies. 
An emergency is hereby defined as any situation or circumstance that is determined to constitute a 
threat to public health, safety, or welfare or to the soundness and integrity of public property, or to the 
delivery of essential services, and where the adverse effects of such emergency may worsen materially 
in the short term with the passage of time. 
 
The Mayor or City Manager must declare a “state of emergency” that would permit a waiver of normal 
purchasing procedures. Departments shall still use such competitive procedures as circumstances 
reasonably permit. Emergency purchasing provisions must not be used to compensate for poor 
planning. 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
15 
 
Bonding 
Bonds provide a form of financial protection against damage. A bond is a binding agreement executed 
by a bidder or vendor and another party to guarantee the performance of certain obligations or duties 
to the purchaser. There are three types of bonds that may be appropriate for inclusion in procurement 
for costly items or construction projects: Bid Bond, Performance Bond, Payment Bond. 
 
Bid Bond 
Bid bonds provide surety that the firm awarded a bid shall not withdraw the bid, shall insure the 
execution of the contract document, and shall furnish any required Payment and Performance 
Bonds. The City of Duluth requires a bid bond if the estimated bids or proposals are for construction 
projects of $100,000 or more. The bid bond shall be in the amount of not less than five (5) percent 
of the total amount payable by the terms of the contract. The guarantee may be in the form of a 
cashier’s check or certified check made payable to the City of Duluth, or a Bid Bond issued by a 
surety company. Bid Bonds will be returned upon award of the contract (O.C.G.A. § 36-91-50). 
 
Performance Bond 
A performance bond is executed subsequent to award by a successful bidder to protect the City of 
Duluth from loss due to the bidder’s inability to complete the contract as agreed, and to secure the 
fulfillment of all contract requirements. Performance bonds shall be required for all public works 
construction contracts with an estimated contract amount greater than $100,000. Prior to 
commencing work, the successful bidder will be required to furnish a performance bond in the 
amount of at least the total amount payable by the terms of the contract and shall be increased as 
the contract amount is increased. The guarantee of performance may be in the form of a cashier’s 
check, certified check made payable to the City of Duluth, or performance bond. When the amount 
of the performance bond required does not exceed $750,000, the City may, in its sole discretion, 
accept an irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association as defined in 
O.C.G.A. §7-1-4 in the amount of and in lieu of the bond otherwise required. 
 
Payment Bond 
The successful bidder will be required to furnish a guarantee of payment for the protection of all 
subcontractors, individuals, or businesses participating in the project or contract. Payment bonds 
shall be required for all public works construction contracts with an estimated contract amount 
greater than $100,000 and must be provided prior to commencing work. In lieu of such payment 
bond, the City, in its discretion, may accept a cashier’s check, certified check made payable to the 
City of Duluth, or an irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association as 
defined in O.C.G.A., §7-1-4. The payment bond or other security accepted in lieu of a payment bond 
shall be in the amount of at least the total amount payable by the terms of the initial contract and 
shall be increased if requested by the City as the contract amount is increased.
