Chair Williams opened the public hearing.
Deputy Director Aron Hall came forward and presented rezoning request Z2023- 003 to
rezone the parcel from C- 2 (General Business District) to HC-A (Highway Commercial -
Auto District). The subject
property totals +/- 2.9 acres. The property is the last southern
property inside the City of Duluth before entering unincorporated Gwinnett County. The
property to the south is Rick Hendrick Chrysler Dodge, which is zoned C- 3. The property
to the east is also zoned
C-#, is in unincorporated Gwinnett County and is currently a car
dealership
called Atlanta Luxury Motors. The property to the west is also in
unincorporated Gwinnett County. It is a residential subdivision zoned R75. The property to
the North is the only adjacent property in the City of Duluth. The property is zoned PUD
Planned Unit Development) and is currently Gwinnett Place Nissan. The subject parcel
has been used as a car dealership for over 20 years.
Chair Williams called for the applicant to come forward.
Tyler Lasser of 299 South Main Street Alpharetta, GA 30009 explained the purpose of the
request to rezone the parcel from C- 2 to HC- A.
Commissioner
Gajjar had questions about parking, drive lanes and the square footage of
additions. Commissioner Williams asked about the southern property line in regards to
the use of the pipeline easement. The applicant stated there will be no changes to that
area. Commissioner
Gajjar asked to see the site plan that is currently being reviewed
by

Moss asked about
conditions related to noise. There was general discussion around the conditions.
Commissioners agreed that the conditions being stated as they are in the staff report will
prevent
noise.

from Rick Case Mazda driving through her yard. She also stated that Rick Case Mazda has
paved nearly up to their property line to the south. She would like a natural buffer to be
maintained. She also spoke of the noise that comes from the dealership. She runs an at-
home daycare and can hear the car alarms when employees are attempting to find cars

development, but wanted to raise those concerns to commission.

Request: Approval of Text Amendments to section 1103, 1104, 1206, 1207, and 1208 of the
City of Duluth Unified Development Code to ensure local zoning procedures are
following state statute.
Chair Williams opened the public hearing.
Planning Director Forrest Huffman came forward and presented that the purpose of this Text
Amendment (TA2023-002) to sections 1103, 1104, 1206, 1207, and 1208 of the City of Duluth Unified
Development Code is to ensure local zoning procedures are following state statute. In 2022 the
Georgia State Legislature passed a statute (O.C.G.A. 36-66-5.1) modifying the posting and hearing
requirements for certain land use hearings and quasi-judicial decisions. These modifications can
be summarized into two broad categories.
1. If the City is to initiate the rezoning of a single-family property to a multi-family classification, or
if the City is to initiate the modification of a single-family zoning district to allow for uses non
typical of a single-family zoning district, the City is obligated to additional posting and hearing
requirements.
2. Hearings on quasi-judicial decisions, those being hearings deciding appeals of administrative
decisions, hearings and decisions on variances, special administrative permits, special
exceptions, conditional use permits, and other similar permits shall be subject to additional
posting and hearing requirements.
These amendments became effective July 1, 2022. However, no zoning or quasi-judicial decisions
prior to July 1, 2023 are to be rendered invalid or void because of a local government's failure to
implement language in their ordinances accomplishing the provisions of Code Section 36-66-5.1.
Chair Williams called for questions/comments from the public.
Being none, Chair Williams called for a general discussion.

Applicant: Matthew Garber

[page 2]
ZBA Minutes
December 20, 2023
Page 2 of 3
Chair Wilson opened the public hearing.
Deputy Director Aron Hall came forward and variance request V2023-020 for a reduction
in distance requirements between a residentially zoned property and a massage business
at the proposed location, 2456 Main Street NW, currently zoned C-2 (General Business
District). To the west of the property is zoned C-2 (General Business District); east is zoned
M-1 (Light Industrial District); south has the railroad and its 200’ right-of-way and beyond
that is Buford Hwy NE in Unincorporated Gwinnett County; to the north is the south end
of Riverbrooke subdivision zoned PUD (Planned Unit Development).
Per the UDC Section 332, massage therapy establishments must meet the following
criteria:

a) A150-foot buffer shall be required between any massage therapy business to
any residentially zoned property from the front door of the structure where
the massage business occurs to the nearest parcel boundary line of any
residentially zoned property as measured by a straight line on the ground.
Should this buffer requirement differ from what is contained in the City of
Duluth Massage Therapy Ordinance in the City of Duluth Code of Ordinances,
the requirement in the Massage Therapy Ordinance shall apply.

b) A message therapy business shall be subject to all other rules and
requirements of the City of Duluth Massage Therapy Ordinance in the City of
Duluth Code of Ordinances and all current and future pertinent local, state,
and federal ordinances.

The request comes before the Zoning Board of Appeals due to three citations received by
a massage and nutrition specialist operating out of Stage 3 Fitness. Stage 3 Fitness, as per
the letter of intent, is focused on a holistic health and well-being approach to fitness
through typical fitness classes, nutrition, and recovery through massage. However,
businesses offering massage services have zoning requirements that need to be met
prior to massage services being conducted at their business regardless of whether that
business is independent or housed within a fitness center.
On September 7, 2023 a code enforcement officer visited Stage 3 Fitness after a
conversation with the City of Duluth Licensing Department suspecting illegal massage
may be occurring. Upon visiting Stage 3 Fitness, the code enforcement officer discovered
evidence confirming this. Massage services had been taking place within Stage 3 since at
least March 2023 when a zoning application was denied due to the distance requirement
from residential to a massage business. The Massage Therapist operating out of Stage 3
Fitness was cited for three separate violations of the code of ordinance: sec. UDC 207.06
prohibited uses; sec. 7-248(a)(1) operating a massage therapy business without a valid city
license; and, sec. 7-4 occupational tax certificate required.
During the month of September, staff had several conversations with the
applicant/owner Matt Garber about the distance requirements for massage businesses.
On October Sth staff met with Mr. Garber to discuss the variance process. Mr. Garber
submitted a Variance Application a week later on October 12th.

2

[page 3]
, ZBA Minutes
December 20, 2023
Page 3 of 3
This application was submitted for the hearing on December 20th, 2023. Ms. Marcos, the
Massage Therapist working out of Stage 3 Fitness, appeared in court on November 15,
2023. She pled guilty to all three citations and was fined $1,000 on sec. 7-248(a)(1); $1,000
on sec. 7-4 OTC, and a reduced fine of $250 for sec. 207.06.
Chair Wilson called for a discussion from the board.
Board members discussed details of the second condition.
Chair Wilson called for the applicant to come forward.
Matthew Garber of 4130 Gold Hill Lane Cumming, Ga. 30040 came forward and stated
that the business will operate by appointment only, there will only be one licensed
massage therapist at a time. Appointments are available for the public not just gym
members.
Denisse Garber of 4130 Gold Hill Lane Cumming, Ga. 30040 came forward and stated that
appointments will be required to alleviate traffic within the parcel.
Chair Wilson called for questions/comments from the public.
Being none, Chair Wilson called for a discussion from the board members.
Board members discussed procedures for massage licensing within the City of Duluth.
Discussed the conditions and how they apply to new employees or if Ms. Marcos decides
to move her business outside the city limits.
Being no further discussion, Chair Wilson called for a motion.
A motion was made by member Pennington, seconded by member Niti to approve
Case V2023-020, with conditions. motion passed 3-0.

3. Matters from the Public - None

A motion was made by member Gajjar, seconded by member Pennington to adjourn
at 6:29pm. All for, motion passed 3-0.

Chair Wilson opened the public hearing.
Planner Kelly Nguyen came forward and presented the purpose of the variance request
(V2023-019) is for a reduction in distance requirements from a residential portion of any
tract of land zoned PUD and any tract or parcel of land upon which is located an
establishment which is licensed and authorized to sell alcoholic beverages, to operate a
by-appointment-only tattoo studio. The site is located within North River Professional
Park at 4181 Pleasant Hill Road and is zoned C-2. This property is located off Pleasant Hill
Road and Peachtree Industrial Boulevard tucked within a professional park behind street
fronting businesses. It is surrounded by parcels zoned C-2 on all four sides.
Per the UDC Section 339, tattoo and body piercing establishments must meet the
following criteria:
a) A tattoo and body piercing establishment shall be located no closer than 600 feet
from any tract or parcel of land which is zoned RA-200, R-100, or located within 600 feet
of any residential portion of any tract of land which is zoned PUD. In addition, no tattoo
and body piercing establishment shall be located within 600 feet of any property located
within the Historic Residential District or the Central Business District.
b) A tattoo and body piercing establishment shall be located no closer than 100 feet
from any tract or parcel of land upon which is located an establishment which is licensed
and authorized to sell alcoholic beverages within the City of Duluth.
Cc) A tattoo and body piercing establishment shall be subject to the rules and
requirements of the City of Duluth Tattoo and Body Piercing Establishment Ordinance in
the City of Duluth Code of Ordinances and all other current and future pertinent local,
state, and federal ordinances.
d) Where the setback requirements of this Section and the Tattoo and Body Piercing
Establishment Ordinance conflict, the setback requirements of the Tattoo and Body
Piercing Establishment Ordinance shall apply.

Board members discussed details of the conditions that include access to the building,
hours of operation, maintenance, and loitering.

1. Case: V2023-018 
 Applicant: TPG Homes 
 Location: 2953 Evanshire Avenue Duluth, GA. 
 Request: Variance from UDC Article 8 to encroach within the impervious buffer. 
 
 

ZBA Minutes 
August 23, 2023 
Page 2 of 3 
 
 
 
2
Chair Wilson opened the public hearing 
 
Director of Community Development & Engineering Margie Pozin came forward and 
presented the purpose of the variance request(V2023-018) is to allow for the 
encroachment of a Gabion Wall and wooden guard rail into the impervious buffer within 
the Evanshire residential development. The request detail a 15-feet encroachment into 
the 75-foot impervious setback along lot #6. The sites are located within the Evanshire 
residential development that was permitted via Z2020-003 to rezone +/- 25.24 acres to 
PUD for the construction of up to 140 residential units. Evanshire is bound to the east by 
Woodbridge subdivision, south by the First Baptist Church of Duluth, and west by Duluth 
Highway 120. The intent of Evanshire is to construct a residential subdivision consisting of 
74 single-family attached dwelling sand 66 single-family detached dwellings. Since 
zoning approval in 2021, construction efforts are well underway with building permit 
approvals. 
 
Chair Wilson called for a discussion from the Board. Being none, Chair Wilson called for 
the applicant to come forward. 
 
Michael Smith representing The Providence Group of Georgia, 11340 Lakefield Drive Johns 
Creek, GA. 30097. Mr. Smith stated that the request of the variance is for safety 
precautions for the future homeowners, the wall will have a structural engineer for 
permitting process. The wall will also help with erosion control. 
 
Chair Wilson called for questions/comments from the public. 
 
L. Penny Poole of 3375 Church Lane Duluth, GA. 30096. Mrs. Poole came forward in 
opposition of the variance request. Ms. Poole expressed her concern with the quality of 
life for the citizens in the area regarding infrastructures and sewage in proximity to the 
west of highway 120 near the historic African American community. 
 
Chair Wilson called for a discussion from the Board. 
 
Board members discuss the voting options which are approve/deny/tabled. The number 
of votes needed to pass the case and what the guidelines are to present the case again if 
it were to get denied. 
 
Being no further discussion, Chair Wilson called for a motion. 
 
 
A motion was made by member Gajjar, seconded by member Pennington to approve 
Case V2023-018, with conditions. motion passed 3-1. 
 
VI. 
OTHER BUISNESS 
 
1. Matters from Staff - None 
2. Matters from Board - None

CITY OF DULUTH

BOARD MEMBERS: 
Ken Wilson, Chair 
 
 
Niti Gajjar 
K.C. Callaway, Vice Chair 
 
Robert Pennington 
Verdi Avila, Secretary 
 
William Latta 
 
MEMBERS PRESENT: Chair Wilson, Vice Chair K.C. Callaway, Secretary Avila, Member Gajjar, Member 
Pennington, Member Latta 
 
MEMBERS ABSENT: None 
 
STAFF PRESENT: Planning Manager Amy Bingham and Planning Technician Wendy Bethancourt 
 
I. 
CALL TO ORDER 
 
Meeting called to order at 6:00pm. 
 
II. 
GENERAL BUSINESS 
 
None 
 
III. 
APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
 
Approval of the September 28, 2022 Minutes. 
 
A motion was made by Secretary Avila, seconded by member Latta to approve the September 28, 2022 
minutes as presented. All for, motion passes 6-0. 
 
IV. 
OLD BUSINESS 
None 

 
 
 
V. 
NEW BUSINESS 
 
A. Public Hearing 
Case: V2022-005 
Applicant: Mishmel Properties 
Location: 3190 Peachtree Industrial Blvd 
Request: Variance to reduce landscape strip 
 
 
Chair Wilson opened the public hearing. 
 
Ms. Bingham presented the purpose of this variance request (V2022-005) which is to allow for the 
redevelopment of the existing gas station located at 3190 Peachtree Industrial Blvd. Two variances are 
requested. The first variance will reduce the number of required off-street parking spaces from 19 to 17. Table 
4-B of the UDC requires 5 parking spaces for every 1,000 square feet of Gross Floor Area (GFA) for the 
proposed retail use. The second variance seeks to eliminate the landscape screening requirements along both 
Abbotts Bridge Rd and Peachtree Industrial Blvd rights-of-way. Section 403.08(a) states that parking located 
between the right-of-way and the building requires a 10-ft landscape strip. The subject property was 
developed in 1987 as a gas station. The approved plan for the site contains 8 fuel stations, 949-sf convenient 
store, and carwash. The property has one ADA parking space. The proposed site plan details a remodel of the 
convenience store and retail space with an increase of the square-footage. 
 
Staff recommends approval with conditions for the landscape strip and denial for the reduced parking spaces. 
 
Chair Wilson called the applicant to come forward. 
 
Naureen Lalani of 1850 Duluth Highway came forward representing the developers. Member Latta asked why 
they were not able to find additional parking space. Ms. Lalani stated that the engineer could not find space 
for those parking spaces, but they are willing to work with staff to two parking spaces. Member Latta asked if 
the remodel would utilize the existing asphalt. Ms. Lalani stated that yes, the existing asphalt would be reused. 
Secretary Avila asked for more information regarding the addition of the space. Ms. Lalani stated that they 
were not increasing the square footage of the space, they only remodeling and converting the convenience 
store and carwash into one building. What used to be a car wash will not be space for retail. Member Latta 
asked if they had a tenant for the retail space. Ms. Lalani stated that she would have to ask the owner. 
Secretary Avila asked what type of business they were developing the site for. Ms. Lalani stated that she 
would have to ask the owner, but it could possibly be a fast-food restaurant. Member Latta asked what the 
proposed hours of operation were. Ms. Lalani stated the owner could answer that question. 
 
Marcell Rebello of 3190 Peachtree Industrial Blvd, the owner of the property came forward. Mr. Rebello 
stated that he intends to open a healthy fast-food alternative in the retail space. Secretary Avila asked if the 
restaurant would be intended for take-out only. Mr. Rebello stated that the space is small and just a few 
tables for dining would not work. Take-out would be the best option. Member Latta asked staff if there was a 
difference between dine-in and a take-out restaurant and if it would be allowed in the intended space. Ms. 
Bingham stated that parking regulations differs for each use. A fast-food restaurant required 15 parking 
spaces per 1000sqft. The applicant would have to meet the additional 15 parking spaces per each 1000sqft. 
Member Latta stated to the applicant that if the intent of the space is for a restaurant and not retail as 

 
 
depicted on the proposed site plan, the variance request would not be adequate. Mr. Rebello stated that the 
use could be reconsidered into a use that meets the code. Member Latta asked for the hours of operation to 
the gas station. Mr. Rebello stated that currently they are open 7 days a week from the hours of 6am to 11pm. 
The intention is to be open 24hrs depending on if there is high demand at night. Member Latta asked when 
the fuel is delivered. Mr. Rebello stated that it varies but typically deliveries arrived twice a day. 
 
Chair Wilson opened the floor to those in favor. Being none, those opposing. Being none. 
 
Chair Wilson closed the public hearing. 
 
A motion was made by Secretary Avila, seconded by member Gajjar to approve the V2022-005 landscape 
variance with conditions. All for, motion passes 6-0. 
 
A motion was made by member Gajjar, seconded by Vice Chair Callaway to deny the V2022-005 parking 
variance. All for, motion passes 6-0. 
 
 
VI. OTHER BUSINESS 
A. Matters from Staff 
 
Ms. Bingham stated that in the upcoming February 2023 meeting, 17 variances will be presented. All are from 
the same development. 
 
B. Matters from Commission 
C. Matters from Public

ADJOURNMENT 
A motion was made by Secretary Avila, seconded by Vice Chair Callaway to adjourn. 
All for, motion passes 6-0.
